# At 1f38013 the money code refuses to spend, but four withdrawn promises still render on public pages and three tests hold one of them in place.

**Codebase evaluation** · 27 August 2026 · `AltivumInc-Admin/quantum-computing` at commit `1f38013` · public repository

This pass read the tree at 1f38013 end to end — the 45-notebook curriculum and its solution files, the Next.js portal and its guard suites, all six Lambdas with their CloudFormation and offline tests, the Stripe and QPU scripts, and both locale dictionaries — and checked each claim against the source, against the production account read-only, and against the test suites where they exist. 109 findings were raised: 60 confirmed outright, 49 partly true, none refuted; 3 high, 33 medium, 73 low, and 10 direct violations of the project's own written rules. All three high-severity findings are one defect in five places — the sponsored-QPU promise withdrawn on 2026-07-28, still shipping on the landing page, the README tagline, and the 02-hardware lesson in both locales, because the August copy sweep was scoped to the pricing family and no guard reaches past it. Since the 2026-08-18 audit, 6 findings were resolved, 53 were re-raised unchanged, 19 were lowered on new evidence and 1 was raised; the deliberate switches are all still off, and the new analytics stack arrived with its four alarms wired to an SNS topic that has no subscribers. The pattern that moved least is the one the project cares most about: nearly every guard written to catch dishonest copy still cannot see the surface where that copy actually lives.

> The rendered version of this document is published as an Artifact. This file is the source of truth and what gets reviewed in a diff. Both are generated from `docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-27.json` and pass through the same redaction gate; identifiers such as `$PROD_ACCOUNT` are substituted deliberately.

## The money path

Surviving: 0 high, 7 medium, 7 low.

### How it actually works

The money path is one Lambda (`lambda/stripe/index.mjs`, 1072 lines) behind an HTTP API v2 with four routes: `POST /checkout`, `POST /portal`, `GET /wallet` (all Cognito-JWT) and `POST /webhook` (public, authenticated by Stripe HMAC — the only route with `Auth: Authorizer: NONE`, template.yaml:186-190). It is DI-core shaped: `createHandlerCore({stripe, ddb, tableName, webhookSecret, siteOrigin})` is pure enough to unit-test, and `lazyCore` (index.mjs:1042) builds the real deps on first invocation, reading `{secretKey, webhookSecret}` from Secrets Manager by `SECRET_ID` so the plaintext never appears in `GetFunctionConfiguration`. `lazyCore` deliberately clears the memo on a failed build, which is what makes a mid-rotation container recover.

One DynamoDB table, `quantum-stripe-wallet`, holds three pk-prefixed row families: `WALLET#<sub>` (credits, tier, subscriptionStatus, clawbackOwedCredits), `EVENT#<id>` (idempotency, TTL'd at 30 days), and `RECEIPT#<paymentIntentId>` (purchasedCredits / refundedCredits / disputedCredits / amountPaidCents, never expiring). TTL is enabled table-wide on `expiresAt`, so `web/__tests__/infra/wallet-ttl.test.ts` pins every occurrence by file, count, and — walking backwards to the nearest row key and `TableName` — by the row it targets.

Exactly-once is `applyOnce` (index.mjs:200): one `TransactWriteItems` of an `attribute_not_exists(pk)` Put on `EVENT#`, the wallet Update, and an optional receipt leg at fixed indexes `EVENT_LEG/WALLET_LEG/RECEIPT_LEG`. The catch branches per leg by name so a replay (EVENT leg) is distinguishable from an OCC loss (`CLAWBACK_RETRY`). `splitAgainstDebt` + `grantThroughDebt` garnish every money-in event against `clawbackOwedCredits`, retrying four times on a lost paydown race.

Grants: `checkout.session.completed`/`async_payment_succeeded` fulfil top-ups from server-stamped `metadata.credits`; subscriptions light up the tier only, and credits arrive on `invoice.paid`, which reads `parent.subscription_details.subscription` (the Basil relocation) and re-retrieves the invoice with `expand:["payments"]` to resolve the PaymentIntent. Clawbacks (`reclaim`, index.mjs:526) compute an ABSOLUTE target from Stripe's cumulative `amount_refunded` (or a dispute pro-rated against `amountPaidCents`), track refunds and disputes on separate counters, floor the balance at zero and book the shortfall as debt, and use the receipt's `${field} = :seen` as an OCC token.

`CATALOG` (index.mjs:137) is the server-side mirror of `TIERS` in `web/src/lib/pricing.ts`. Nothing offline compares them; only `scripts/stripe/check-catalog-parity.mjs` does, and it needs a live key. Its sibling `check-webhook-parity.mjs` checks the nine `REQUIRED_WEBHOOK_EVENTS` and a pinned `api_version`; both refuse an account that does not match `--expect-account`. `provision-sandbox.mjs` builds the sandbox from `CATALOG`, `e2e-sandbox.mjs` drives real Stripe objects against a deployed sandbox stack, and the untracked `rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs` recreates an endpoint, stores the new signing secret, recycles the function, and probes it. `scripts/founding-credit/` is the one credit writer with no payment behind it; its ceiling is a DynamoDB `ConditionExpression`, not arithmetic. Metering is off everywhere and `NEXT_PUBLIC_BILLING_URL` is absent, so no money has moved.

### What is genuinely good here

- `lambda/stripe/index.mjs:281-293` — `applyOnce` branches on the transaction's cancellation reasons PER LEG by index (`EVENT_LEG`/`WALLET_LEG`/`RECEIPT_LEG`), never on "the first reason", so a duplicate delivery, a lost debt-paydown race and a lost receipt update are three distinct outcomes instead of one ambiguous one.
- `lambda/stripe/index.mjs:589` — clawback arithmetic is absolute, not incremental: `target = min(purchased, floor(purchased * fraction))` computed from Stripe's cumulative `amount_refunded`, so a replayed or out-of-order delivery is a no-op and correctness survives the 30-day `EVENT#` TTL expiring inside Stripe's longer dispute window.
- `web/__tests__/infra/wallet-ttl.test.ts:143-166` — the `expiresAt` guard does not merely count occurrences; for each one it walks backwards to the nearest row-key marker and the nearest `TableName` and refuses anything that is not provably the `EVENT#` marker or the `DAY#` row on `ledgerTable`. This is the strongest guard in the repo against the documented wallet-vaporizing hazard.
- `web/__tests__/infra/credit-writers.test.ts:106-108` — the `CREDIT_WRITE` regex matches three spellings of a balance move (`ADD credits`, the dynamically-pushed `adds.push("credits `, and "builds a `WALLET#` key AND issues an update") after a real hole let `e2e-sandbox.mjs`'s absolute `SET` through undetected.
- `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:99` and `lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs:289` — both metering kernels convert micro-dollars to credits with `Math.ceil`, so rule 4's round-up is implemented identically on both surfaces rather than asserted in prose.
- `scripts/founding-credit/issue.mjs:126-137` — the $200 cohort ceiling is enforced by DynamoDB on the write (`issued <= :maxIssued AND creditsIssued <= :maxCredits`, both precomputed constants), not by the runner's arithmetic, so the 21st issuance is refused even if the script is wrong.
- `lambda/stripe/template.yaml:284-321` — the `SignatureRejected` metric filter and alarm close a gap that was invisible to both existing alarms (the invocation succeeds, so `AWS/Lambda Errors` is blind; the response is 4xx, so the 5xx alarm is blind); `template.test.mjs` pins the filter pattern to a literal exported from `index.mjs`.
- `scripts/stripe/check-webhook-parity.mjs:70-77` and `check-catalog-parity.mjs:88-95` — both verify `GET /v1/account` against `--expect-account` before reading anything else and exit non-zero on a mismatch, which is the right answer to "every `stripe` CLI profile on this machine points at the wrong account".

### The webhook-rotation script writes a 1Password-sourced API key into Secrets Manager without verifying which Stripe account that key belongs to, and it is still untracked in git

`scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs:115-117` — `fe5efb27d` · medium · confirmed · correctness · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `fe7c51b2f` · fix plan 08

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD, and still untracked (`git status --porcelain scripts/stripe/` reports `?? scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs`; `git ls-files scripts/stripe/` lists only the other four). The script verifies `process.env.STRIPE_API_KEY` against `--expect-account` (:83-86) and creates the webhook endpoint with THAT key. But the key it writes into Secrets Manager comes from a completely different source — `spawnSync("op", ["read", secretKeyRef])` at :115, defaulting to `op://Quantum Learner/Stripe/add more/Secret Key` (:54) — and is never checked against the account at all. The two halves of `{secretKey, webhookSecret}` are therefore proved to come from the same account by nothing.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. (1) THE MISMATCH SCENARIO. The finder invokes the Altivum Logic / Tj-Scents hazard, but that CLAUDE.md warning is about `stripe` CLI *profiles*, and this script never reads a CLI profile — it reads a fixed `op://` item in the Quantum Learner vault. The script's own documented invocation (:29-35) sources `STRIPE_API_KEY` from that *exact same* reference, so under documented usage the two halves are byte-identical and `--expect-account` transitively covers both. The finder missed the mismatch path that actually exists: the `--secret-key-ref` default (:54) is the LIVE item (Makefile:42 `KEYREF ?= op://Quantum Learner/Stripe/add more/Secret Key`; Makefile:48 shows sandbox is a *different* item, `op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key`), and the flag appears nowhere in the usage header — `grep -rn "secret-key-ref"` returns exactly one hit in the tree, its own definition. So a SANDBOX rotation that swaps `--expect-account/--url/--secret-id/--function` but forgets the undocumented flag silently writes the LIVE secret key beside a sandbox webhook secret. There is also no `sk_live_` guard on the op-read half, only on `STRIPE_API_KEY` (:65-66). (2) THE GUARD IMPACT IS INVERTED. "Invisible to `git ls-files`-based guards" is not a defect: that guard exists to stop commercial terms being *published* in a public repo, and its own comment at web/__tests__/infra/no-commercial-terms.test.ts:181-188 documents ls-files as deliberate ("The disclosure surface is exactly what git publishes… a walker would make the guard pass in CI while failing on a contributor's machine"). An untracked file publishes nothing; it becomes scannable the moment it is committed, which is the only moment it matters. And `grep -nEi "$COMMERCIAL_TERMS_PATTERN"` over the script returns NO MATCHES, so the guard would find nothing in it even once tracked. Severity medium -> low: the documented path is safe by construction, the damaging path needs a specific undocumented mis-invocation, and the harm only lands if someone then drives the sandbox function's checkout/subscription routes — a path that is dormant anyway (storefront closed, rule 15; wallet metering off).

**Impact.** If the 1Password item resolves to a different account (the owner's login also controls Altivum Logic `$STRIPE_OTHER_ACCOUNT` and Tj-Scents, and CLAUDE.md records that every `stripe` CLI profile on this machine already points at the wrong one), the deployed Lambda ends up verifying webhooks signed by account A while creating Checkout Sessions and retrieving subscriptions on account B. The rotation probe cannot catch it: it only exercises the signature half. Being untracked also means the script is invisible to `git ls-files`-based guards — `web/__tests__/infra/no-commercial-terms.test.ts:181-189` enumerates via `git ls-files -z`, so this file is never scanned — and it can be lost with the working tree.

**Evidence.** scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs:83-86 (identity check on `key`, i.e. STRIPE_API_KEY only); :115-117 `const opRead = spawnSync("op", ["read", secretKeyRef], ...); const payload = JSON.stringify({ secretKey: opRead.stdout.trim(), webhookSecret: created.secret });`; `git status --porcelain scripts/stripe/` → `?? scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs`.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: confirmed · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, medium, ran locally). Every element of the claim holds, and I reproduced the defect end to end in a fully stubbed harness (no Stripe, AWS, or 1Password call was made).

FACTS VERIFIED (read):
- `git status --porcelain scripts/stripe/` → `?? scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs`; `git ls-files scripts/stripe/` lists only the other four; `git log --oneline --all -- scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs` is EMPTY — never committed on any branch.
- `grep -n "opRead|process.env.STRIPE_API_KEY|=== key|secretKeyRef" scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs` returns exactly 5 lines (48, 54, 115, 116, 117). The env key and the op-read key are never compared, and the op-read key is never sent to `GET /v1/account`. The only identity check is :84-86, on `key` alone.
- `grep -n "secretKey" lambda/stripe/index.mjs` → :1064 `const { secretKey, webhookSecret } = await loadSecret(...)`, :1066 `new Stripe(secretKey, ...)`. So the unverified half is exactly what creates Checkout Sessions and retrieves subscriptions. Impact chain is real.
- `sed -n '181,189p' web/__tests__/infra/no-commercial-terms.test.ts` → `execSync("git ls-files -z", ...)`. Untracked file is genuinely never scanned.

REPRODUCTION (executed): `cd <scratchpad> && node harness.mjs` — a copy of the script with `child_process` and `fetch` replaced by stubs. Driving it as a SANDBOX rotation (`--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD`, `STRIPE_API_KEY=$STRIPE_TEST_KEY...`) with the default `--secret-key-ref`, the script printed `Rotating $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD (Quantum Learner Sandbox)`, then `probe HTTP 200 — the deployed function verifies the new secret`, then `Rotation complete.` — while the payload piped to `put-secret-value` was:
  `{"secretKey":"$STRIPE_LIVE_KEY_LIVE_ACCOUNT_KEY","webhookSecret":"$WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENDPOINT_SECRET"}`
Two halves, two accounts, zero warnings. The finder's point that the probe cannot catch it is confirmed: it returned 200 because it only exercises the webhook-secret half.

WHAT MAKES THIS SHARPER THAN THE FINDING STATES (strengthening, not a correction): the concrete trigger is not a hypothetical 1Password mix-up. `Makefile:48` records this repo's own sandbox convention — `make stripe-parity ACCOUNT=$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD KEYREF="op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key"` — i.e. sandbox work uses a DIFFERENT 1Password item, while `rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs:54` hardcodes the LIVE item as its default. Any sandbox rotation that forgets `--secret-key-ref` writes a `sk_live_` key into a sandbox-scoped secret. That is the reproduction above.

NOTHING DOWNSTREAM CATCHES IT: `grep -n "secretsmanager|SECRET_ID" scripts/stripe/check-*-parity.mjs` returns no Secrets Manager reads — the `make stripe-parity` the script recommends on its own last line only talks to Stripe and never inspects the deployed secret. And `grep -n "spawnSync|STRIPE_API_KEY" scripts/stripe/*.mjs` shows this is the ONLY script in the directory that sources a key from anywhere but `process.env.STRIPE_API_KEY`; every sibling is single-source and structurally immune.

SEVERITY: medium, not higher. It needs operator error to fire, on a hand-run tool, and the storefront is closed (rule 15) so no learner checkout is currently exposed. But the tool exists specifically to be run against live `quantum-stripe`, the failure is silent and self-congratulatory, and one direction of it deposits a live secret key into a sandbox-scoped secret. The fix is three lines: re-call `GET /v1/account` with the op-read key and `die()` unless it also equals `--expect-account`.

### Nothing prevents a second concurrent subscription, and cancelling either one resets the still-paying subscriber to the free tier

`lambda/stripe/index.mjs:968` — `fa67d24a6` · medium · confirmed · correctness · ran locally · re-raised from `f552e4181` · fix plan 07

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD. `POST /checkout` gates only the top-up path on tier — `if (spec.mode === "payment" && !(await hasPaidTier(sub)))` (index.mjs:968) — so a `plus` subscriber can check out `ql_pro_monthly`, or the same tier twice, with no existing-subscription check anywhere. Stripe will happily bill both. `customer.subscription.deleted` then does `applyOnce({ eventId, sub, setTier: "free", setSubStatus: "canceled" })` unconditionally (index.mjs:794) with no check of whether another active subscription exists for that customer.

**Impact.** A learner who resubscribes at a different tier without cancelling first pays twice and, per finding above, receives whichever grant each subscription's frozen metadata carries. When they cancel the redundant one, the webhook writes `tier: "free"` over a customer who is still paying — losing their top-up entitlement (`hasPaidTier` gates `/checkout` for credit packs) and their tier gate — with nothing to restore it until the next `invoice.paid` at the period boundary. Dormant while the storefront is closed.

**Evidence.** lambda/stripe/index.mjs:966-970 (`spec.mode === "payment"` is the only tier guard on checkout); :791-796 `case "customer.subscription.deleted": ... setTier: "free", setSubStatus: "canceled"`.

Low today; a legitimate medium the day the storefront opens, and it belongs in the same "decide the upgrade path" work item the audit already opened.

### Refund and dispute clawbacks are capped separately against the same purchase, so a refunded-then-disputed charge reclaims up to twice what was bought

`lambda/stripe/index.mjs:589` — `f7be45dd5` · medium · confirmed · correctness · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `f0187a23b` · fix plan 07

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD; no commit has touched `lambda/stripe/` since the prior audit (`git log -- lambda/stripe/` tops out at dd7abb7, before 4aec7f8). `reclaim` computes `target = restore ? 0 : Math.min(purchased, Math.floor(purchased * effectiveFraction))` and writes it to one counter chosen by `field` — `refundedCredits` for `charge.refunded` (index.mjs:816) and `disputedCredits` for `charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn` (index.mjs:831). Each is bounded by `purchased` alone; nothing sums them. The receipt carries both counters (index.mjs:399-400) but no code reads one while writing the other.

**Correction.** The mechanism and the diagnosis are right, but the Impact paragraph's headline scenario is the one variant Stripe blocks, and the case the finder demoted to a single sentence is the actually-reachable one.

1. WRONG — "a full refund ... a subsequent dispute of the same charge ... sets disputedCredits = 1900". Stripe's Dispute object documents `is_charge_refundable`: "If true, it's still possible to refund the disputed payment. **After the payment has been fully refunded, no further funds are withdrawn from your Stripe account as a result of this dispute.**" No funds withdrawal means no `charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn`, and the handler deliberately ignores `charge.dispute.created` (index.mjs:824-826). So the "0 credits AND 1,900 credits of debt" figure does not arise the way the finding describes it.

2. UNDERSTATED — "A partial refund followed by a dispute produces the same over-reclaim in smaller proportion." This is the real bug, and it is not a smaller-proportion version of the headline: it happens precisely because the dispute is NOT scaled down. Stripe documents it explicitly (docs.stripe.com/disputes/best-practices, "Disputes on partially refunded payments"): "While uncommon, a customer can dispute a payment for the full amount even if they've already received a partial refund ... it amounts to an over-refund of more than the original purchase." The dispute arrives at the full charge amount, so `effectiveFraction` = 1 and the dispute leg targets the WHOLE grant on top of whatever the refund leg already took.

3. MISSED — a second reachable ordering the finding does not mention: dispute-then-refund. `is_charge_refundable: true` means a disputed charge can still be refunded (refunds.md warns of `charge_for_pending_refund_disputed` and "duplicate reimbursements to the customer"). That ordering reproduces the full 2x over-reclaim the finding attributed to refund-then-dispute.

4. SCOPE — the exposure is partly self-healing. `restore` sets the dispute counter to 0 unconditionally regardless of how much was reinstated, so the documented resolution of the partial case (issuer rectifies; `charge.dispute.funds_reinstated`) clears the phantom debt and returns the credits. The debt only stands permanently if the dispute is lost with no reinstatement.

**Impact.** Purchase 1,900 credits for $19. A full refund sets `refundedCredits = 1900` and drains the balance. A subsequent dispute of the same charge — Stripe prices a dispute at the charge amount, not the net-of-refund amount — sets `disputedCredits = 1900`, finds a zero balance, and books the whole 1,900 as `clawbackOwedCredits`. The learner ends at 0 credits AND 1,900 credits of debt for a single purchase, and both spend gates refuse every request until they buy their way clear. A partial refund followed by a dispute produces the same over-reclaim in smaller proportion. Dormant: no live volume and the storefront is closed.

**Evidence.** lambda/stripe/index.mjs:589 `const target = restore ? 0 : Math.min(purchased, Math.floor(purchased * effectiveFraction));`; :816 `field: "refundedCredits"`; :831 `field: "disputedCredits"`; :636-639 books the uncovered remainder as `owedDelta`.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: partly true · correct as written: confirmed. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, medium, ran locally). Read lambda/stripe/index.mjs:523-690 (reclaim) and :805-850 (the two callers). The mechanism is exactly as claimed: `target = restore ? 0 : Math.min(purchased, Math.floor(purchased * effectiveFraction))` at :589 is bounded by `purchased` alone and written to one counter selected by `field`; nothing sums `refundedCredits` and `disputedCredits`.

Purchase 2000 credits for 2000 cents, then:

  B. refund 1000c, dispute 2000c   -> credits=0 owed=1000 counters sum 3000/2000  OVER +1000
  C. dispute 2000c, then refund 2000c -> credits=0 owed=2000 counters sum 4000/2000 OVER +2000

Any phantom debt locks the learner out of both metered surfaces until they buy their way clear, which inverts rule 7 (fail toward undercharging).

### The per-subscription credit grant is stamped once at signup and never re-derived, so repricing CATALOG in lockstep with TIERS leaves existing subscribers on the old grant forever, undetected

`lambda/stripe/index.mjs:752` — `f119ba729` · medium · confirmed · correctness · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 07

**Claim.** `POST /checkout` stamps `subscription_data.metadata.credits` from `CATALOG` at session creation (index.mjs:1046-1052 region), and `invoice.paid` reads `subscription.metadata.credits` off the retrieved Subscription on every renewal (index.mjs:752-757). Nothing ever rewrites that metadata: `customer.subscription.updated` (index.mjs:798-802) writes only `setSubStatus: obj.status` — never `tier`, never a re-derivation of credits from the subscription's current price. The handler's own test admits it at `lambda/stripe/index.test.mjs:208-212` ("repricing CATALOG changes NEW subscribers only. Existing subscribers keep the grant they signed up with until their subscription metadata is explicitly backfilled"). There is no backfill script anywhere in the repo, and `scripts/stripe/check-catalog-parity.mjs` compares TIERS↔CATALOG↔Stripe *prices* but never inspects live subscription metadata.

**Correction.** Three parts of the reasoning are wrong. (1) "Undetected / no test can see it" is false: repricing `CATALOG` credits is exactly what fails the tests, and the failing test IS the one carrying the NOTE. I copied lambda/stripe to scratchpad, changed `ql_plus_monthly.credits` 1900 -> 2400, and ran `node --test`: 74 pass unmodified, 2 fail after the change — "CATALOG credit counts mirror the published pricing" (index.test.mjs:123, hardcoded literal) and "POST /checkout creates a subscription session with server-set metadata" (index.test.mjs:213, `assert.equal(s.subscription_data.metadata.credits, "1900")`). The repricer cannot land the change without editing line 213, three lines below the comment that states the consequence and names the remedy. The tripwire is at the edit site, with the explanation attached. (2) "If a price is edited in the Dashboard" is not a real Stripe mechanic — a Price's `unit_amount` is immutable; repricing means creating a NEW price and moving the lookup key, and existing subscriptions stay on the OLD price until explicitly migrated. Under that mechanic the stamp is *correct* grandfathering, not staleness: the subscriber who pays the old $19 keeps the old 1900-credit grant. The alternative the finding implies — re-deriving credits from CATALOG at each `invoice.paid` — would grant an unmigrated legacy subscriber the NEW, larger allotment while they still pay the OLD, lower price. That is credit issued beyond what was paid for: a direct hit on rule 12's bound and rule 11's "every credit was paid for." The stamped metadata is the safe direction; re-derivation is the unsafe one. (3) The `tier`-staleness half is not shown to be reachable. A plan switch would need the Billing Portal's `subscription_update` feature, which is off in Stripe's default portal configuration and is configured nowhere in this repo (`stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create({ customer, return_url })` at index.mjs:1006 passes no configuration). Switching via `/checkout` instead creates a second subscription, each carrying its own correct metadata. Category is closer to ops-gap than correctness, and medium overstates it.

**Impact.** Rule 8's lockstep guarantee stops at the catalog. Raise Plus to a larger grant and `pricing.ts`, `CATALOG` and the Stripe price can all agree while every pre-existing Plus subscriber silently keeps receiving the smaller grant they signed up with — an under-delivery against advertised copy that no test, no parity script and no alarm can see. The same staleness applies to `tier`: if a plan is switched or a price is edited in the Dashboard, `customer.subscription.updated` records the status change and leaves `tier` and `credits` pointing at the old plan indefinitely. Dormant while the storefront is closed and no subscription exists.

### Rule 13 is violated literally: the monthly credit counts are hardcoded into i18n copy in both locales, duplicating the TIERS-derived line on the same card

`web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:893` — `f67e4ceaf` · medium · confirmed · rule-violation · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 02

**Claim.** CLAUDE.md rule 13 says "Credit counts and prices belong in `TIERS`, never hardcoded into i18n copy — that shipped once and rendered a new price beside a stale grant." `plusF1: "1,900 credits every month"` (en.ts:893, es.ts:821) and `proF1: "6,500 credits every month — a 10% bonus over pay-as-you-go"` (en.ts:898, es.ts:827) do exactly that. The tier card renders the SAME sentence twice: once derived, `t("pricingUi.creditsEveryMonth", { credits: formatCredits(tier.monthlyCredits) })` → "1,900 credits every month" (pricing-page-content.tsx:224-229), and once hardcoded via `copy.features` (pricing-page-content.tsx:234-236, from `tierCopy` at :50). No test ties the copy string to `TIERS.monthlyCredits`: grepping `1,900`/`6,500`/`1900`/`6500` across `web/__tests__/` and `web/src/components/pricing/` returns nothing.

**Correction.** Two things are wrong. (1) SCOPE, the main one: "The tier card renders the SAME sentence twice" and "duplicates a sentence verbatim on every paid card today" is overstated. Verbatim duplication occurs on exactly ONE card in ONE locale — Plus/English. Pro/EN differs (the bullet carries the "— a 10% bonus over pay-as-you-go" tail). BOTH Spanish cards differ, because `formatCredits` (pricing.ts:26-32) hardcodes the English word "credits" and the "en-US" locale, so the ES derived line renders "1,900 credits cada mes" beside the bullet "1,900 créditos cada mes". That English leak in the ES derived line is a separate `formatCredits` defect, not this finding — but it means the "verbatim on every paid card" impact claim does not hold as written. (2) CITATION: the finder cites web/src/lib/pricing.ts:246 for the Plus `featureKeys` array; it is at line 269 (246 is `monthlyCredits: 0` on the Free tier). Everything else in the claim stands.

**Impact.** Change `TIERS.plus.monthlyCredits` and the same card renders two different credit counts side by side — the derived line updates, the bullet does not — and the whole test suite stays green. That is precisely the failure rule 13 was written after. It also duplicates a sentence verbatim on every paid card today, which is a visible copy defect.

**Evidence.** web/src/lib/pricing.ts:246 `featureKeys: ["pricingUi.plusF0", "pricingUi.plusF1", "pricingUi.plusF2"]`; web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:893 `plusF1: "1,900 credits every month",`; web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:774 `creditsEveryMonth: "{{credits}} every month",`; web/src/components/pricing/pricing-page-content.tsx:225-228 renders `formatCredits(tier.monthlyCredits)` through that key.

### A free-tier top-up attempt is refused 403 by the server but rendered as a retryable English-only error, bypassing i18n

`web/src/components/pricing/top-up.tsx:48` — `fb90dc829` · low · confirmed · consistency · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 12

**Claim.** `<TopUp />` renders for every visitor whenever `billingLive` is true (`pricing-page-content.tsx:286-290`) — there is no tier gate. The server refuses a free-tier top-up with `403 {"error":"subscription required"}` (`lambda/stripe/index.mjs:968-970`, and the same guard for the custom path at :938). `startTopUp` surfaces that as a `BillingHttpError` with `status: 403` (`billing-client.ts:80`), but `top-up.tsx` catches only `BillingAuthError` and falls through to `setError("Could not start checkout. Please try again.")` (:44-49) — a hardcoded English string, even though `pricingUi.checkoutFailed` exists in both locales and `checkout-button.tsx:64` uses it correctly.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. (1) The "retryable error contradicts the disclosed policy" impact is not a defect and is not addressed by the proposed fix: pricingUi.checkoutFailed in en.ts:873 is VERBATIM the hardcoded string ("Could not start checkout. Please try again."), and the Spanish value (es.ts:810) carries the same retry advice ("Inténtalo de nuevo"). Switching to the key changes the language and nothing else. Only the locale-bypass half of the finding stands. (2) checkout-button.tsx is not a counterexample for this case: it is rendered only with tier.checkoutLookupKey (pricing-page-content.tsx:260-261, its sole usage) and both tier keys are mode:"subscription" in CATALOG (index.mjs:138-139), which the `spec.mode === "payment"` guard at :968 does not gate — so CheckoutButton can never receive a "subscription required" 403. No path in the app renders distinct copy for that condition; TopUp is the only UI that can produce it. (3) Minor: the custom-path guard is at index.mjs:932, not :938 (938 is the closing paren of the amount range check).

**Impact.** A free-account visitor with the storefront open is told to retry an action that can never succeed, and a Spanish-locale visitor is shown English on a payment surface where every other string is translated. The `topUpFootnote` copy does say "Top-ups require an active plan" in both locales, so the policy is disclosed — but the error path contradicts it with retry advice. Dormant: the storefront is closed, so `billingLive` is false and the panel does not render.

**Evidence.** web/src/components/pricing/top-up.tsx:43-49 (only `BillingAuthError` is special-cased; :48 is the hardcoded string); web/src/components/pricing/checkout-button.tsx:64 `{t("pricingUi.checkoutFailed")}`; lambda/stripe/index.mjs:968-970; web/src/components/pricing/pricing-page-content.tsx:286-290.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: confirmed · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). Every cited fact checks out, and I reproduced the render.

Source (all line numbers exact):
- /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/web/src/components/pricing/top-up.tsx:43-49 — `catch (e)` special-cases only `BillingAuthError`; line 48 is literally `setError("Could not start checkout. Please try again.");`, byte-identical to `en.ts:873 pricingUi.checkoutFailed`. It is the only occurrence of that literal outside `en.ts` (`grep -rn "Could not start checkout" web/src web/__tests__`).

### provision-sandbox.mjs and the Makefile document a stale sandbox account id that no longer matches the provisioned sandbox

`scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs:40` — `f5dfdb4d3` · low · partly true · docs-drift · observed live · fix plan 08

**Claim.** `provision-sandbox.mjs`'s usage block prescribes `--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD` (:40), and `Makefile:48` prescribes the same id for the sandbox parity run. But `scripts/stripe/e2e-sandbox.mjs:16` targets `$STRIPE_SANDBOX`, and CLAUDE.md:55-57 states plainly that `$STRIPE_SANDBOX` is "Quantum Learner Sandbox" while "an older `$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD` is recorded in some places and is NOT the one that is provisioned". CLAUDE.md itself carries the contradiction: :55 names the correct id and :82 names the stale one.

**Correction.** The impact sentence "the sandbox catalog and webhook endpoint were never provisioned by the documented invocation of the script that is supposed to build them, so what e2e-sandbox.mjs runs against was stood up some other way" is wrong. `--expect-account` is a required operator-typed argument with no default (provision-sandbox.mjs:65), so the stale string in the header comment never reaches the wire — the operator simply typed the correct id. A dry run against the real sandbox shows all three products and all six CATALOG prices already "ok" against what this exact script builds. It was stood up by this script, not some other way. Also wrong: "no in-repo tiebreaker" — CLAUDE.md:56-57 explicitly names $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD as "NOT the one that is provisioned", and the guard's own refusal message prints the real account id AND its dashboard display name, handing the operator the answer at the moment of failure.

**Correction.** Two of the three impact claims are wrong. (a) "leaves an operator holding two account ids with no in-repo tiebreaker" is false — CLAUDE.md:55-57 is precisely that tiebreaker ("Sandbox is $STRIPE_SANDBOX … An older $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD is recorded in some places and is NOT the one that is provisioned"), and the finder quotes it in its own evidence; a second tiebreaker is the guard's own error string, which names the authenticated account and display name. (b) "the sandbox catalog and webhook endpoint were never provisioned by the documented invocation … so what e2e-sandbox.mjs runs against was stood up some other way" is unsupported and contradicted by ac25c22's commit message, which describes the sandbox as carrying exactly what provision-sandbox.mjs creates (literal `ql_credits` product id, one price per CATALOG lookup key, an endpoint with all nine events pinned to the SDK apiVersion). The script was evidently run with the correct id passed on the command line; only the example value in its comment is stale. (c) "blocks the sandbox-first discipline" overstates it — the run aborts before any write with a message naming the correct account, one flag value from correct.

**Impact.** Copy-pasting either documented command with the sandbox key exits 1 with `WRONG ACCOUNT` — a safe failure, but it blocks the sandbox-first discipline CLAUDE.md makes mandatory for every Stripe change, and it leaves an operator holding two account ids with no in-repo tiebreaker. It also means the sandbox catalog and webhook endpoint were never provisioned by the documented invocation of the script that is supposed to build them, so what `e2e-sandbox.mjs` runs against was stood up some other way.

**Evidence.** scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs:40 `--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD`; Makefile:48 `make stripe-parity ACCOUNT=$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD KEYREF="op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key"`; scripts/stripe/e2e-sandbox.mjs:16 `--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX`; CLAUDE.md:55 vs CLAUDE.md:82.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, low, observed live). All textual claims verified at the cited lines (`awk 'NR==40' scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs`, `NR==48 Makefile`, `NR==16 scripts/stripe/e2e-sandbox.mjs`, CLAUDE.md 52-58 and 82): three in-repo sites carry the superseded id (provision-sandbox.mjs:40, Makefile:48, CLAUDE.md:82) against two carrying the real one (e2e-sandbox.mjs:16, CLAUDE.md:55).

Reproduced both documented commands live against Stripe, read-only:

1. `STRIPE_API_KEY="$(op read 'op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key')" node scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs --expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD --dry-run` → `WRONG ACCOUNT: key belongs to $STRIPE_SANDBOX (Quantum Learner Sandbox), expected $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD. Refusing to write.`, exit 1. (I confirmed `--dry-run` is genuinely write-free first: every POST/DELETE in the file sits in an `else` branch of an `if (dryRun)`, lines 141-233.)

2. `make stripe-parity ACCOUNT=$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD KEYREF="op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key"` → `WRONG ACCOUNT: key belongs to $STRIPE_SANDBOX ... Refusing to continue.`, make Error 1.

So the copy-paste failure is real and the live sandbox key does belong to $STRIPE_SANDBOX, confirming which id is stale.

What refutes the impact chain: `... provision-sandbox.mjs --expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX --dry-run` prints `ok` for `ql_credits`, `ql_plus`, `ql_pro` and for all six prices (ql_plus_monthly 1900c, ql_pro_monthly 5900c, ql_credits_500/2000/5000/10000), then "Catalog is provisioned." The sandbox already matches exactly what this script would build. `git log -1 --format=%B ac25c22` says "THE SANDBOX. $STRIPE_SANDBOX mirrors live's structure ... sandbox e2e 6/6" — the same commit that rewrote CLAUDE.md's sandbox line left three copies of the old id behind. Same-commit comment drift, not a disagreement about which account exists.

Severity low: nothing at runtime, in CI, or on any money path reads these strings — Makefile:48 is a `@#` shell comment inside the recipe and provision-sandbox.mjs:40 is a docstring. The blast radius is one operator paste that fails loudly, before any write, with the correct id printed. It blocks a re-run, not a first build. This is documentation drift caught by a working guard — the CLAUDE.md rule ("every script takes --expect-account and refuses a mismatch rather than trusting a written-down id") is satisfied, not violated; provision-sandbox.mjs:65 requires the flag and :101-106 refuses on exact inequality.

### The account-migration runbook still prescribes 4 of the 9 required webhook events and no pinned api_version — it reproduces the exact production gap found on 2026-08-17

`docs/account-migration-runbook.md:322` — `f9059a4d2` · low · confirmed · docs-drift · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `f9059a4d2` · fix plan 11

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD. Step 27 instructs: "Register a **NEW** Stripe webhook endpoint at `WebhookUrl` ... subscribe `checkout.session.completed`, `invoice.paid`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`". That is four of the nine in `REQUIRED_WEBHOOK_EVENTS` (index.mjs:118-128): `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, `checkout.session.async_payment_failed`, `charge.refunded`, `charge.dispute.funds_withdrawn` and `charge.dispute.funds_reinstated` are all absent. It also says nothing about pinning `api_version`, which is creation-only and cannot be set from the Dashboard.

**Correction.** The impact framing is wrong on two counts, and both are in the repo. (1) Step 27 explicitly scopes the endpoint to "**test mode** while monetization is draft," so following it cannot "rebuild, exactly, the live configuration" or leave "the clawback path dark in production" — a test-mode endpoint carries no live traffic. ### The cutover runbook's rate-verification step still asserts the retired at-cost framing and points at Bedrock pricing, in a public repo

`docs/billing-cutover-runbook.md:186-198` — `f31847a0b` · low · confirmed · docs-drift · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `f5029e6b8` · fix plan 11

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD; the file has not been touched since 95dc909, which predates the prior audit. §1.1d "Verify the tutor metering rate table" still says `RATES` holds "Anthropic first-party list prices as a documented placeholder", still says "Bedrock is partner-priced and the AWS Price List API returns no entries", still instructs the operator to "Confirm each against <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/>" (:194), and still states "Charging at cost is deliberate (margin is the subscription, not a markup on inference), which is exactly what makes the basis load-bearing" (:195-198). All four claims were superseded on 2026-08-17: the tutor moved to Anthropic's first-party API, CLAUDE.md records `RATES` as "a verified cost basis rather than a placeholder", and rules 5/9 replaced at-cost with a single shared markup.

**Correction.** Two sub-claims in the Impact paragraph are wrong, and the scope is understated.

(1) WRONG MECHANISM. The finder says `no-commercial-terms.test.ts` misses the sentence "because every BANNED pattern requires a number." That is not how the guard is built. The 16 BANNED patterns split into two families: identifier-assignment patterns, which require an assignment operator `\s*[:=](?!=)` and NO digit at all, and prose patterns, which require a figure. I proved the number-free half fires: `const <markup-named ident> = someVar` → true, `<breakeven-named key>: computeIt()` → true. The actual reason the runbook sentence escapes is that it is prose (no `[:=]`, so the identifier family cannot fire) AND carries no figure (so the prose family cannot fire) — it falls in the seam between the two families, not past a uniform number requirement. A reader who believed the finder's version would conclude a number-free markup constant is committable, which is false.

(2) INFLATED RULE-6 FRAMING. "The at-cost sentence is also a commercial-model statement sitting in a public repo" overstates the disclosure harm. Rule 6 bans the spread, cost basis, and margin math. This sentence asserts a markup of $MARKUP_MULTIPLE under a model the founder retired on 2026-08-17 — it is false about today's economics and therefore discloses nothing true about the current spread. The real harm is operator misdirection (the primary claim), not disclosure.

(3) SCOPE UNDERSTATED, in the finder's favor. The same drift runs past :186-198. :405-406 repeats "The Bedrock rate table is unverified … first-party list prices as a placeholder (see §1.1d)" and calls it "Blocks re-opening the storefront." :277-280 instructs preserving `FoundationModelId=anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-...` and `ModelId=arn:aws:bedrock:...` — parameters that no longer exist; `lambda/tutor/template.yaml:28` says outright "There is no ModelId parameter any more." :294 says "the roster's Bedrock grants land either way"; that IAM grant is gone too. §1.1d is the worst instance, not the only one.

**Impact.** An operator following the cutover runbook verifies the tutor's cost basis against the wrong provider's price sheet and reaffirms a commercial framing the founder retired — in a document that is the prescribed procedure for turning metering on. The at-cost sentence is also a commercial-model statement sitting in a public repo; `web/__tests__/infra/no-commercial-terms.test.ts` misses it because every BANNED pattern requires a number and this sentence carries none.

### The clawback's zero-floor on the balance is computed from a read outside the transaction and written with no condition, so a concurrent clawback drives the wallet negative

`lambda/stripe/index.mjs:622-638` — `f3c1bf7e2` · low · confirmed · correctness · ran locally · re-raised from `f3c1bf7e2` · fix plan 07

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD. `reclaim` reads the wallet with a separate `GetItemCommand` (:620-623), computes `applied = Math.min(move, Math.max(0, balance))` (:636) and passes `deltaCredits = -applied` into `applyOnce`. The wallet leg carries a `ConditionExpression` only when `hasOwedGuard` is set (index.mjs:268-271), and `hasOwedGuard` requires a finite `expectedOwed`, which `reclaim` supplies only when `owedDelta < 0` (:668-670) — i.e. on a restore. On a withdrawal, `owedDelta = move - applied >= 0`, so there is no condition on the wallet update at all. The receipt leg's OCC token (`${field} = :seen`) serializes clawbacks against the SAME receipt, but two clawbacks against DIFFERENT receipts for the same learner are independent transactions.

**Impact.** Two refunds or a refund and a dispute on two different purchases, landing concurrently, both read balance = N and both subtract up to N, leaving `credits` negative. A negative balance reads as "metering unconfigured" to the client's counter — the exact failure the code comment at :617-619 says the debt field exists to avoid — and hides the top-up path when the learner most needs it. Dormant: requires concurrent clawbacks on a live wallet, and no money has moved.

**Evidence.** lambda/stripe/index.mjs:620-623 (GetItem outside the transaction); :636 `const applied = Math.min(move, Math.max(0, balance));`; :268-271 (the only wallet-leg ConditionExpression, gated on `hasOwedGuard`); :668-670 (`expectedOwed` supplied only when `owedDelta < 0`).

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). Reproduced at HEAD (1f38013). Every structural claim checks out in /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/stripe/index.mjs: the wallet GetItem is outside the transaction (:619-621), `const applied = Math.min(move, Math.max(0, balance));` at :636, `expectedOwed` is passed only on a restore (`...(owedDelta < 0 ? { expectedOwed: owedNow } : {})` at :668), and the wallet leg's ONLY ConditionExpression is gated on `hasOwedGuard` (:247, :274-276 — the finder cited :268-271, which is the same Update leg block, a 3-line citation slip and nothing more). The receipt leg's OCC is `attribute_exists(pk) AND ${field} = :seen` on `receiptKey(paymentIntent)` (:673-680), so it serializes only against the SAME payment intent.

I wrote a scratchpad harness that imports the real `createHandlerCore` and backs it with an in-memory DynamoDB that actually evaluates the three ConditionExpression shapes the handler emits and actually applies SET/ADD atomically per transaction. Command:
  cd /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/stripe && node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-cperez-dev-altivum-inc-quantum/b7fc46e5-3806-4423-bbf8-8ccaa78ee81d/scratchpad/repro.mjs

Setup: WALLET#u1 credits=500, owed=0; two receipts RECEIPT#pi_A and RECEIPT#pi_B, each purchasedCredits=300, for the same sub; two `charge.refunded` deliveries (full refund each) run concurrently, gated so both wallet reads land before either TransactWriteItems.

  Concurrent  -> HTTP 200, 200 | credits = -100 | clawbackOwedCredits = 0 | refundedCredits A/B = 300/300
  Sequential  -> HTTP 200, 200 | credits =    0 | clawbackOwedCredits = 100 | refundedCredits A/B = 300/300
(the sequential control is repro_seq.mjs in the same directory, identical but for awaiting the deliveries in turn — so the divergence is purely the interleaving, not the harness).

Note the second half of the corruption, which the finding does not mention and which makes it worse rather than better: the debt field that the comment at :614-618 says exists precisely to hold the shortfall records ZERO. The 100 credits of shortfall vanish from the ledger entirely — they are neither in `credits` nor in `clawbackOwedCredits`.

The impact chain is real end to end: lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:349 passes `credits` through unclamped, and web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts:190-192 `counter()` maps any value `< 0` to `null` — which that file documents as "the server did not report it". At web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx:780 the top-up affordance renders only when `budget.walletCredits != null`, so a negative balance hides it, exactly as the handler comment fears.

DynamoDB's own TransactionConflict detection does not save this: the losing interleaving is read-A, read-B, commit-A, commit-B, where the two transactions never overlap and no conflict is raised. (In the narrower overlapping case a "TransactionConflict" reason code is not "ConditionalCheckFailed", so :289-296 falls through to `throw`, Stripe retries, and the re-read is correct — which is why only the non-overlapping interleaving is the bug.)

Severity low, agreeing with the finder and for the reasons given: the storefront is closed (rule 15), no purchase receipts exist in production, and `reclaim` returns early with `CLAWBACK_UNRECLAIMED` when there is no receipt — so nothing can fire today. It also needs two distinct payment intents clawed back concurrently for one learner. The damage when it does fire is corrupted wallet accounting and a hidden top-up path, not money leaving.

**Verification — correct as written** (confirmed, low, read). Accurate on every mechanical point; I tried and failed to refute it.

VERIFIED (all reads of /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/stripe/index.mjs):
- :619-623 balance/owed come from a standalone GetItemCommand outside the transaction; :636 `const applied = Math.min(move, Math.max(0, balance));`.
- :274-276 the wallet leg's ConditionExpression is gated on `hasOwedGuard` = `Number.isFinite(expectedOwed)`, and :668 supplies expectedOwed only when `owedDelta < 0`. On a withdrawal owedDelta = move - applied >= 0, so the wallet leg is a bare unconditioned `ADD credits :amt`.
- The OCC token is on receiptKey(paymentIntent) (:669-680), per payment intent. Two clawbacks on two DIFFERENT purchases for one learner touch different receipt rows and are genuinely independent. The code's own comment at :673-677 says that condition "is the only thing closing the lost-update window" — and it does not cover the wallet item.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
- No external serializer: lambda/stripe/template.yaml sets ReservedConcurrentExecutions: !Ref MaxConcurrency, Default 10, and there is no SQS/FIFO in front of the webhook. Concurrent invocations are live.
- DynamoDB's transaction-conflict detection does NOT save it: the two TransactWriteItems need not overlap. T1 can commit entirely between T2's GetItem and T2's write, and there is no read-set validation for an item read outside the transaction.
- No test covers it: index.test.mjs:856 (R5) exercises the SAME-receipt retry via the receipt OCC (cancelledAt(2)); R4 (:845) asserts the floor only in the uncontended single-event case.
- Impact chain confirmed end to end: lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:349 returns Number(credits) with no floor; web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts:190 counter() returns null for anything < 0; lambda/qpu/qpu-core.test.mjs:710 pins null as meaning "unconfigured metering"; web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx:780 gates the low-balance/top-up surface on `walletCredits != null`. So a negative balance really does render as "metering unconfigured" and hide the top-up path — the exact failure the comment at :615-618 says the debt field exists to prevent.

NUANCE (does not contradict the claim, worth carrying): both wallet legs are atomic ADDs, so the AGGREGATE reclaimed amount stays exactly correct. I traced balance=150 with two concurrent 100-clawbacks: race gives credits=-50/owed=0, serial gives credits=0/owed=50, and both reconcile to the same place after a later top-up (splitAgainstDebt) or a funds_reinstated restore. The damage is representational — the shortfall lands in `credits` as a negative instead of in clawbackOwedCredits, the receipt's `${field}Unrecovered` records 0, and the `clawbackOwedCredits = 0` spend gate the serial path would have armed is silently bypassed (the negative balance blocks spending arithmetically instead).

SEVERITY: low is right and I would not raise it. The storefront is closed (rule 15), so no RECEIPT# rows exist and reclaim exits at "no purchase receipt" (:566-576) before reaching this code; the founding-credit gift is deliberately receipt-less (:63-72). Reaching the bug needs an open storefront, two purchases by one learner, and two clawbacks landing inside one another's read-write window.

## Metering and the spend fences

Surviving: 0 high, 3 medium, 9 low.

### How it actually works

The QPU money path is one DI-core, `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs`, wired by a five-line `index.mjs`. Rule 16's four fences are constants at the top of it: `DEVICE`/`DEVICE_ARN`/`DEVICE_REGION` (IQM Garnet, eu-north-1, enforced by `validateSubmitBody`), `MAX_SHOTS = 1000`, `DAILY_CAP_MICROS` + `KILL_KEY`, and the server-minted cost-estimate credential (`requiredShotsFor` → `correctCents` → a `CRED#<sub>` row; `credentialOptionsCollide` moves the unsolvable band with any reprice instead of hardcoding it). `LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS` is 0, and `submit()` refuses at line 563-568 on `effectiveCap > 0` before arithmetic, because the allowance leg's `attribute_not_exists(spentMicros)` clause would otherwise hand a cap-0 learner one free run.

Every submit is one `TransactWriteItemsCommand`: leg 0 is the funding source (ledger allowance or `WALLET#<sub>`), legs 1-3 are the day cap, the idempotency `Put`, and a `ConditionCheck` on the `KILL` row. Cancellation reasons are decoded in a fixed order — idempotency first, then kill, day, funding — and the allowance→wallet fallback runs at most once. Braket submission happens only after the reservation commits; a `CreateQuantumTask` failure runs `releaseReservation`, and anything after the task exists never refunds.

Metering is the pair (wallet table, rate factor). `createHandlerCore` gates it once at line 253-257: a wallet without a usable `RATE_CARD` degrades to exactly the no-wallet behaviour and logs the pinned, alarmed `RATE_CARD_INVALID`. Both kernels — `creditsForMicros` (qpu-core.mjs:97) and `creditsForUsage` (tutor-billing.mjs:276) — throw `RATE_FACTOR_REQUIRED` rather than default to raw cost, and both multiply before the ceil so the round-up stays at most one credit. `RATE_CARD` reaches both stacks through a byte-identical `!If [HasRateCard, !Sub "{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}"…]` line, pinned by `web/__tests__/infra/rate-card-parity.test.ts`; the deployed halves are compared value-blind by `scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs`. `quantum-qpu-reconcile` deliberately carries `WALLET_TABLE` but no `RATE_CARD` — it refunds the `creditsCharged` recorded on the task row, never a re-derivation.

All of this is switched off: `WalletTableName` and `RateCardSecret` both default to `""`, so today an over-allowance submit 402s and nothing debits a wallet.

The client half is where the seams are. `web/src/lib/qpu-budget.ts` re-derives credits with a factorless `Math.ceil(micros / 10_000)`, and `web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts` throws away `creditsCharged`, `fundedBy` and `clawbackOwedCredits` that the server already publishes. Meanwhile `qpu-submit-panel.tsx`, `playground/hardware-panel.tsx` and the pricing page's `<meta name="description">` all promise "at cost… no markup" — a promise rule 9 retired on 2026-08-17 and which three Jest tests now require to be present. The tutor path, by contrast, gets this right: it streams the server's settled `credits` back in the meta trailer rather than letting the browser guess.

### What is genuinely good here

- lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:253-257 — metering is gated as a PAIR at the composition root: a wallet table without a usable factor collapses to `walletTable = undefined` (exactly the metering-off path) and emits the pinned `RATE_CARD_INVALID`, so downstream code never has to re-check the factor and a misconfiguration can never fall through to raw-cost debiting (rule 5).
- lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:563-568 — the `effectiveCap > 0` guard, with the comment naming precisely why a zero cap alone is insufficient: the allowance leg permits a first submit via `attribute_not_exists(spentMicros)`, so a cap-0 learner routed down that path would receive one real-money run free. This is rule 11 enforced by a guard, not by a constant.
- lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:659-678 and lambda/qpu/reconcile.mjs:131-146 — both refund paths read the `creditsCharged` recorded on the task row at debit time rather than re-deriving from `estMicros`, so a change to the conversion between debit and refund cannot silently under-refund (rule 7).
- lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:687 and lambda/qpu/reconcile.mjs:145 and lambda/tutor/index.mjs:497 — every wallet credit-back carries `ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(pk)`, so a refund can never materialize a wallet row nobody paid for (rule 11), and each site turns the resulting cancellation into a loud, alarmed log rather than a swallowed failure.
- scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:14-19,74-76 — value-blind by construction, and it refuses to print even a hash prefix, with the reason spelled out: a rate factor is a short low-entropy string, so an unsalted hash prefix is dictionary-recoverable. Rule 6 honored in an operational tool whose output lands in CI logs.
- web/__tests__/infra/no-commercial-terms.test.ts:180-204 — the rule-6 scanner enumerates via `git ls-files` rather than walking the filesystem (so CI and a contributor's machine see the same set) and carries a non-vacuity assertion that it scanned more than 200 files, which is the guard's own guard.
- lambda/tutor/template.yaml:369-448 — the reserve/settle imbalance alarm. An hour that ends with more `tutorReserve` lines than `tutorSettle` lines fires, which is how a reservation stranded by a timeout or OOM between debit and settle becomes visible even though nothing sweeps the tutor wallet the way reconcile.mjs sweeps the QPU tasks table.
- lambda/tutor/index.mjs:411-419 — the tutor returns the SERVER's settled `credits` in the meta trailer (`{model, label, credits: charged}`) instead of letting the browser re-derive a price. This is the pattern the QPU client should be following and is not.

### RATES overstates sonnet-5's current cost, and the comment calls the resulting overcharge "the safe direction"

`lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs:66-74` — `faa1b8f26` · medium · partly true · correctness · observed live · re-raised from `fcbbf15c1` · fix plan 09

**Claim.** Unchanged at HEAD. The comment records that sonnet-5 carries introductory pricing below the $3/$15 per MTok in `RATES` through 2026-08-31, then calls the resulting effective-markup divergence "a transient rule 5 divergence in the safe direction". Rule 7 defines the safe direction as undercharging the learner; a cost table above true cost charges the learner more, which is the opposite direction.

**Correction.** Two parts of the finding are wrong, in opposite directions. (1) The headline reasoning — that the comment "calls the resulting overcharge 'the safe direction'" in violation of rule 7 — misreads the sentence. Line 69-70 says "a transient rule 5 divergence in the safe direction". Rule 5's stated harm is arbitrage ("the LOWEST markup sets the effective margin... every rational learner spends their credits exclusively on whichever is cheaper"), so a HIGHER markup on one surface is genuinely the non-harmful direction for the rule the comment actually names, and rule 7 is conditioned on uncertainty ("Where metering is uncertain") which does not obtain when the provider publishes both figures. The finder drops the "rule 5" qualifier that makes the phrase accurate. The wording, which the finding calls "the durable problem", is its weakest part. (2) Far more importantly, the finder's scope and impact are wrong in the project's disfavor: "the introductory window closes on 2026-08-31, four days from HEAD" and "The table is otherwise correct as the post-2026-08-31 steady state and needs no edit when the window lapses" are both false. Anthropic CANCELLED the reversion. The overstatement is permanent, not transient, and the table does need an edit. The real defect is not the word "safe" — it is the comment's closing sentence telling the next reader that no edit is needed.

### The wallet-funded confirm step prints a dollar figure a cent below the credit figure beside it, for about half of all shot counts

`web/src/lib/qpu-budget.ts:26` — `feba570d2` · low · confirmed · correctness · observed live · fix plan 09

**The code.** `grep -n "export const usd\|export const creditsForMicros" web/src/lib/qpu-budget.ts` returns exactly line 26 (`Math.round(micros / 10_000) / 100`) and line 34 (`Math.ceil(micros / MICROS_PER_CREDIT)`). `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx:1244-1245` renders them adjacent: `{runCredits} credits` `({usd(micros)})`, with `runCredits = creditsForMicros(micros)` (:918).

**Arithmetic, executed.** A node one-liner over the legal range at the IQM rates in `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:61-62` (300_000 + 1_450·shots):
`node -e 'const T=300000,S=1450;let bad=0;for(let s=1;s<=1000;s++){const m=T+S*s;const c=Math.ceil(m/10000);if("$"+(Math.round(m/10000)/100).toFixed(2)!=="$"+(c/100).toFixed(2))bad++}console.log(bad)'` → **495**. ### A wallet-funded refund whose recorded charge is missing is a silent no-op in the reconciler and unalarmed in the submit path

`lambda/qpu/reconcile.mjs:133-156` — `fa6d6b85c` · low · partly true · correctness · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 09

**Claim.** `run()` passes `creditsCharged: Number(row.creditsCharged?.N ?? 0)` at :225. When a `fundedBy: "wallet"` row lacks that attribute, `refund` builds `ADD credits :pos` with `:pos = "0"`, which succeeds, marks the task FAILED at :174, and returns — the learner is never refunded for a run that never happened, with no log line and nothing to alarm on. `qpu-core.mjs` handles the identical condition properly, logging `qpu-release-credits-unrecorded` at :676 and calling it "an audit gap" — but that literal appears in no `FilterPattern` in lambda/qpu/template.yaml, unlike every other money log line in the stack.

**Correction.** The impact sentence overstates reachability. "Once metering is on, the reconciler's version loses a learner's money silently" needs a second precondition the finding never states: a task row carrying `fundedBy: "wallet"` but no `creditsCharged`. That state cannot be produced by the only writer. `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:487-488` writes both attributes into the SAME `Put` item (`fundedBy: { S: fundedBy }` immediately followed by `...(fundedBy === "wallet" ? { creditsCharged: { N: String(creditsNeeded) } } : {})`), and `grep -n "fundedBy" lambda/qpu/*.mjs` finds no other writer of the attribute anywhere in the stack. So turning metering on is NOT sufficient to make this a money-loss path; it also requires a hand-edited row, a partial migration, or a future code change that splits the two writes. This is the same "should be impossible" condition qpu-core.mjs:673-676 defends against — the defect is an asymmetry in defense-in-depth between two sibling refund paths, not a latent money-loss bug waiting on the metering flip. The finder's own "Impact: Dormant" is right, but for a different and stronger reason than the one given (dormant because the state is unproducible, not merely because metering is off).

**Correction.** The claim that qpu-core's `qpu-release-credits-unrecorded` branch leaves money owed is wrong — that branch falls back to `creditsForMicros(cost, rateFactor)` and completes the refund (qpu-core.mjs:672-678), which is why it is not in the money-loss alarm set. The reconciler's `?? 0` default is unreachable because `fundedBy: "wallet"` and `creditsCharged` are written by one atomic Put (qpu-core.mjs:487-488) and were introduced in the same commit (4504100), so no row shape lacking the attribute has ever existed.

**Impact.** Dormant. Once metering is on, the reconciler's version loses a learner's money silently, and the submit path's version is logged but invisible to the alarms, so neither reaches an operator. Both are the "money owed a learner" class the other refund guards go out of their way to surface.

**Evidence.** `grep -rn 'credits-unrecorded' lambda/qpu/` returns one hit, qpu-core.mjs:676, and no template match. By contrast lambda/qpu/template.yaml:587 covers `qpu-release-failed` and `qpu-refund-wallet-row-missing`, :572 covers the orphaned-row line, and :620 covers reconcile's `wallet row missing for refund`. reconcile.mjs has no equivalent of qpu-core.mjs:670-678's `Number.isFinite(recorded) && recorded > 0` check.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: partly true · correct as written: refuted. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, low, ran locally). MECHANISM REPRODUCED. I wrote a scratch harness against the real `createReconcileCore` (a wallet-funded SUBMITTED row with `creditsCharged` deliberately absent, Braket stubbed to FAILED, ddb stub returning success), ran `cd /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/qpu && node --test repro-audit-check.test.mjs`, then deleted the file (`git status --porcelain` clean). Output was exactly what the finding predicts:

  REFUND LEG 0: TableName "wallet", UpdateExpression "ADD credits :pos",
                ConditionExpression "attribute_exists(pk)", :pos = { N: "0" }
  TASK STATUS LEG: {":failed":{"S":"FAILED"},":submitted":{"S":"SUBMITTED"}}
  SUMMARY: {"checked":1,"completed":0,"failed":1,"pending":0,"orphaned":0}
  LOG LINES: ["qpu-reconcile: {...summary...}"]   <- the ONLY line emitted

So the refund is a zero-credit no-op, the row is transitioned to FAILED (killing the `#s = :submitted` guard that would let a later tick retry), and nothing distinguishes it from a correct refund in the logs. Every cited line number checks out: reconcile.mjs:225 is `creditsCharged: Number(row.creditsCharged?.N ?? 0)`, :146 is `":pos": { N: String(funding.creditsCharged) }`, :174 is `SET #s = :failed`, and reconcile.mjs has no analogue of the `Number.isFinite(recorded) && recorded > 0` guard at qpu-core.mjs:669-678. (The DynamoDB step itself — that `ADD` with operand 0 is accepted rather than rejected — is reasoned from the API contract, not exercised live; the read-only constraint rules out a real table write. Nothing in the path depends on it failing.)

ALARM GAP CONFIRMED. `grep -n "FilterPattern" lambda/qpu/template.yaml` returns exactly four: :572 `"qpu-reconcile: orphaned row"`, :587 `?"qpu-release-failed" ?"qpu-refund-wallet-row-missing"`, :620 `"wallet row missing for refund"`, :650 `"rate card missing or invalid"`. `grep -rn "credits-unrecorded" lambda/` hits only qpu-core.mjs:676 plus its three `.aws-sam` build copies — no template match. I enumerated every emitter (`grep -n "console.error(\|log(\`" lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs lambda/qpu/reconcile.mjs`): reconcile:196, reconcile:214, qpu-core:255, :615 and :743 are each covered by one of the four filters; :676 is the sole money-adjacent line with no filter. The finding's "unlike every other money log line in the stack" holds. And it cannot be caught indirectly — the alarms in template.yaml are the Lambda `Errors` metric (:483/:504/:526), `Invocations` (:551), and the four log-derived metrics; `console.error` does not throw, so it never increments `Errors`.

One point in the stack's favor the finding does not mention: qpu-core's version does NOT strand money. After logging, it falls back to `refundCredits = creditsForMicros(cost, rateFactor)`, so the learner is made whole there — that half really is a pure audit-visibility gap, exactly as the finding says. The reconciler is the half with no fallback.

Severity low is right, and arguably generous. Beyond the unproducible-state argument above, `walletTable` is `""` in the deployed QPU function, so `creditsNeeded` is 0 and `fundedBy` is never "wallet" at all today (qpu-core.mjs:431). No wallet-funded task row has ever existed in production. The useful takeaway for the reader is narrow but real: if reconcile.mjs is ever to be trusted as the backstop the submit path is, it should carry the same `recorded > 0` guard, and `qpu-release-credits-unrecorded` should get the fifth metric filter that its four siblings already have.

This is the same "should be impossible" condition qpu-core.mjs:673-676 defends against — the defect is an asymmetry in defense-in-depth between two sibling refund paths, not a latent money-loss bug waiting on the metering flip. **Verification — correct as written** (refuted, low, ran locally). The finding's precondition — a `fundedBy: "wallet"` task row that lacks `creditsCharged` — cannot be produced by any writer in this repo.

1. **Single writer, one atomic Put.** `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:474-491` is the only code that creates a task row. The item literal writes `fundedBy: { S: fundedBy }` and, on the very next line, `...(fundedBy === "wallet" ? { creditsCharged: { N: String(creditsNeeded) } } : {})`. The two attributes are written by the same expression in the same `Put`, guarded `attribute_not_exists(idempotencyKey)`, inside the same `TransactWriteItems` as the wallet debit. There is no partial-write window: DynamoDB items are atomic, and the only later mutation of that row is `SET #s = :s, taskArn = :arn` (:629), which removes nothing. `grep -rln 'tasksTable\|TASKS_TABLE' --include='*.mjs' .` finds only `index.mjs`, `qpu-core.mjs`, `reconcile.mjs`, the two test files, and `backfill-counters.mjs` — and the backfill only writes `completedRuns`/`completedShots` on the LEDGER table (:101-105). No migration, no admin script, no second writer.

2. **`creditsCharged` can never be 0 on a wallet row either.** `creditsNeeded = walletTable ? creditsForMicros(cost, rateFactor) : 0` (:431), and a wallet-funded run is only possible when `walletTable` is set (:564-568 returns 402 otherwise). `cost = IQM_PER_TASK_MICROS + IQM_PER_SHOT_MICROS * shots` ≥ 300,000 micros (:61-62, :104), and `creditsForMicros` rounds up over `MICROS_PER_CREDIT = 10_000` (:97-99), so the recorded figure is ≥ 30 for any real run. The `?? 0` at reconcile.mjs:225 is an unreachable default, not a live path.

3. **No legacy row shape exists.** `git log --oneline -S'fundedBy' -- lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs` and the same `-S'creditsCharged'` both return commit 4504100 as the introducing commit — the two attributes shipped together, so there is no older on-disk shape carrying one without the other. And metering has never been on (`WalletTableName` defaults to `""`, template.yaml:63-65), so zero wallet-funded rows exist in production at all.

4. **The qpu-core comparison is backwards, not just asymmetric.** The finding calls `qpu-release-credits-unrecorded` (qpu-core.mjs:676) a "money owed a learner" line that the alarms miss. Read the three lines around it: the handler logs the audit note and then `refundCredits = creditsForMicros(cost, rateFactor)` — it *still refunds*, deliberately, "rather than strand the money" (:672-678). No money is owed on that branch. The lines that ARE alarmed are exactly the ones where money is stranded: `qpu-refund-wallet-row-missing` (:743, refund undeliverable without minting a row — rule 11), `qpu-release-failed` (:615), reconcile's `wallet row missing for refund` (reconcile.mjs:196), and the orphaned-row line. `lambda/qpu/template.test.mjs:209-232` pins each of those phrases to the packaged source. The absence of a filter for a "should be impossible" note on a branch that refunds correctly is curation, not a gap.

5. **Even a hypothetical mismatch would not be silent.** If a wallet-funded row somehow reached the reconciler with `WALLET_TABLE` unset, `TableName: undefined` throws a validation error that `isAlreadyTerminal` does not match, so it rethrows and aborts the sweep loudly (reconcile.mjs:183-200). Both functions take the wallet table from the same `!If [HasWalletTable, ...]` in one template (template.yaml:191, :306), so they deploy in lockstep.

Commands run: `node --test lambda/qpu/reconcile.test.mjs` (14/14 pass, including "a refund cancelled by the missing-wallet-row guard is logged loudly, not thrown"); `grep -rn 'credits-unrecorded' lambda/` (confirms the finder's one-hit grep, plus three `.aws-sam/build/` copies); `grep -n 'FilterPattern' lambda/qpu/template.yaml` (confirms no filter for that phrase); `git log -S'fundedBy' -S'creditsCharged' -- lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs`.

What survives is a style observation, not a defect: reconcile.mjs does not repeat qpu-core's belt-and-braces `Number.isFinite(recorded) && recorded > 0` check on a condition neither file can reach. Adding it would be harmless defense-in-depth; its absence loses no one's money, on a path that is doubly dormant (metering off, condition unreachable). Reporting it as "a learner is never refunded" overstates a state the code cannot enter, and the "money owed a learner" framing of the qpu-core half is contradicted by the fallback three lines below the log call.

The claim that qpu-core's `qpu-release-credits-unrecorded` branch leaves money owed is wrong — that branch falls back to `creditsForMicros(cost, rateFactor)` and completes the refund (qpu-core.mjs:672-678), which is why it is not in the money-loss alarm set. The reconciler's `?? 0` default is unreachable because `fundedBy: "wallet"` and `creditsCharged` are written by one atomic Put (qpu-core.mjs:487-488) and were introduced in the same commit (4504100), so no row shape lacking the attribute has ever existed.
