### The reconcile sweep has no per-row error isolation, so one bad row stops all refunds and all medal counters

`lambda/qpu/reconcile.mjs:207-231` — `f0c0225c1` · low · partly true · correctness · ran locally · re-raised from `ff69eae9c` · fix plan 09

**Claim.** Unchanged at HEAD. The `for (const row of rows)` loop awaits `braket.send(GetQuantumTaskCommand)` at :217, `markCompleted` at :220 and `refund` at :223 with no try/catch around the body. Any throw propagates out of `run()`, so the remaining rows are never processed and even the summary log at :232 is skipped. The wallet path widens the blast radius: if `fundedBy === "wallet"` while `walletTable` is undefined — a rollback that clears `WalletTableName` after wallet-funded rows exist — the refund leg is built with `TableName: undefined` at :138, the SDK throws, neither benign-cancellation branch at :187-199 matches, and `throw e` kills the sweep. Because the row stays SUBMITTED, every subsequent five-minute tick hits it again: the reconciler is permanently wedged with no Errors-alarm distinction between that and a transient failure.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong as written.

(1) SCOPE. "One such row halts every refund and every completedRuns/completedShots increment for that tick" is overstated. Rows scanned BEFORE the failing row are fully processed and committed in that tick; only rows at or after it in DynamoDB Scan order are skipped. My repro (4 SUBMITTED rows, row 2 throwing) shows k1's refund TransactWriteItems committing, then the abort — 1 of 4 rows processed, not 0. The correct statement is: every row ordered at or after the wedged row is never processed, this tick and every tick after, because scan order is stable for a fixed item set. Rows before it drain, so from tick 2 onward the wedged row is first and the blockage becomes total for the remaining set — but new rows that hash before it still get serviced.

(2) MECHANISM of the wallet variant. "The refund leg is built with `TableName: undefined` at :138, the SDK throws" is not how it fails. AWS SDK JS v3 does no client-side required-member validation: I probed the real @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb with a stub requestHandler and it serialized the leg happily with TableName simply absent from the body (`{"TransactItems":[{"Update":{"Key":{"pk":{"S":"WALLET#u1"}},...}}]}` — no TableName). The error is a server-side ValidationException from DynamoDB after a network round trip, not an SDK throw. Net outcome (a throw that neither :187 nor :194 matches, aborting the sweep) is identical, so the conclusion survives; the described mechanism does not.

(3) Minor: the wedge is not undetected. `quantum-qpu-reconcile-errors` (template.yaml:495-514, Errors Sum > 0, Period 300, EvaluationPeriods 1) transitions to ALARM on the first wedged tick and holds. The finder's "no Errors-alarm distinction between that and a transient failure" is literally true, but the "permanently wedged" framing reads as silent failure and it is not — it is a red alarm on the alerts topic.

**Correction.** Three parts of the claim are wrong or overstated.

(1) The title — "one bad row stops all refunds and all medal counters" — is false. Each `ddb.send` is awaited and committed independently; there is no outer transaction. Rows processed BEFORE the throwing row in scan order commit normally, and because those writes are status-guarded and idempotent, the next tick re-walks the prefix harmlessly. The accurate statement is: the SUFFIX of the scan after the poison row is never processed on that tick.

(2) "no Errors-alarm distinction between that and a transient failure" is wrong. `template.yaml:495-517` declares `ReconcileErrorsAlarm` (AWS/Lambda `Errors`, Sum, Period 300, EvaluationPeriods 1, threshold > 0) wired to `AlertsTopic`, and `template.test.mjs` asserts every function in the stack has one ("every Lambda function has an Errors alarm wired to the alerts topic" — passing). A permanent wedge errors on every 5-minute tick and holds the alarm continuously; a transient failure clears after one period. Duration IS the distinction, and it is exactly how the alarm is configured to express it.

(3) The two "ordinary" examples offered to make the defect non-dormant are weak, so the "permanently wedged" half of the claim rests only on the dormant wallet scenario. An `@aws-sdk/client-braket` throttle is retried by the SDK's default standard strategy and is transient by definition — it self-heals on the next tick, costing at most a five-minute delay in refunds and medal counters, on guarded idempotent writes that lose nothing by being late. A "task ARN Braket no longer knows" can only enter the table from `CreateQuantumTask`'s own response, so it is not an ordinary case either.

What survives intact: there genuinely is no per-row try/catch, a throw does abandon the remaining rows, and the summary log at :232 is skipped. The wallet mechanism is also correct as described — `template.yaml:305` sets `WALLET_TABLE` via `!If [HasWalletTable, ..., !Ref AWS::NoValue]`, so `process.env.WALLET_TABLE || undefined` yields `undefined`, `refundLeg` is built with `TableName: undefined` at :138, and neither benign-cancellation branch matches a ValidationException.

**Impact.** Dormant (no wallet-funded rows can exist yet), but the same shape already applies to an ordinary Braket `GetQuantumTask` throttle or a task ARN Braket no longer knows: one such row halts every refund and every `completedRuns`/`completedShots` increment for that tick and every tick after it.

**Evidence.** reconcile.mjs:204-234 — no try/catch inside the loop. reconcile.mjs:134-148 builds `refundLeg` from `walletTable` without checking it is defined, though `createReconcileCore`'s own doc comment at :69-71 says "Unset = metering disabled; no wallet-funded rows can exist to refund" — an assumption a rollback breaks.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, low, ran locally). The defect reproduces. I ran it against the real module, not by reading.

Repro (executed): `node /private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/repro.mjs`, which imports `createReconcileCore` from `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/qpu/reconcile.mjs` and feeds it 4 SUBMITTED rows with a braket stub that throws ThrottlingException on row 2. Output:

  run() THREW: ThrottlingException - Rate exceeded
  refund/markCompleted transactions attempted: 1 ['["ledger:USER#u_k1","ledger:DAY#2026-07-07","tasks:undefined"]']
  summary log lines emitted: []

So all three claimed consequences hold: `run()` rejects, rows 3 and 4 are never touched, and the summary log at :232 is skipped entirely. `grep -n "try\|catch" lambda/qpu/reconcile.mjs` returns only the two `.catch()` handlers at :121 and :183, both inside `markCompleted`/`refund` — the `for (const row of rows)` body at :207-231 has no isolation. Unchanged at HEAD (1f38013).

SDK probe (executed): copied a probe into `lambda/qpu/` to use its node_modules and ran it — a real `DynamoDBClient` with a throwing requestHandler, sent a `TransactWriteItemsCommand` whose Update leg has `TableName: undefined`. It serialized without complaint (see correction (2)).

Baseline (executed): `cd lambda/qpu && npm test` — 88/88 pass. None of the 88 covers per-row isolation. `reconcile.test.mjs:231-253` shows the authors reasoned about exactly this hazard for one case only ("It must NOT throw — one unpayable refund must not abort the whole sweep"), and `:255-267` asserts the opposite for everything else ("a genuinely unexpected error on markCompleted still THROWS"). So fail-loud is deliberate; what is missing is catch-log-count-continue, which is a different thing from swallowing and would preserve the loudness the comments at :48-56 are protecting.

Why low, not medium. The wallet variant is doubly dormant: `fundedBy: "wallet"` is only ever written by `qpu-core.mjs:487-488` under metering, which requires `WalletTableName`, and the template gates it (`HasWalletTable`, template.yaml:91,191,306) — so the rollback the finder posits is the only way to get such a row, and metering has never been on. The live variant needs a *persistently* failing `GetQuantumTask`: a transient throttle is retried three times by the SDK's default standard retry mode and the next 5-minute tick re-runs the row anyway, so a one-off throttle costs one tick, not a wedge. A durable wedge needs something like an ARN outside `arn:aws:braket:eu-north-1:${AccountId}:quantum-task/*` (the IAM scope at template.yaml:329-331, which would give AccessDenied every tick) or a task Braket no longer knows. Real, but narrow — and alarmed when it happens.

### The deployed rate-card guard checks only RATE_CARD, so a half-metered deploy still reports MATCH

`scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:33-55` — `ffd037b04` · low · partly true · correctness · observed live · re-raised from `f251543c8` · fix plan 09

**Claim.** Unchanged at HEAD. `FUNCTIONS` is `["quantum-tutor", "quantum-qpu-submit"]` and `readRateCard` queries only `Environment.Variables.RATE_CARD`. But metering on BOTH stacks is the pair (wallet table, factor): qpu-core.mjs:253-257 and lambda/tutor/index.mjs:191-195 each require `WALLET_TABLE` as well. A deploy that sets `RateCardSecret` on both stacks but `WalletTableName` on only one leaves one surface metered and the other silently refusing or free, and this script prints "OK: both surfaces carry the identical rate configuration (MATCH)" and exits 0.

**Correction.** The impact framing is wrong in two places. (1) Rule 5: a half-wallet deploy cannot produce two different markups. Divergent markups require divergent RATE_CARD values, and the script DOES catch that — the `distinctValues > 1` branch at :95-100 fails on it. A missing WALLET_TABLE yields no markup at all on that surface, not a second one. (2) "silently refusing or free" — "free" does not hold for the QPU direction: `LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0` (qpu-core.mjs:47) plus the load-bearing `effectiveCap > 0` guard (:563) means an unmetered QPU refuses over-allowance runs with 402 rather than running them free; on the tutor side an absent wallet refuses paid models and leaves only the deliberately-free Haiku path. Both halves therefore fail toward not charging (rule 7), so what this gap actually costs is observability during a two-step cutover — an operator reading "MATCH" as "both surfaces are live" — not margin, and not a rule 5 breach.

**Correction.** The impact is inverted. The finder frames the blind spot as leaving a surface "silently refusing", but that direction (WALLET_TABLE set, RATE_CARD absent/unusable) is exactly what IS covered — by the script's own PRESENT-UNUSABLE and states.size>1 FAIL branches, and, in the both-absent case, by dedicated per-stack CloudWatch alarms `quantum-tutor-rate-card-invalid` / `quantum-qpu-rate-card-invalid` (metric filters on `"rate card missing or invalid"`, lambda/tutor/template.yaml:505-540, lambda/qpu/template.yaml:645-674) fed by the RATE_CARD_INVALID cold-start log at tutor/index.mjs:193 and qpu-core.mjs:255. The ONLY state the script cannot see is the opposite, fail-safe one: factor present, wallet absent. That surface degrades to today's deliberate behaviour and charges nothing new. Also: the rule citations are a stretch. Rule 5 governs markup divergence between *metered* surfaces — a surface that is entirely off is not a second surface at a lower markup — and rule 12's cost bound still holds because LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS is 0 (qpu-core.mjs:47) behind the `effectiveCap > 0` guard (:563). Rule 14 is about the storefront preceding metering, not the two surfaces' symmetry.

**Impact.** Dormant, but this script is the only check that can see the deployed halves — `web/__tests__/infra/rate-card-parity.test.ts` is explicit that it covers only "the half a clone can see". A partial cutover is exactly the state rule 14's ordering and rule 5's one-markup requirement exist to prevent, and it is the state this guard cannot detect.

**Evidence.** scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:44-48 requests only `Environment.Variables.RATE_CARD`; the three FAIL branches at :85-100 key on ABSENT/PRESENT/PRESENT-UNUSABLE of that one key. `lambda/qpu/template.yaml:91-92` gates `WALLET_TABLE` and `RATE_CARD` on two independent conditions (`HasWalletTable`, `HasRateCard`), so they can be set apart.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, low, observed live). The mechanical claim reproduces exactly. `scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:33` is `FUNCTIONS = ["quantum-tutor", "quantum-qpu-submit"]` and `readRateCard` (`:44-48`) queries only `Environment.Variables.RATE_CARD`; nothing in the file mentions WALLET_TABLE. `lambda/qpu/template.yaml:91-92` and `lambda/tutor/template.yaml:114-118` gate the two env vars on two independent conditions (`HasWalletTable`, `HasRateCard`), so they are settable apart — and `docs/billing-cutover-runbook.md:290-303` explicitly invites the split ("Deploy with them empty first ... add them in a second deploy once §1.1d's rate verification is done"), with §2.1 and §2.3 as separate deploys.

Reproduced with a read-only PATH stub in the scratchpad that answers the script's exact query with an identical factor for both functions (simulating RATE_CARD set on both, WALLET_TABLE on the tutor only):
`PATH="$SCRATCH/bin:$PATH" node scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs`
-> "PRESENT quantum-tutor / PRESENT quantum-qpu-submit / OK: both surfaces carry the identical rate configuration (MATCH)", EXIT=0.

Live state (read-only, real account): `node scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs` prints ABSENT/ABSENT, exit 0; `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-tutor --region us-east-2 --query 'Environment.Variables.{WALLET_TABLE:WALLET_TABLE,RATE_CARD_PRESENT:RATE_CARD}'` (and the same for quantum-qpu-submit) returns null for both keys on both functions. So the gap is entirely dormant today.

Also confirmed the direction of the blind spot: the *complementary* half is already covered — `qpu-core.mjs:253-257` and `tutor/index.mjs:191-195` log RATE_CARD_INVALID when a wallet is set without a usable factor, alarmed by `quantum-*-rate-card-invalid` (qpu template :662, tutor template :527). The uncovered direction is specifically factor-present/wallet-absent, which is silent in both handlers (grep shows the `if` is only `wallet && !factorUsable`) and invisible to this script — the only automated check that reads deployed configuration (`check-lambda-drift.mjs:92` reads LastModified only).

**Verification — correct as written** (partly true, low, observed live). The mechanical claim checks out, verbatim, at HEAD. `scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:32` sets FUNCTIONS to the two pricing lambdas; `readRateCard` (:34-55) passes `--query Environment.Variables.RATE_CARD` and nothing else; all three FAIL branches (:85-100) key on ABSENT / PRESENT / PRESENT-UNUSABLE of that one key. Metering really is the pair: both handlers say so in their own comments and both gate on it — `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:253-257` (`const walletTable = walletTableRaw && factorUsable ? walletTableRaw : undefined`) and `lambda/tutor/index.mjs:191-195` (`const metering = wallet && factorUsable ? {...} : undefined`). And the two halves can be set apart: `HasWalletTable` and `HasRateCard` are independent CFN conditions in both templates (qpu/template.yaml:91-92,191,196; tutor/template.yaml:114-118,145,151). So yes — RATE_CARD identical on both plus WalletTableName on only one prints "OK: both surfaces carry the identical rate configuration (MATCH)" and exits 0.

What the finder missed is which half is blind. The script sees every state in which a surface is configured-but-refusing; that is its three FAIL branches plus the two alarms cited in the correction. What it cannot see is factor-present/wallet-absent — and in that state the un-flipped surface sits in precisely the state both surfaces are in today: tutor serves free haiku and refuses paid models up front, QPU runs the allowance path where `effectiveCap` defaults to `LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0` and `fitsAllowance` requires `effectiveCap > 0`, so a new learner gets a 402. Nothing is charged, nothing new leaks; it fails toward undercharging, which is rule 7's own direction. Note also that the script's ABSENT/ABSENT message ("metering is off on both surfaces") stays behaviourally TRUE no matter what WALLET_TABLE holds, because factor-absent collapses to metering-off in both kernels — so the wallet blind spot cannot make that message lie either. The MATCH string is narrowly worded too ("carry the identical rate configuration"), and the script's header scopes itself to rate configuration rather than to the pair.

Live state, observed read-only: `node scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs` → "ABSENT quantum-tutor / ABSENT quantum-qpu-submit / OK: metering is off on both surfaces", exit 0; and `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-tutor|quantum-qpu-submit --region us-east-2 --query 'Environment.Variables'` returns keys `[SECRET_ID]` and `[EDGE_SECRET, LEDGER_TABLE, RESULTS_BUCKET, TASKS_TABLE]` respectively — neither RATE_CARD nor WALLET_TABLE is set on either function, so the gap is fully dormant.

Worth fixing (query WALLET_TABLE alongside RATE_CARD and fail on asymmetry — a few lines, still value-blind since presence is all that prints), but it is a coverage gap on the safe side of a switched-off system, not a money-losing hole. `docs/billing-cutover-runbook.md:297-305` already carries a manual "verify metering specifically" step that dumps `Environment.Variables`, though that runbook predates the RATE_CARD mechanism (it still names Bedrock `ModelId`/`FoundationModelId` and mentions no `RateCardSecret`), so it should not be counted as a live guard. Severity low, as the finder said.

> Correction. The impact is inverted. The finder frames the blind spot as leaving a surface "silently refusing", but that direction (WALLET_TABLE set, RATE_CARD absent/unusable) is exactly what IS covered — by the script's own PRESENT-UNUSABLE and states.size>1 FAIL branches, and, in the both-absent case, by dedicated per-stack CloudWatch alarms `quantum-tutor-rate-card-invalid` / `quantum-qpu-rate-card-invalid` (metric filters on `"rate card missing or invalid"`, lambda/tutor/template.yaml:505-540, lambda/qpu/template.yaml:645-674) fed by the RATE_CARD_INVALID cold-start log at tutor/index.mjs:193 and qpu-core.mjs:255. The ONLY state the script cannot see is the opposite, fail-safe one: factor present, wallet absent. That surface degrades to today's deliberate behaviour and charges nothing new. Also: the rule citations are a stretch. Rule 5 governs markup divergence between *metered* surfaces — a surface that is entirely off is not a second surface at a lower markup — and rule 12's cost bound still holds because LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS is 0 (qpu-core.mjs:47) behind the `effectiveCap > 0` guard (:563). Rule 14 is about the storefront preceding metering, not the two surfaces' symmetry.

### A clawback debt lockout is indistinguishable from an empty wallet on both the server response and the client

`web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts:112-139` — `fa369a577` · low · confirmed · correctness · observed live · re-raised from `fceac83b1` · fix plan 09

**Claim.** Unchanged at HEAD. `qpu-core.mjs:355` publishes `clawbackOwedCredits` on GET /qpu/budget expressly so the condition is diagnosable, and the `Budget` interface (qpu-client.ts:112-139) and `getBudget` (:203-217) both omit it. The server side conflates it too: the wallet leg's condition at qpu-core.mjs:444-447 fails identically for a missing row, an insufficient balance, and a non-zero clawback, and all three surface as `json(402, {error: "insufficient-credits", creditsNeeded})` at :540.

**Impact.** Dormant. Once metering is on, a learner carrying a clawback debt sees a healthy positive balance beside a hard 402 reading "Not enough credits", with nothing on either the wire or the screen saying why — which is the manual-GetItem debugging session the budget field was added to prevent.

**Evidence.** qpu-core.mjs:350-355 comment: "a learner carrying one sees a healthy positive balance next to a hard 402 and nothing anywhere says why — the first debugging step was a manual GetItem." The field is published and no consumer reads it.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, observed live). Every cited line is exact at HEAD 1f38013 (`git diff --stat HEAD -- web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs` is empty).

SERVER SIDE — verified by reading and by running the suite. /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:355 publishes `clawbackOwedCredits: walletTable ? Number(wallet?.Item?.clawbackOwedCredits?.N ?? 0) : null` on GET /qpu/budget, under a comment saying it exists precisely so the 402 can explain itself. The wallet debit leg at :444-446 is one ConditionExpression with three clauses — `attribute_exists(pk) AND credits >= :need AND (attribute_not_exists(clawbackOwedCredits) OR clawbackOwedCredits = :zero)` — so DynamoDB reports a single `ConditionalCheckFailed` for the leg and the handler cannot tell which clause bit; :540 answers all three with `json(402, {error: "insufficient-credits", creditsNeeded})`. `node --test qpu-core.test.mjs` (54 pass) contains this at :647 (`transact: canceled(R(0))` → 402) and at :713, whose own assertion text is "the balance still reads healthy — that is the confusing part". No extra GetItem is done on the failure path, so the server genuinely cannot disambiguate.

CLIENT SIDE — reproduced with the compiler, not by eye. Probe file importing the real `Budget` type, then:
`cd web && npx tsc --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck --moduleResolution bundler --module esnext --target es2022 <scratchpad>/probe.ts`
→ `error TS2339: Property 'clawbackOwedCredits' does not exist on type 'Budget'.` while `b.walletCredits` on the adjacent line type-checks. `getBudget` (:203-217) maps six fields and drops this one. `grep -rn clawbackOwedCredits web/src` returns exactly one hit — the optional field on `Wallet` in /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/web/src/lib/billing-client.ts:28 — and nothing consumes it either: neither qpu-submit-panel.tsx nor wallet-badge.tsx reads it. The field is published and dead on arrival across the whole web app.

ONE POINT THE FINDING UNDERSTATES. The rendered copy is not the neutral "Not enough credits" the finding quotes; en.ts:736 reads "This run needs {{credits}} credits and your wallet doesn't cover it." Beside a balance line that renders `walletCredits` (qpu-submit-panel.tsx:430-432), a debt-carrying learner is told something demonstrably false about their own balance, not merely something unhelpful. That makes the defect slightly worse than described, not weaker, so it stays CONFIRMED rather than PARTLY_TRUE.

SEVERITY — low, and dormant confirmed live, not just from CLAUDE.md: `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-qpu-submit --query "Environment.Variables"` returns only LEDGER_TABLE, TASKS_TABLE, RESULTS_BUCKET and the edge secret — no wallet table. So `walletTable` is falsy in production: the budget endpoint reports both `walletCredits` and `clawbackOwedCredits` as null and the wallet leg never executes. Reaching this state also requires a purchase plus a refund/dispute exceeding the balance, and the storefront is closed. No spend fence is weakened — the debit still refuses while a debt stands (rule 12 holds); the loss is purely diagnosability, which is what the server field was added to buy and the client never collected. Fix is small: add `clawbackOwedCredits: counter(raw.clawbackOwedCredits)` to `Budget`/`getBudget` and branch the 402 copy on it.

1. Server publishes it — lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:350-355: comment "The debt gate is `clawbackOwedCredits = 0` in BOTH metered backends, so a learner carrying one sees a healthy positive balance next to a hard 402 and nothing anywhere says why — the first debugging step was a manual GetItem", then `clawbackOwedCredits: walletTable ? Number(wallet?.Item?.clawbackOwedCredits?.N ?? 0) : null`.
2. Client drops it — the `Budget` interface (web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts:112-139) and `getBudget` (:203-217) carry capMicros/spentMicros/remainingMicros/credentialed/completedRuns/completedShots/walletCredits/tasks and nothing else. `grep -rn clawbackOwedCredits web/src` returns exactly one hit repo-wide under web/src — the type declaration at billing-client.ts:28 — and zero renders anywhere.
3. Server conflates on submit — qpu-core.mjs:444-446 is one ConditionExpression: `attribute_exists(pk) AND credits >= :need AND (attribute_not_exists(clawbackOwedCredits) OR clawbackOwedCredits = :zero)`. DynamoDB returns a single ConditionalCheckFailed for the leg, so `failed(0)` at :538-540 answers all three causes with `json(402, {error:"insufficient-credits", creditsNeeded})`.

I looked for the usual refutations and found none — no guard, no test, no recorded decision. `git log -S "clawbackOwedCredits: walletTable" -- lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs` gives ac25c22, and `git show --stat ac25c22` touched only qpu-core.mjs and qpu-core.test.mjs; the client was never updated to match.

Severity low is right and I would not raise it. Fully dormant: live WalletTableName is "" (CLAUDE.md: the live QPU function has no wallet metering), so walletTable is null, walletCredits is null, the balance line at :430-432 never renders, and the wallet leg is never built. No money is misdirected — the gate refuses correctly and fails toward not spending (rule 7 direction). This is a diagnosability/UX defect on a switched-off path; the fix is small (parse the field in getBudget, and either name the debt in the refusal token or re-read the wallet row before choosing the 402 message).

### The wallet-funded confirm step still quotes a client re-derivation, and the client discards the authoritative charge the server already returns

`web/src/lib/qpu-budget.ts:34` — `f579f3c94` · low · confirmed · correctness · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `fcb02bbf1` · fix plan 09

**Claim.** Unchanged at HEAD. `creditsForMicros = (micros) => Math.ceil(micros / MICROS_PER_CREDIT)` takes no factor, and its own comment asserts "the figure the wallet-funded confirm step quotes MUST be the figure the server debits" — a claim true only while both are off. qpu-submit-panel.tsx:918 computes `runCredits` from it and :1244 renders it as the pre-click disclosure. Meanwhile qpu-core.mjs:635-644 returns `creditsCharged` on the 202 and `taskSummary` (qpu-core.mjs:219-220) publishes `fundedBy` and `creditsCharged` on every row of GET /qpu/budget — and `qpu-client.ts:253-260` drops both from the success shape, while the `QpuTask` interface at :101-110 omits them so the run history cannot show them either.

**Correction.** Three parts of the reasoning are wrong or overstated. (1) "the run history can never show them" is false: `getBudget` does NOT drop the fields from `tasks` — web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts:215 is a bare cast, `tasks: Array.isArray(raw.tasks) ? (raw.tasks as QpuTask[]) : []`, so `fundedBy`/`creditsCharged` are present on every task object at runtime. Only the TS interface omits them; surfacing them is a two-line type declaration, not plumbing. The history also does show a per-run cost today — `usd(t.estMicros)` at qpu-submit-panel.tsx:1356 — it just shows true AWS dollars rather than credits debited. (2) "the client discards the authoritative charge the server already returns" holds only for the 202/200-duplicate SUCCESS shape. On the 402 path the client keeps the server's authoritative figure (qpu-client.ts:266-268 `creditsNeeded`) and the panel renders it (:1052 → outcomeMessage :1412 → `qpuUi.insufficientCredits`). And nothing post-submit renders a charge at all today (the success message at :1042-1045 names only the task arn), so dropping `creditsCharged` from that shape produces no wrong number — the only wrong number is the pre-click quote. (3) The finder under-scoped the surface: `WalletBar` (qpu-submit-panel.tsx:332) computes the same unfactored `creditsForMicros(costMicros(100))` and renders it LIVE today — it is the branch taken at :243 for any learner without an allowance, i.e. everyone — inside the sentence "A 100-shot run costs {runCost} credits, billed at the Amazon Braket price with no markup" (:346-357). That live copy, not the dormant confirm step, is the larger cutover hazard, and it is a rule 13 surface.

**Impact.** Dormant while metering is off. At cutover the confirm screen understates the debit and the run history can never show what a run actually cost, even though the server states both. CLAUDE.md already names this as blocking the cutover; the missing `QpuTask` fields extend it to the history surface.

**Evidence.** grep for `creditsCharged|fundedBy|clawbackOwedCredits` across web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts and web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx returns nothing. **Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). Verified at HEAD 1f38013, working tree clean for all four cited files (`git status --porcelain` on them returned nothing). Every cited line number is exact.

THE ASYMMETRY IS REAL, AND I REPRODUCED IT. `web/src/lib/qpu-budget.ts:34` is `Math.ceil(micros / MICROS_PER_CREDIT)` — no factor parameter. The server's kernel `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:97` is `creditsForMicros(micros, factor) => Math.ceil((micros * factor) / MICROS_PER_CREDIT)` and REQUIRES the factor. Ran:

  node -e "import('./lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs').then(m => { ... })"

against a 1,000-shot IQM run (1,750,000 micros): client quote 175 credits; server debit 175 / 263 / 350 / 525 at factors 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3; and with no factor the server throws `qpu-core: rate factor missing or invalid; metered pricing refused`. So the two agree only at factor 1, i.e. only while metering is off. The comment at qpu-budget.ts:32 ("the figure the wallet-funded confirm step quotes MUST be the figure the server debits") is a claim the code cannot keep once a factor is deployed. `web/__tests__/lib/qpu-budget.test.ts:174-181` locks the client to the unfactored peg, so nothing reddens at cutover.

THE CLIENT DOES DISCARD THE SERVER'S FIGURE. `qpu-core.mjs:635-644` returns `fundedBy` and `creditsCharged` on the 202, threaded from the debit ("the SAME figure as the debit — threaded, never recomputed"). `qpu-client.ts:253-260` rebuilds the success shape as an object literal carrying only `taskArn`/`estMicros`/`circuitHash` — a genuine projection that drops both. `grep -rn "creditsCharged\|fundedBy\|clawbackOwedCredits" web/src/` returns exactly one hit, `billing-client.ts:28` (an unrelated `clawbackOwedCredits`), confirming the finder's negative-grep evidence.

THE HISTORY HALF HOLDS, WITH ONE NUANCE WORTH KNOWING. `QpuTask` (qpu-client.ts:101-110) omits both fields, and `RunHistory` (qpu-submit-panel.tsx:1342-1362) really does exist and render, showing `usd(t.estMicros)` — raw AWS cost in USD, not credits debited. So under a factor the history would understate too. Nuance for whoever fixes it: `qpu-client.ts:215` is `raw.tasks as QpuTask[]`, a bare cast rather than a field projection, so `fundedBy`/`creditsCharged` DO reach the browser on GET /qpu/budget and only the TypeScript type hides them — the history side is a one-line interface change, while the submitTask side needs an actual code change.

ONE CONSEQUENCE THE FINDING DOES NOT NAME: `runCredits` also gates submission, not just disclosure — `walletCovers` at qpu-submit-panel.tsx:920 feeds `canSubmit` at :921-922. Under a factor the client would also enable the submit button for runs the wallet cannot fund, turning a clean client-side refusal into a server 402.

DORMANCY CONFIRMED, which is why I keep this at low. `lambda/qpu/template.yaml:63-65` and `:74-76` both default `WalletTableName` and `RateCardSecret` to `""`, and `:191` omits `WALLET_TABLE` entirely when unset, so `creditsNeeded` is 0 and `fundedBy` is never "wallet" today. CLAUDE.md already names this exact item as a cutover blocker ("the QPU confirm step quotes a client-derived figure … the server must publish the priced quote and the panel must render it BEFORE the flip"), so this finding corroborates a known open item rather than surfacing an unknown one. Direction of the error matters though: at cutover the learner is quoted LESS than they are debited, which is the wrong side of rule 7.

### The QPU confirm banner still tells the learner the debit is the AWS price converted at the peg — the formula the metering kernel exists to override

`web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx:316` — `ff43686cf` · low · partly true · correctness · observed live · re-raised from `f5a2a88f1` · fix plan 02

(1) The audience claim is false: the banner renders for NO ONE on the live site and never for a signed-out visitor. `web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx:102` computes `const qpuOn = authed && isQpuConfigured();` and line 160 renders `<QpuSubmitPanel/>` only under `{qpuOn && ...}`, so authentication is a hard precondition — the panel's internal `load === "signed-out"` state is a mid-session token expiry, not an anonymous visitor. And `isQpuConfigured()` (web/src/lib/qpu-client.ts:15) requires `NEXT_PUBLIC_QPU_URL`, which is NOT set in the live Amplify build: the shipped chunk that contains this very sentence inlines only the review-email endpoint, never the QPU API id `7zosw1794g`. (2) The finding under-scopes to line 316. The same at-cost/no-markup claim is made five more times on the same surface — `qpu-submit-panel.tsx:305` ("You pay for these runs at cost. We add nothing on top."), `:313` ("with no markup", which is UNCONDITIONAL and therefore renders in the sponsored branch too), `:348` and `:355` ("billed at the Amazon Braket price with no markup"), and `:786` ("credits fund every run at the same Braket rates, with no markup"). Fixing line 316 alone leaves the falsehood standing in both branches.

**Correction.** Real defect, four framing errors. (1) "Renders for every signed-out visitor, i.e. everyone" is false — workspace/page.tsx:102 gates the panel on `authed && isQpuConfigured()`, so only signed-in learners without a stamped allowance see it. (2) Scope is one of six identical strings in the same file (305, 313, 316, 348, 355, 786) plus hardware-panel.tsx:119 and pricing/page.tsx:14; PRODUCT.md:144 names :305, not :316. ## The tutor

Surviving: 0 high, 4 medium, 12 low.

### How it actually works

The tutor is one streaming Lambda (`quantum-tutor`, nodejs22.x, us-east-2) behind an AWS_IAM Function URL, fronted by the CloudFront+WAFv2 stack in `lambda/tutor/edge.yaml` (per-IP 300/min, OPTIONS scope-dropped) with `ReservedConcurrentExecutions: 5` as a second ceiling. I verified all of that live: AuthType AWS_IAM, InvokeMode RESPONSE_STREAM, CORS AllowHeaders content-type / x-amz-content-sha256 / x-tutor-auth, MaxAge 3600, concurrency 5, LastModified 2026-08-18T01:08Z.

`index.mjs` is a DI core (`createHandlerCore({client, corpus, verifier, wallet, rateFactor})`) wrapped by `awslambda.streamifyResponse`. Request flow: `parseBody` rejects >16 KiB by byte length (`BODY_TOO_LARGE` → `TOO_LONG_MESSAGE`), `slug` is looked up with `hasOwnProperty` (prototype-safe), `question` is sliced to `MAX_QUESTION_CHARS`, and a missing section or empty question streams `OUT_OF_SCOPE_MESSAGE`. Model selection (:290-310): `ROSTER.free` models bypass auth and metering entirely; anything else requires `metering` (wallet AND a usable `rateFactor`), a verified Cognito ID token on `x-tutor-auth`, and `isAllowed(tier, requested)` — a known-but-disallowed model is refused in-band, never downgraded. Paid requests take a pre-flight reserve sized by `maxCreditsFor` (worst case = full prompt as a cache WRITE at 1.25x plus `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS[model]` out), and `settle()` refunds down to real usage capped at the reserve. Because the response is committed as HTTP 200 before the model call, every failure is in-band: `TUTOR_ERROR_SENTINEL` plus an exact client-matchable string, with `deadlineGuard(45_000)` converting a hung stream into a throw the catch can reach.

`tutor-core.mjs` and `tutor-billing.mjs` are pure kernels — no imports, no `process` — enforced by `web/__tests__/infra/tutor-kernel-purity.test.ts`, because `scripts/gen-tutor-core.mjs` copies both verbatim into gitignored `web/src/lib/*.generated.ts`. `web/src/lib/tutor.ts` re-exports only sentinels, `MAX_QUESTION_CHARS`, `stripGuideForTutor`, `ROSTER`, `MODEL_LABELS`; I confirmed by grepping `web/out/_next/static/chunks` that `creditsForUsage`, `RATES`, `CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER`, `readUsage` and `maxCreditsFor` are all tree-shaken out — only model ids ship.

Grounding is a build artifact: `scripts/build_tutor_corpus.mjs` reduces every `NN-*/GUIDE.md` through `stripGuideForTutor` into gitignored `corpus.json`, failing the build on truncation; `deploy-check.mjs` gates on corpus freshness and on every roster id being a bare first-party Anthropic id.

Live state matters: the deployed function's environment is `{SECRET_ID: quantum-tutor}` only — no `WALLET_TABLE`, no `USER_POOL_ID`, no `RATE_CARD` — so `metering` is undefined, every paid model refuses with `METERING_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE`, and the only reachable path is free, unmetered Haiku. All eight stack alarms exist and are OK, and both SNS subscriptions are confirmed (real ARNs, not PendingConfirmation). The `quantum-tutor` secret exists (changed 2026-08-17) and the deployed `.mjs` files are byte-identical to git.

### What is genuinely good here

- The kernel-purity guard is real and load-bearing, not aspirational: web/__tests__/infra/tutor-kernel-purity.test.ts:37-50 asserts tutor-core.mjs and tutor-billing.mjs contain no `process`, no static import/re-export, and no dynamic import()/require() — which is what makes it structurally impossible for the rate factor read to land in a file that gets copied into the public web bundle (rule 6 as structure rather than discipline).
- The rule-6 leak the copy could have caused does not happen: grepping web/out/_next/static/chunks for CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER, creditsForUsage, RATE_FACTOR_REQUIRED, readUsage, maxCreditsFor and estimateTokens returns zero hits, while `fable-5` (a ROSTER name the picker legitimately needs) appears once. Tree-shaking drops the whole billing kernel from the shipped bundle.
- index.mjs:271-289 gets the reserve/settle ordering right in the one way that matters: `reserved = need` is assigned only AFTER `wallet.debit` resolves, so a ConditionalCheckFailedException can never be "refunded" by settle(), and the refund leg (index.mjs:487-501) carries `ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(pk)` so a refund can never MINT a wallet row (rule 11).
- index.mjs:183-186 caps the charge at the reserve (`Math.min(creditsForUsage(...), reserved)`), and tutor-billing.mjs:289 scales by the factor BEFORE the ceil rather than after — so the single round-up stays at most one credit regardless of the factor instead of being multiplied by it (rule 7).
- The deadline guard is the right shape: index.mjs:143-153 races every await against a rejecting promise so a hung stream becomes a normal throw the catch can convert into the in-band sentinel, rather than a runtime process kill that would leave the client rendering a truncated body as an authoritative answer.
- tutor-billing.mjs:239 requires BOTH `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` to be present rather than reading a Bedrock-shaped object as all-zeroes, and the SDK's own docstring (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/resources/messages/messages.d.ts:405-406, "Total input tokens in a request is the summation of input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, and cache_read_input_tokens") independently confirms the EXCLUSIVE assumption readUsage is built on.
- The operational half is actually deployed, not just templated: all eight alarms from template.yaml exist in us-east-2 and read OK (quantum-tutor-errors, -corpus-missing, -usage-shape-unrecognized, -orphan-reserve, -orphan-reserve-daily, -refund-failure, -rate-card-invalid, -high-invocations-stack), the old console-created `quantum-tutor-high-invocations` is gone as the runbook required, and both SNS topics' email subscriptions carry real subscription ARNs rather than PendingConfirmation.
- scripts/build_tutor_corpus.mjs:54-67 turns corpus truncation from a WARN that scrolled past into a non-zero exit gated behind an explicit ALLOW_TUTOR_TRUNCATION=1, and deploy-check.mjs:87-112 rebuilds every GUIDE with the same buildCorpusEntry the writer used — I ran it and it correctly reported 03-algorithms and 05-quantum-chemistry as stale.
- ask-tutor.tsx:313-322 splits the TUTOR_META_SENTINEL trailer off the accumulator BEFORE rendering and degrades a malformed/truncated trailer to "no cost line" rather than discarding an answer the learner already has — and ask-tutor.tsx:203 keys the abort cleanup on `slug` rather than an empty dep array, which is what actually makes abort-on-navigation work for a component mounted in the root layout.

Severity medium, not high: this is docs-only with no runtime, money-path or deployed-behavior effect, and tutor metering is off. ### PRODUCT.md tells the public the tutor is "Charged at cost" with no markup on inference, which the shipped rate-factor mechanism and rules 5/9 contradict

`PRODUCT.md:118-121` — `f37e73da0` · medium · confirmed · docs-drift · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 02

**Claim.** PRODUCT.md's AI-tutor paragraph states "Charged at cost — the margin is the subscription, not a markup on inference." That was true of the pre-#237 design. Since dd7abb7 the tutor's metered path REQUIRES an injected `rateFactor` and refuses rather than defaulting to raw provider cost, precisely because raw cost "is a rate that differs from every other surface (rule 5)". Rule 9 says the QPU debits "at the same markup as the tutor", which only parses if the tutor carries a markup.

**Correction.** Two parts of the finder's reasoning are wrong. (1) The impact framing — "A public product document states a commercial policy — how customers are charged for inference ... publishing a false pricing claim" — overstates what PRODUCT.md is. tests/test_pricing_prose.py:29 classifies it explicitly: "# Learner-facing prose surfaces. (PRODUCT.md / docs/ are internal design docs.)" and deliberately excludes it from the learner-facing prose guard, whose scope is GUIDES/NOTEBOOKS/README.md/CLAUDE.md. Customer-facing pricing text lives in web/src/lib/pricing.ts and the i18n copy, separately test-guarded in both locales under rule 13. No customer-facing surface repeats this sentence, so the "false pricing claim reaching customers" path requires a human to copy an internal design doc into shipped copy. (2) The finder scopes the drift to one sentence when the whole document is stale by construction: PRODUCT.md's last commit is 95dc909 (#233), which predates both 4b027bd (#235, tutor off Bedrock) and dd7abb7 (#237, rate factor). The same region also still asserts the 2026-08-02 hardware decision that CLAUDE.md rule 9 explicitly supersedes. This is one instance of a wholesale staleness, not a discrete defect. The finder also missed the sharpest evidence available: PRODUCT.md contradicts ITSELF. Line 141 says hardware "compute carries a margin alongside the subscription"; under rule 5 (one markup across every metered surface) that cannot coexist with line 120's at-cost tutor, with no code required to see it.

**Impact.** A public product document states a commercial policy — how customers are charged for inference — that the code implements the opposite of. Anyone quoting PRODUCT.md into a pitch, a FAQ, or shipped copy would be publishing a false pricing claim, and a future contributor reading it as the product's intent would be steered straight into the rule-5 divergence the RATE_CARD mechanism exists to prevent.

### The deployed tutor grounds answers in a corpus that still contains the two false API claims commit 0108042 removed, and make drift cannot see it

`scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs:61-67` — `f2787155b` · medium · confirmed · correctness · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 10

**Claim.** The tutor's entire knowledge is `corpus.json`, a build artifact baked into the deploy package from `NN-*/GUIDE.md` at deploy time. `check-lambda-drift.mjs`'s `sourceFiles()` filters `/\.(mjs|js)$/`, so `corpus.json` is never compared against git. Commit 0108042 (#242, 2026-08-19) edited 03-algorithms/GUIDE.md and 05-quantum-chemistry/GUIDE.md specifically to remove code that "taught the wrong answer without erroring", and the deployed corpus predates it (function LastModified 2026-08-18T01:08Z). `make drift` reports the tutor green because all three `.mjs` files are byte-identical to git.

**Correction.** The stale-deployed-corpus defect is real and reproduces exactly, but the finding's location and mechanism are wrong. It anchors at `scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs:61-67` and says the `/\.(mjs|js)$/` filter is why "corpus.json is never compared against git." (a) `corpus.json` is untracked and gitignored (`.gitignore:49`), so there is no git version to compare; the script never invokes git at all — it shells only to `aws`, `curl`, `unzip` and reads `join(srcDir, file)` from the WORKING TREE. (b) Therefore widening that filter would NOT surface this: the working-tree `lambda/tutor/corpus.json` is byte-identical to the deployed one in all seven sections, so a `.json`-inclusive drift check compares stale-to-stale and still prints `OK  quantum-tutor`. The real gap is that freshness is only knowable by re-deriving from `NN-*/GUIDE.md`, which only `deploy-check.mjs` does — and it reads the LOCAL file, never the deployed package, so even running it in CI would catch a stale local build, not a stale deploy.

**Impact.** On the only live tutor path, a learner asking about `scripts/variational_utils.py` on 03-algorithms is grounded in text that still lists Adam as a bundled optimizer wrapper, and a learner on 05-quantum-chemistry is grounded in text that still claims `ansatz.py` builds UCCSD. buildSystemPrompt orders the model to answer ONLY from that text and forbids it from guessing API names, so the tutor will state the corrected-away claims confidently. Nothing in CI, drift, or the eight CloudWatch alarms can surface a stale corpus; only a hand-run deploy-check.mjs can.

**Evidence.** I downloaded the deployed package (`aws lambda get-function --function-name quantum-tutor --query Code.Location`, unzipped) and read its corpus.json: `03-algorithms` text contains "Adam" = true, `05-quantum-chemistry` text contains "UCCSD, HEA, custom" = true. Both strings were deleted by `git diff 4aec7f8..HEAD -- 03-algorithms/GUIDE.md 05-quantum-chemistry/GUIDE.md`. `node lambda/tutor/deploy-check.mjs` exits 1 with `stale: corpus entry "03-algorithms" differs from a fresh build of its GUIDE.md (rebuild)` and the same for 05-quantum-chemistry. Meanwhile the deployed index.mjs / tutor-core.mjs / tutor-billing.mjs all diff clean against the working tree.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: confirmed · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, medium, observed live). Reproduced end to end. Read-only throughout; nothing written outside the scratchpad.

1. THE FILTER (scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs:61-67). `sourceFiles()` is `readdirSync(dir).filter(f => /\.(mjs|js)$/.test(f))`. corpus.json cannot match. Stronger than the finding says: `git check-ignore -v lambda/tutor/corpus.json` -> `.gitignore:49`, and `git ls-files lambda/tutor/` does not list it. The corpus is a gitignored build artifact, so there is no git object to diff against — widening the filter to .json would only compare the deployed corpus to whatever stale local build happens to be on the operator's disk.

2. THE DEPLOYED CORPUS IS STALE, on exactly the two cited sections and no others.
   `aws lambda get-function --function-name quantum-tutor --region us-east-2 --query Code.Location --output text` -> curl -> unzip. Package contains corpus.json (110k). Extracting the script-list lines:
     DEPLOYED 03: `variational_utils.py — Classical optimizer wrappers (COBYLA, SPSA, Adam) with logging`
     DEPLOYED 05: `ansatz.py — Parameterized ansatz circuit builders (UCCSD, HEA, custom)`
   Working tree (03-algorithms/GUIDE.md:360, 05-quantum-chemistry/GUIDE.md:327) reads `(COBYLA, SPSA) with per-iteration history and callbacks` and `(UCCSD-inspired singles-only, hardware-efficient)`. `git diff 4aec7f8..HEAD -- 03-algorithms/GUIDE.md 05-quantum-chemistry/GUIDE.md` shows commit 0108042 (#242) as the only edit to either file.

THE CLAIMS IN THE DEPLOYED TEXT ARE FALSE. `grep -n "def \|[Aa]dam" 03-algorithms/scripts/variational_utils.py` -> only `optimize_cobyla` and `optimize_spsa`; no Adam anywhere. `05-quantum-chemistry/scripts/ansatz.py` is a 6-line re-export of `hardware_efficient_ansatz` and `uccsd_singles_circuit` only — no full UCCSD, no "custom".

4. THE GUARD AGREES. Rather than rebuild anything, I fed the DOWNLOADED corpus to the repo's own checker: `node --input-type=module -e 'import {corpusFreshnessProblems, listGuideSections} from ".../deploy-check.mjs"; ...'` -> `stale: corpus entry "03-algorithms" differs from a fresh build of its GUIDE.md (rebuild)` + the same for 05-quantum-chemistry. `node lambda/tutor/deploy-check.mjs` as-is also exits 1 with both lines (the local corpus.json is dated 17 Aug and is byte-for-byte the same stale build).

DRIFT REPORTS GREEN. `node scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs` (full run, 11 functions) -> `OK  quantum-tutor  2026-08-18T01:08:34` and `All 11 functions match git.` The tutor row's only annotation is `(not packaged, assumed ops-only: cfn-slice.mjs, deploy-check.mjs)` — corpus.json is never mentioned. I also diffed the three packaged .mjs against the working tree: index.mjs, tutor-core.mjs, tutor-billing.mjs all identical.

6. NOTHING ELSE CATCHES IT. `grep -rn "deploy-check\|build:corpus\|corpus" .github/workflows/` -> no matches. The tutor template has 8 alarms (`grep -c "AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm" lambda/tutor/template.yaml`); the only corpus-related one is TutorCorpusMissingAlarm, whose own description scopes it to "could not load its grounding corpus" — missing, not stale.

7. THE PATH IS LIVE, not dormant. `tutor-core.mjs:205-206` buildSystemPrompt does say "Answer ONLY using the lesson text provided below" and "NEVER invent or guess Amazon Braket, PennyLane, or Qiskit APIs, method names, parameters..." — verbatim as the finding describes. The `quantum-tutor` secret exists (`aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id quantum-tutor`, metadata only, LastChanged 2026-08-17). NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTOR_URL is set in the live Amplify env: the production chunk at https://quantum.altivum.ai/_next/static/chunks/04-kvrr1wh1sg.js contains `["AskTutor",0,function({wallet,authToken}={}){...w="https://$CF_DOMAIN.cloudfront.net/"` and that endpoint answers (`curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code}` -> 200 on both GET and OPTIONS). I deliberately did NOT post a question — that would spend real Anthropic inference — so the last link (model repeats the stale line) is inferred from the prompt text, not observed.

ONE PRECISION NOTE, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding: "only a hand-run deploy-check.mjs can [surface it]" is generous to deploy-check. It reads the LOCAL corpus.json, never the deployed artifact. It exits 1 here only because nobody rebuilt locally either. Run the documented deploy path (`npm run predeploy` = build:corpus && deploy-check) and the local corpus is rebuilt fresh, deploy-check reports green, and a stale DEPLOYED corpus stays invisible. Nothing in the repo detects the deployed condition; the only thing that does is downloading the artifact and comparing, which is what step 4 above had to do by hand.

SEVERITY: medium, agreeing with the finder. Narrow blast radius (two sentences in a 110k corpus, wrong only if a learner asks about those two scripts) but on a live, signed-in, user-facing AI surface, and the structural half repeats — every future GUIDE.md edit silently diverges the tutor's knowledge from the curriculum with no automated signal.

### On fable-5 a thinking-only generation streams zero answer text but still debits the reserve, and the panel renders the empty-state hint beside the charge

`lambda/tutor/index.mjs:388-392` — `f56ff5083` · low · confirmed · correctness · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 09

**Claim.** THINKING["fable-5"] is "adaptive" and tutor-billing.mjs:102 records that the model rejects `{type:"disabled"}`, so thinking is always on; MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS["fable-5"] is 4,000 and thinking bills against that same ceiling as output. The stream loop writes only `text_delta` chunks, so a generation that exhausts its ceiling while still thinking writes no answer bytes — but settle() still prices the real usage (all 4,000 output tokens at the dearest rate on the sheet) and charges up to the reserve.

**Correction.** The rule 7 framing is wrong. Rule 7 governs metering that is UNCERTAIN ("where metering is uncertain, the learner is charged less"). Nothing is uncertain here: `message_start` + `message_delta` deliver an exact, readable usage report, and `creditsForUsage` (lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs:276-290) prices the tokens the platform genuinely bought. Charging real cost for real tokens is the settle path working as designed, not an inversion of rule 7. What is actually wrong is a product/refund gap — the learner pays for a generation that shows them nothing — plus a misleading render. Also understated: the empty answer is a KNOWN, already-mitigated risk, not an unconsidered one. MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS' own comment (tutor-billing.mjs:150-158) says 800 on fable-5 "would be consumed reasoning and return a truncated answer — or an empty one", and 4,000 was chosen for exactly that reason. Combined with `EFFORT["fable-5"] = "low"` and a short, lesson-grounded prompt, the residual is the tail where 4,000 tokens are ALSO exhausted by thinking. The finder presents it as the ordinary consequence of "thinking is always on"; it is the tail case that survives a deliberate mitigation.

**Impact.** Dormant — fable-5 requires pro tier plus metering, and the deployed function has neither. But when metering ships it charges a learner the platform's most expensive per-token rate for a response containing no answer, which inverts rule 7. Because metered clients always send `meta: true`, the trailer keeps the body non-empty, so ask-tutor.tsx's `if (!acc.trim())` guard never fires: the panel falls through to `tutor.emptyHint` ("Ask anything about this lesson…") with a cost line reading "Claude Fable 5 · N credits" directly beneath it.

**Evidence.** index.mjs:388-392 `if (ev?.type === "content_block_delta" && ev.delta?.type === "text_delta") { stream.write(ev.delta.text); }` — thinking_delta is silently skipped and nothing else writes. tutor-billing.mjs:106-111 `THINKING = { ..., "fable-5": "adaptive" }` with :102 "fable-5 REJECTS {type:\"disabled\"} with a 400. Thinking is always on." index.mjs:411-419 writes the meta trailer after settle regardless of whether any text was produced. ask-tutor.tsx:325-334 the empty-body guard; :447-461 the emptyHint fallback; :466-473 the cost line.

### Haiku is free on every tier including Pro, while the pricing page publishes 1 credit per Haiku question

`lambda/tutor/index.mjs:294-295` — `f7b4670c4` · low · partly true · consistency · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `fb40af359` · fix plan 09

**Claim.** `ROSTER.free` contains `haiku-4-5`, and `ROSTER.plus`/`ROSTER.pro` both include it too. The handler's branch at :294-295 short-circuits any `ROSTER.free` model past auth, tier lookup, reserve and settle — `metered` stays false and `reserved` stays 0 — regardless of who is asking. So a Pro subscriber selecting Claude Haiku in the picker is charged nothing, while `TUTOR_RATES[0]` publishes `typicalCreditsPerQuestion: 1`.

**Correction.** The second half of the title/claim — "while the pricing page publishes 1 credit per Haiku question" — is wrong, and it is the finding's entire "consistency" premise. `TUTOR_RATES` is not published as a current charge. The pricing page renders the table under `pricingUi.tutorTypical`, which reads, in BOTH locales: EN "Typical credits per question once tutor metering ships. Today every question is answered free by Claude Haiku, and the model is not selectable." / ES "Créditos típicos por pregunta cuando se lance la medición del tutor. Hoy cada pregunta la responde gratis Claude Haiku…" (web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:794-795, es.ts:738-739). So the published sheet states exactly what the code does today; there is no advertised-vs-actual contradiction, and no rule 13 exposure. Second correction: the finding frames the exposure as a Pro subscriber. The larger one is the anonymous caller — the :294-295 branch is taken with no token check and no counter at all, so unbounded free Haiku is available to anyone, which breaks rule 2 (the only sanctioned free AI is a hard-capped 10-question trial) more directly than it breaks rule 12. Third: the finding cites CLAUDE.md's remedy ("drop `free` from the tutor ROSTER") without noting that tutor-billing.test.mjs:68-71 asserts strict tier nesting ("paying can never REMOVE a model"), so that literal edit would strip Haiku from plus and pro as well — the fix has to be a metered-Haiku branch, not a roster deletion.

**Impact.** Dormant today (metering is off, so nothing is charged for anything), but it is a rule-5 hole the RATE_CARD mechanism does not close: one wallet means the lowest markup sets the effective margin, and Haiku's markup here is zero and unbounded on every tier. Rule 12's bound — cost to serve bounded by granted plus purchased credits — does not hold for a subscriber who only ever asks Haiku. CLAUDE.md's open work names the remedy ("drop `free` from the tutor ROSTER", add the 10-question trial counter), but the factored-metering work landed without it, so the mechanism's rule-5 claim is narrower than it reads.

**Evidence.** tutor-billing.mjs:35-39 `ROSTER = { free: ["haiku-4-5"], plus: ["haiku-4-5", "sonnet-5"], pro: ["haiku-4-5", "sonnet-5", "opus-5", "fable-5"] }`. index.mjs:294-295 `if (ROSTER.free.includes(requested)) { model = requested; // the funnel model: free for everyone, no auth }` — no `metered = true`, so index.mjs:271 `if (metered)` never reserves. pricing.ts:180-184 `{ model: "Claude Haiku", typicalCreditsPerQuestion: 1, ... }`. No trial counter exists: grep for `trial|lifetime` across lambda/tutor/*.mjs returns nothing.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: partly true · correct as written: refuted. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, low, ran locally). The code behavior reproduces exactly as claimed, and the repo already has a passing test that asserts it.

Read-verified the cited lines. `grep -n "" /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/tutor/index.mjs | sed -n '285,312p'` shows :293-310 verbatim: `if (requested && MODEL_IDS[requested]) { if (ROSTER.free.includes(requested)) { model = requested; // the funnel model: free for everyone, no auth } else { ...auth, readTier, isAllowed... metered = true; } }`. `metered` is initialized false at :292 and set true only in the else branch; `reserved` is assigned only inside `if (metered)` (:312-345). `ROSTER = { free: ["haiku-4-5"], plus: [..haiku..], pro: [..haiku..] }` at tutor-billing.mjs:35-39, confirmed. `grep -rniE "trial|lifetime" lambda/tutor/*.mjs` returns nothing — no trial counter exists, as claimed.

EXECUTED: `cd /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/tutor && node --test --test-name-pattern "M6"` → 7 pass, 0 fail. That test is index.test.mjs:545 — "M6: haiku is free for a signed-in caller — answered, metered at zero, no debit" — which drives `createHandlerCore` with `stubWallet({ tier: "pro" })`, a valid verifier, `rateFactor: 1`, and `{model: "haiku-4-5", meta: true}`, then asserts `wallet.calls.debits.length === 0` ("the funnel model never debits") and `meta.credits === 0`. So a Pro-tier caller getting Haiku for free is not an accident the handler falls into — it is the specified, test-locked contract, stated in the test header comment at index.test.mjs:278 ("haiku-4-5 is free for EVERYONE") and in tutor-billing.mjs:20-21 ("`free` is the anonymous and signed-out tier: the tutor stays free to use, which is the whole funnel").

The picker half of the claim also checks out: web/src/components/ask-tutor.tsx:114 sets `models = TUTOR_ROSTER[wallet.tier]` (tutor.ts:45 re-exports the lambda's ROSTER through a generated copy), :119 defaults `useState("haiku-4-5")`, and :496-512 renders the `<select>` when the tier has more than one model. So a Pro subscriber's DEFAULT selection is the free model. Note this is dormant in production twice over: the picker only renders when a wallet exists, and CLAUDE.md records the live tutor as unmetered (`UserPoolId`/`WalletTableName` both `""`).

Where I land: the defect is real but is a known, deliberate, documented open item, not an oversight the factored-metering work overlooked. CLAUDE.md's open-work list names it verbatim ("Gate `<AskTutor />` on tier; add the free-trial question counter; drop `free` from the tutor `ROSTER`"), and rule 15 keeps the storefront closed until that work lands. The genuinely useful residue — worth keeping, but it is the finding's impact paragraph rather than its headline — is that an unmetered, unauthenticated Haiku surface means the rule 12 bound does not hold, and the RATE_CARD factor mechanism does not close it because it only governs surfaces that reach the metered branch at all. Severity low: dormant, disclosed on the pricing page, and already on the pre-launch checklist.

### resolveModel and TIER_DEFAULT are dead code encoding the opposite policy from the handler, kept green by their own tests

`lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs:185-193` — `f9b7fba6e` · low · confirmed · dead-code · ran locally · re-raised from `f25112b4a` · fix plan 10

**Claim.** `resolveModel` documents and implements a silent downgrade — "an unknown or disallowed request quietly serves the tier default rather than failing a learner's question" — while index.mjs:306 does the opposite for a known-but-disallowed model (`if (!isAllowed(tier, requested)) return refuse(NOT_IN_PLAN_MESSAGE);`), with index.mjs:286-288 stating why. `TIER_DEFAULT.pro === "opus-5"` describes a per-tier default the handler has never had: index.mjs:199 hard-defaults every caller, pro included, to `"haiku-4-5"`. Neither export is imported by index.mjs, ask-tutor.tsx, deploy-check.mjs, or any non-test file.

**Impact.** Two contradictory model-selection policies live in one module and only the wrong one has passing tests asserting its behaviour (tutor-billing.test.mjs:112-118 pins `resolveModel("free", "opus-5") === "haiku-4-5"`). That is how the refused policy gets "restored" by a future contributor who trusts the green suite. It is also copied verbatim into the generated web kernel, though tree-shaking keeps it out of the shipped bundle.

**Evidence.** tutor-billing.mjs:45-49 `TIER_DEFAULT = { free: "haiku-4-5", plus: "sonnet-5", pro: "opus-5" }`; :189-193 `export function resolveModel(tier, requested) { const t = ROSTER[tier] ? tier : "free"; if (requested && isAllowed(t, requested)) return requested; return TIER_DEFAULT[t]; }`. A repo-wide grep for both identifiers finds them only in tutor-billing.mjs, tutor-billing.test.mjs (lines 9, 19, 109-118) and the prior audit doc. The same file's `creditsForUsage({free: true})` option (tutor-billing.mjs:276-277) is likewise test-only.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). Every clause reproduces; I could not refute any of them.

DEAD CODE. `grep -rn "resolveModel\|TIER_DEFAULT" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git` (run at /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum) returns matches only in lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs (:45, :189-192), lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.test.mjs (:9, :19, :109, :112-118), the gitignored generated web copy, and docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-18.{md,json}. `sed -n '38,56p' lambda/tutor/index.mjs` shows the import list is ROSTER, MODEL_IDS, MODEL_LABELS, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, USAGE_SHAPE_UNRECOGNIZED, isAllowed, modelRequestOptions, readUsage, creditsForUsage, maxCreditsFor, estimateTokens — neither dead export. `grep -n "from \"" lambda/tutor/deploy-check.mjs` shows :37 imports only `{ ROSTER, MODEL_IDS }`; web/src/lib/tutor.ts:38 imports only `{ ROSTER, MODEL_LABELS }`; ask-tutor.tsx names neither.

CONTRADICTORY POLICY. `node -e "import('./lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs').then(m=>console.log(m.resolveModel('free','opus-5')))"` printed `haiku-4-5` — the silent downgrade its doc comment at :185-188 advertises. `sed -n '275,320p' lambda/tutor/index.mjs` shows :306 `if (!isAllowed(tier, requested)) return refuse(NOT_IN_PLAN_MESSAGE);` for that same known-but-disallowed case, with :286-289 explaining why ("serving Haiku to someone who asked for (and expected to pay for) Opus is a mis-serve, not a graceful degrade"). The finding is correctly scoped: it claims the contradiction only for the KNOWN-but-disallowed case, which is the one the handler genuinely inverts. (For an unknown name the handler's own comment at :288-289 endorses the fall-through, so test lines 109/113/118 do not contradict it — the finding does not claim otherwise.)

TIER_DEFAULT.pro. Same node import printed `TIER_DEFAULT = {"free":"haiku-4-5","plus":"sonnet-5","pro":"opus-5"}` and `resolveModel('pro', undefined) = opus-5`. `grep -n "model = \|creditsForUsage\|maxCreditsFor" lambda/tutor/index.mjs` returns only :199 `let model = "haiku-4-5"`, :295 `model = requested`, :307 `model = requested` — the per-tier default is never consulted for any tier, pro included. Divergence is in the rule-7 safe direction (cheaper model), so no money consequence.

GREEN SUITE. `cd lambda/tutor && node --test tutor-billing.test.mjs` -> 25 pass, 0 fail; `sed -n '105,120p' tutor-billing.test.mjs` confirms :116 `assert.equal(resolveModel("free", "opus-5"), "haiku-4-5")` pins the policy the handler refuses. That is exactly the "restored by a future contributor who trusts the green suite" hazard the finding names.

WEB KERNEL. Accurate as hedged. `grep -n "resolveModel\|TIER_DEFAULT" web/src/lib/tutor-billing.generated.ts` -> :48, :192, :195 (scripts/gen-tutor-core.mjs:27 copies the file verbatim). `git check-ignore -v web/src/lib/tutor-billing.generated.ts` -> `.gitignore:68`, so it never enters the public repo. `grep -rl "TIER_DEFAULT\|resolveModel" web/out` across 520 shipped JS files returns nothing, matching the finding's own "tree-shaking keeps it out of the shipped bundle". No rule-6 exposure either way — the dead exports carry no markup or cost basis.

SIDE CLAIM. `creditsForUsage({free:true})` is test-only as stated: the handler's one call site (index.mjs:227) passes `{ factor: metering.factor }`; `grep -rn "free: true" lambda/ web/src` hits only tutor-billing.test.mjs:177, 286, 287, 290.

SEVERITY. Low, and I would not raise it. No live path executes either export; the module is pure and moves no money through them; the deployed tutor is free and unmetered. The cost is repo hygiene plus a green test asserting a deliberately-rejected policy in a file whose whole subject is money.

**Verification — correct as written** (confirmed, low, ran locally). I tried hard to refute this and could not. Every sub-claim holds.

Dead outside tests. `grep -rn "resolveModel\|TIER_DEFAULT" .` (excluding node_modules/.git/docs) returns only `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs:45,189,192` and `lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.test.mjs:9,19,109,113,114,116,118`. `index.mjs`'s import block (lines 42-53) pulls ROSTER, MODEL_IDS, MODEL_LABELS, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, USAGE_SHAPE_UNRECOGNIZED, isAllowed, modelRequestOptions, readUsage, creditsForUsage, maxCreditsFor, estimateTokens — neither dead export. `deploy-check.mjs`, `handler-wiring.test.mjs`, `web/src/lib/tutor.ts:38` (imports only ROSTER + MODEL_LABELS) and `ask-tutor.tsx` do not reference them either.

Severity: low is correct, not inflated. Worth noting for the reader: this exact item is already recorded in `docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-18.md:684` and its fix plan item 4 (line 2255) — it is a still-unfixed prior finding, not a new one.

### The usage merge lets message_delta's nullable input legs overwrite message_start's real counts, and readUsage's `?? 0` keeps the migration alarm silent when it does

`lambda/tutor/index.mjs:401-405` — `f51eac289` · low · partly true · correctness · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `f07ce0f4d` · fix plan 10

**Claim.** `usage = { ...usage, ...ev.usage }` on `message_delta` spreads every key the event carries. The SDK types that payload as `MessageDeltaUsage` with `input_tokens: number | null`, `cache_creation_input_tokens: number | null` and `cache_read_input_tokens: number | null`. When those arrive null, they replace message_start's real values; `readUsage` still passes its `"input_tokens" in usage` presence check and coerces each null through `?? 0` into a finite zero, so it returns a valid object rather than null.

**Correction.** The defect requires `message_delta.usage` to carry explicit `null` input legs. Published Anthropic streaming docs show the fields are either absent (spread does not overwrite — safe) or present as real cumulative numbers (overwriting is the correct read), report `0` rather than `null` when nothing was cached, and state that message_delta token counts are cumulative. No null example exists. The cited `number | null` type is a generated-type artifact — the same interface marks `server_tool_use` non-optional while the docs' own example omits it — so it is not evidence of wire behavior. The residual is a hardening suggestion (match the SDK's `!= null` guard at MessageStream.js:445), not a live undercharge; the claimed magnitude is also overstated, since in cache-read steady state the correct and clobbered charges are frequently identical.

**Correction.** Two parts are wrong. (1) The `?? 0` is NOT what keeps the alarm silent — `node -e "console.log(Number(null), Number.isFinite(Number(null)))"` prints `0 true`, so `Number(usage.input_tokens)` coerces null to a finite 0 with or without the `?? 0`; deleting the nullish default would change nothing. The title's attribution is misplaced (the `?? 0` only matters for an ABSENT key, and an absent key is never copied by the spread in the first place, so that path is already safe). (2) "A large silent undercharge" does not survive the arithmetic. `node /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/probe3.mjs` against the real `RATES` at factor 1: in the cache-READ steady state that prompt caching is designed to produce (14 uncached in / 5,529 cache-read / 400 out) the nulled report prices IDENTICALLY for haiku-4-5 and sonnet-5 (1 credit either way) and drops opus-5 from 2 to 1 — the round-up to whole credits absorbs most of it. The loss is material only on the first question of a cache window or an uncached prompt: sonnet-5 3→1, opus-5 5→1, fable-5 9→2. Also, the trigger is a type-legal but unobserved payload: the documented `message_delta` frame carries either `usage:{"output_tokens":N}` (keys absent — the spread is then a correct merge) or the cumulative form with real numbers (also correct); the SDK's `!= null` guard covers the absent case too, so its existence is evidence of defensiveness, not proof the service emits explicit nulls.

**Impact.** On the input-dominated tutor workload the generation would then be priced at output-only — a large silent undercharge in the safe direction, but with no signal: `USAGE_SHAPE_UNRECOGNIZED` fires only when readUsage returns null, so the very alarm built to catch a provider field change (template.yaml:337-366) cannot see this one. Dormant today (the deployed function has no WALLET_TABLE, so settle never prices anything), but it lands the moment metering is switched on. Neither test double can catch it: index.test.mjs:309 emits `message_delta` with only `output_tokens`, and probe-cache.mjs uses a non-streaming create() whose single `res.usage` never exercises the split at all.

**Evidence.** index.mjs:401-405. node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/resources/messages/messages.d.ts:319-340 `interface MessageDeltaUsage { cache_creation_input_tokens: number | null; cache_read_input_tokens: number | null; input_tokens: number | null; output_tokens: number; ... }`. tutor-billing.mjs:239-247 `if (!("input_tokens" in usage) || !("output_tokens" in usage)) return null; const out = { input: Number(usage.input_tokens ?? 0), ... }; return Object.values(out).every(Number.isFinite) ? out : null;`. index.test.mjs:309 `yield { type: "message_delta", usage: { output_tokens } };`. probe-cache.mjs:42-51 calls `client.messages.create` without `stream: true`.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: refuted · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (refuted, low, ran locally). The mechanism is real but the trigger is not. The finding's whole premise — "when those arrive null" — is inferred from a generated TypeScript type, and the documented wire shape contradicts it.

What I verified as TRUE (executed, /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/repro.mjs importing the real `readUsage`/`creditsForUsage` from /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/tutor/tutor-billing.mjs): if `message_delta` ever carried explicit nulls, `{...usage, ...ev.usage}` does clobber the input legs, `readUsage` returns `{input:0,output:400,cacheRead:0,cacheWrite:0}` rather than null, and the `usage && !readUsage(usage)` alarm at index.mjs:222 stays silent. So the second half of the chain is exactly as described.

What refutes it — the provider never sends those nulls. `WebFetch https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming` (302 from docs.claude.com), then `grep -n "message_delta" -A3 <saved> | grep -i usage` and `grep -n '"input_tokens": *null\|"cache_read_input_tokens": *null\|"cache_creation_input_tokens": *null' <saved>`:
- Every plain example omits the input legs entirely: `"usage": {"output_tokens": 15}`. Absent keys are not copied by object spread, so message_start's values survive untouched.
- The one example where they appear carries real cumulative numbers: `"usage":{"input_tokens":10682,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":510,"server_tool_use":{...}}` — and note it reports `0`, not `null`, in precisely the case where nothing was cached.
- The page states outright: "The token counts shown in the `usage` field of the `message_delta` event are *cumulative*." Cumulative means overwriting with them is the CORRECT read, not a clobber. A cumulative counter's nil value is 0.
- Zero `null` input legs appear anywhere on the page.
Running both documented shapes through the merge (`node -e` spread check) yields the right answer in each case: absent → `input_tokens:14, cache_read:5529` preserved; present → the delta's cumulative values adopted.

The cited type evidence does not carry the weight put on it. `MessageDeltaUsage` also declares `server_tool_use: ServerToolUsage | null` as non-optional, yet the docs' basic `message_delta` example omits that key entirely — so "required and nullable" in this generated type does not mean the wire always sends the key, and is not evidence that nulls arrive. Nor does the SDK's own guard prove it: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/sdk/lib/MessageStream.js:445-455` writes `if (event.usage.input_tokens != null)` with the comment "Update other usage fields if they exist in the event" — `!= null` catches undefined as well as null, so it is consistent with absence being the only real case.

Two of the finding's subsidiary claims are accurate and worth keeping: index.test.mjs:309 does emit only `output_tokens`, and probe-cache.mjs:42-51 is non-streaming, so neither double exercises a delta that carries input legs at all.

What is left is a hardening nit, not a defect: the handler's merge is less defensive than the SDK's reference accumulator. A one-line `!= null` guard would cost nothing. But there is no reproducible undercharge here — and even in the hypothetical, the magnitude is smaller than claimed. `creditsForUsage` at factor 1 on a 5,529-token prefix (repro2.mjs) gives opus-5 correct=5 vs clobbered=2 on a cache-WRITE turn, but correct=2 vs clobbered=2 in cache-READ steady state, because cache reads price at 0.1x. "Priced at output-only" is literally what happens to the fields, but on the steady-state cached workload that is often the same charge, not "a large silent undercharge."

I could not exercise the real streaming endpoint: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in env, no `ant` CLI, and the key lives in Secrets Manager, which CLAUDE.md forbids reading. So this rests on the vendor's published wire contract plus the SDK source, not on a captured live stream.

Published Anthropic streaming docs show the fields are either absent (spread does not overwrite — safe) or present as real cumulative numbers (overwriting is the correct read), report `0` rather than `null` when nothing was cached, and state that message_delta token counts are cumulative. No null example exists. The cited `number | null` type is a generated-type artifact — the same interface marks `server_tool_use` non-optional while the docs' own example omits it — so it is not evidence of wire behavior. The residual is a hardening suggestion (match the SDK's `!= null` guard at MessageStream.js:445), not a live undercharge; the claimed magnitude is also overstated, since in cache-read steady state the correct and clobbered charges are frequently identical.
