Client components that read and parse localStorage on the render path therefore have no boundary above them: review-dashboard.tsx:110 `snapshot()` calls dueCardIds() and getAllCardIds(), hooks/use-workspace.ts:24 `snapshot()` calls getAllCardStates(), completedCount(), getAllMeasurements() and dueCount(). Each of those wraps its own scan in try/catch, so the current safety is a property of every individual call site rather than a backstop — and there is nothing to catch a throw from the code between them, or from a component that forgets.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong, and one relevant fact is omitted.

(1) "no not-found page for a mistyped /learn/<slug>" is false. Next's built-in not-found IS emitted by the export: `web/out/404.html` (24,937 bytes) contains `404` and `This page could not be found.` and is served at https://quantum.altivum.ai/404.html (HTTP 200). Live, `https://quantum.altivum.ai/learn/does-not-exist-xyz` returns **HTTP 404** and a fully rendered page — the host's error response serves `index.html` (the response body is byte-identical in length to `web/out/index.html`, 79,457 bytes), so a mistyped slug lands on the home page with a 404 status, never a blank. What is actually missing is a *custom* `not-found.tsx`, i.e. the 404 body is generic/mis-targeted — not that there is no not-found page at all.

(2) "there is nothing to catch a throw from the code between them" is false for one of the two cited call sites. `web/src/hooks/use-workspace.ts:24-41` wraps the ENTIRE `snapshot()` body in a single try/catch returning `SERVER_SNAPSHOT` — that covers `getAllCardStates()`, `completedCount()`, `getAllMeasurements()`, `dueCount()` AND every loop and `epochDay(Date.now())` call between them. It is a function-level backstop, not per-call-site defensiveness. Only `review-dashboard.tsx:109-110` `snapshot()` is itself unwrapped, and both of its callees are internally guarded (`review-store.ts:146-157` `getAllCardIds` has its own try/catch; `dueCardIds` is built on it).

That is precisely the highest-risk render path the finding worries about — dynamically imported widgets keyed off a localStorage-derived `kind` — on /review and every lesson route.

Also: the cited location `review-dashboard.tsx:106` is `entries: RosterEntry[];` inside `interface RosterState`. The comment the finding is paraphrasing ("src/app carries no error boundary") is at line 90; `snapshot()` is at 109-110.

**Verification — correct as written** (refuted, low, observed live). The file-absence half is true and trivially re-confirmed: `find /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/web/src -name 'error.tsx' -o -name 'global-error.tsx' -o -name 'not-found.tsx'` returns nothing, and WidgetErrorBoundary (web/src/components/quantum/widget-fence.tsx:137) is the only hand-written boundary. But the stated DEFECT — the impact paragraph — is false in both of its halves, and that paragraph is the whole basis for calling this correctness rather than polish.

(1) "blanks the route with no fallback UI" is wrong. Next 16.2.6 ships a built-in default global error boundary. web/node_modules/next/dist/client/components/app-router.js:456 reads "At the very top level, use the default GlobalError component as the final fallback" and wraps the Router in RootErrorBoundary with errorComponent = the builtin. That builtin (node_modules/next/dist/client/components/builtin/global-error.js) renders a styled card: h1 "This page couldn't load", message "Reload to try again, or go back.", plus Reload and Back buttons. It is in the shipped export, not just node_modules: `grep -rl "Reload to try again, or go back" /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/web/out/_next/static/chunks/` → out/_next/static/chunks/03edqrb4zdj~g.js. A thrown client render gets a generic-but-real recovery UI with a retry affordance, not a blank page.

(2) "no not-found page for a mistyped /learn/<slug>" is wrong. Observed live: `curl -s -o /tmp/404live.html -w "HTTP %{http_code}" -L https://quantum.altivum.ai/learn/not-a-real-section` → HTTP 404. The build already emits out/404.html and out/_not-found.html from Next's builtin not-found (themed inside RootLayout, `grep -o 'name="robots" content="[^"]*"' web/out/404.html` → noindex), and it is deployed: `curl -s -o /tmp/direct404.html -w "%{http_code}" https://quantum.altivum.ai/404.html` → HTTP 200. What actually renders at the mistyped path is index.html served at 404 status — `md5 -q /tmp/404live.html` equals `md5 -q` of `curl https://quantum.altivum.ai/` (both 75d19419b2cbb2de43312fb1b54de943, 79457 bytes) — because Amplify's default `/<*>` → `/index.html` 404 rewrite decides the 404 document, not the App Router. Adding not-found.tsx would therefore change nothing about the live behaviour the finding complains of; the lever is the Amplify redirect rule, which is not in this repo.

(3) The "no backstop, only per-call-site guards" reasoning is wrong for one of the two sites it cites. web/src/hooks/use-workspace.ts:24 wraps the ENTIRE snapshot() body in a single try/catch returning SERVER_SNAPSHOT — covering getAllCardStates(), completedCount(), getAllMeasurements(), dueCount() AND the code between them, which the finding explicitly asserts nothing catches. (review-dashboard.tsx:108-110 is as described: getAllCardIds() carries its own try/catch at review-store.ts:147, and getCardStateRaw at :99.)

(4) The cited comment is a recorded deliberate decision, not evidence of an accident: review-dashboard.tsx:86-91 explains that liveWidgetFor uses Object.hasOwn specifically so a corrupt localStorage `kind` cannot resolve through the prototype chain — "The documented 'corrupt kind falls back to the recall card' guarantee lives here." The absence is known, guarded at the one place it could bite, and cheap to code around.

(5) This exact finding has already been adjudicated twice in the repo's own audit history with these same corrections: docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-16.md:466 ("'no not-found page' is wrong about what ships: the build already emits web/out/404.html ... Likewise the App Router has a default root error boundary; the gap is the absence of *custom* ones, i.e. a polish item, with no concrete failure mode stated"), and docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-18.json:2664 restates it again.

What survives is genuinely small and is not what was filed: there is no CUSTOM error/not-found UI, so a throw replaces the whole document with Next's unbranded generic card (losing nav, theme and locale) instead of an in-app recovery. That is a design-polish item on a fully-guarded path, not a correctness defect, and the finder's own "low" is if anything generous for it.

### consumeHandoff() still runs inside a render-phase useState initializer, so a discarded render destroys the playground-to-workspace circuit

`web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx:902` — `f16d5f4fa` · low · partly true · correctness · ran locally · re-raised from `f0d2975d1` · fix plan 13

**Claim.** Unchanged. `const [handoff] = useState(() => consumeHandoff());` performs a destructive `sessionStorage.removeItem` (qpu-handoff.ts:60-68) inside a render-phase lazy initializer. React makes no guarantee that a render is committed: under StrictMode's double-invoke, or any concurrent render that is thrown away, the removeItem side effect persists while the state it produced does not. The adjacent comment ("State initializers run exactly once, so the consume never re-fires on re-render") is true of re-renders and does not cover a discarded render. The right shape is peekHandoff() in the initializer with the clear in a commit-phase effect — peekHandoff already exists at qpu-handoff.ts:55-57 and is unused in src/.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. (1) The named trigger is disproven: React does NOT lose the handoff under StrictMode's double-invoke. I instrumented the initializer and confirmed it runs TWICE (calls = 2), yet the committed state is the FIRST call's result — the one that got the circuit — so the StrictMode case renders the handoff QASM, not PRESETS[0]. (2) The residual trigger ("any concurrent render that is thrown away") has no reachable path to this component in this app: `grep -rn "Suspense|useTransition|startTransition|useDeferredValue|next/dynamic|React.lazy" web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx web/src/components/workspace/` returns 0 hits, and the whole of web/src contains "Suspense" only in src/app/login/page.tsx and src/lib/circuit-url.ts — neither above SubmitForm. SubmitForm mounts from a plain post-await setState in Panel's fetch effect (qpu-submit-panel.tsx:170-190, default lane, no transition), so nothing in the /workspace tree can throw that render away short of a time-sliced default render restarted by a higher-priority interrupt, which I could not reproduce. The impact sentence ("a learner ... can silently lose it") therefore describes no demonstrated user-reachable path.

**Correction.** The named primary mechanism — "under StrictMode's double-invoke" — is factually wrong and must be struck. React 19.2.4 keeps the FIRST initializer call's value: react-dom-client.development.js:8264-8278 assigns from the first call (8268) and discards the second call's return (8272, the impurity probe), and the StrictMode second render pass installs HooksDispatcherOnRerenderInDEV (7761), whose useState never re-invokes the initializer. Verified empirically — under <StrictMode> the committed value is the handoff, not the preset — which matters more than the finder knew, since StrictMode IS on by default here (next.config.ts sets no reactStrictMode; next/dist/build/define-env.js:143-144 maps null to true for __NEXT_STRICT_MODE_APP). Only the "discarded concurrent render" half stands, and the app tree contains no Suspense, lazy, dynamic() or transition around SubmitForm (used once at web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx:165; mounted at qpu-submit-panel.tsx:260 off a plain default-lane setState in a promise continuation), so the sole reachable trigger is a discrete-event interruption forcing a prepareFreshStack restart mid-render — rarer than "a discarded render at exactly the SubmitForm mount" implies.

**Impact.** A learner who compiles a circuit in the playground and routes to /workspace#hardware can silently lose it and land on the default PRESETS[0] instead, with no error. Narrow: it needs a discarded render at exactly the SubmitForm mount, and the loss is recoverable by going back to the playground. But peekHandoff being present and unused means the safe primitive was written and then not wired.

**Evidence.** qpu-submit-panel.tsx:898-902; qpu-handoff.ts:60-68 `consumeHandoff` (removeItem, unconditional); qpu-handoff.ts:55-57 `peekHandoff` — `grep -rn consumeHandoff web/src` shows the one call site, `peekHandoff` has none outside __tests__/lib/qpu-handoff.test.ts.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, low, ran locally). The code reads exactly as cited — web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx:902 is `const [handoff] = useState(() => consumeHandoff());`, and web/src/lib/qpu-handoff.ts:60-68 `consumeHandoff` does an unconditional `sessionStorage.removeItem`. `peekHandoff` (qpu-handoff.ts:55-57) is indeed unused in src/ (grep -rn "consumeHandoff|peekHandoff|writeHandoff" web/src web/__tests__ shows the one src call site; peek appears only in __tests__/lib/qpu-handoff.test.ts and __tests__/components/playground/playground-bench.test.tsx).

I reproduced both halves in jsdom against the repo's own React 19.2.4 / RTL, using a faithful copy of the line-902 shape plus an instrumented counter:

  cd /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/web && npx jest --config /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-cperez-dev-altivum-inc-quantum/b7fc46e5-3806-4423-bbf8-8ccaa78ee81d/scratchpad/sp/jest.config.js

(scratchpad-only files: sp/jest.config.js, sp/strict.test.tsx, sp/strict2.test.tsx; nothing in the repo was written — `git status --porcelain` is unchanged from the session-start snapshot.)

Results:
- `render(<StrictMode><Mimic/></StrictMode>)` → "STRICT: initializer calls = 2 | rendered = OPENQASM..." — double-invoke happens, handoff SURVIVES. The finder's headline mechanism does not hold. (And StrictMode double-invoke is dev-only regardless; next.config.ts sets no reactStrictMode either way.)
- A genuinely discarded render — a sibling that suspends AFTER the component rendered, inside a Suspense boundary — DOES destroy it: "SUSPENSE/consume: calls = 3 | rendered = PRESET_FALLBACK | storage = cleared". Swapping in `peekHandoff()` under the identical setup renders the QASM ("SUSPENSE/peek: rendered = OPENQASM..."), confirming the proposed fix is the right shape.

So the abstract defect is real and the suggested fix (peek in the initializer, clear in a commit-phase effect) is correct — but it is a latent purity violation, not a defect a learner can hit today: the one construct that provably triggers it (a Suspense boundary) does not exist anywhere above SubmitForm, and the trigger the finding actually names is empirically false. Worth fixing as hygiene, or as insurance before anyone wraps /workspace in Suspense or a transition; not worth reporting as a circuit-losing bug.

### /workspace is still the only walled route with no metadata, and two files now document a noindex it does not have

`web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx:1` — `f2d4f2e61` · low · confirmed · docs-drift · observed live · re-raised from `f3f8d7a2e` · fix plan 13

**Claim.** Still true, and the drift has spread. workspace/page.tsx opens with `"use client"`, which makes a `metadata` export impossible, and it exports none — while /credentials, /review, /runbook, /playground and /glossary each carry `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` at their page.tsx:7. robots.ts:13 deliberately allows everything ("Noindex + absent from the sitemap is the correct exclusion"), so a rendered noindex is the only mechanism, and /workspace has none. auth-wall.tsx:57-59 asserts "the per-page robots noindex keeps the walled URLs out of search indexes", and sitemap.ts:8-11 now names workspace explicitly in the list of routes that "carry a noindex meta and redirect unauthenticated visitors to /login".

**Impact.** A crawler that reaches /workspace by any route other than the sitemap gets a page with no exclusion signal, only a client-side JS redirect it does not execute. Low: the URL is not linked from any public page and the rendered DOM is the auth gate. The docs half is the more durable cost — two source comments now state a protection that does not exist, so the next reader will not think to add it.

**Evidence.** `for f in credentials review runbook playground glossary workspace; do grep -n 'robots' web/src/app/$f/page.tsx; done` returns `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` for the first five and nothing for workspace. web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx:1 `"use client";`. auth-wall.tsx:57-59; sitemap.ts:8-11. `git diff 4aec7f8..HEAD -- web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx` is empty.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, observed live). I tried to refute this three ways — a workspace-level layout.tsx carrying metadata, a root-layout robots default, and an X-Robots-Tag header at the CDN — and all three came back empty. Every claim holds, at source, at build output, and on the deployed site.

SOURCE. `cd web/src/app && grep -rLn "robots" --include=page.tsx . | sort` lists exactly nine page.tsx files with no `robots`: auth/callback, changelog, founding-ten (both), login, `/`, pricing, privacy, and workspace. Cross-referencing `PUBLIC_PATHS` + `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` in auth-wall.tsx:20-27 (`/`, `/pricing`, `/login`, `/auth/callback`, `/privacy`, `/changelog`, `/e2e-fixtures`, `/founding-ten`), all eight others are public routes that are *supposed* to be indexable — so /workspace is indeed the ONLY walled route without it. `ls -la web/src/app/workspace/` shows page.tsx is the only file in the directory (no layout.tsx), `sed -n '1,2p'` confirms line 1 is `"use client";`, and web/src/app/layout.tsx's root `metadata` sets metadataBase/title/description/openGraph/twitter but no `robots`. So there is no inheritance path.

BUILD OUTPUT. `cd web && for f in workspace glossary credentials review runbook playground; do grep -o '<meta name="robots"[^>]*>' out/$f.html; done` — the five walled peers each emit `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"/>`; workspace.html emits nothing.

LIVE (this is the part that settles it). `curl -s https://quantum.altivum.ai/workspace | grep -o '<meta name="robots"[^>]*>'` returns nothing while the same curl against /glossary and /review both return `noindex, nofollow`. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"` on /workspace returns 200. `curl -sI https://quantum.altivum.ai/workspace | grep -i x-robots` returns nothing — no header-level exclusion either. `curl -s https://quantum.altivum.ai/robots.txt` is `User-Agent: * / Allow: /`, matching robots.ts:13's deliberate design, and `curl -s .../sitemap.xml | grep -c workspace` is 0. Live <title> is the bare inherited `Quantum Learner`, further confirming no page-level metadata. So the URL is crawlable, 200, and carries zero exclusion signal of any kind.

DOCS DRIFT. Both cited comments are verbatim at the cited lines. sitemap.ts:8-11 names workspace inside the parenthetical list of routes that "carry a noindex meta"; that sentence is simply false for one of its seven members. auth-wall.tsx:57-59's "the per-page robots noindex keeps the walled URLs out of search indexes" is a generalization with exactly one exception, and that exception is workspace. `git diff --stat 4aec7f8..HEAD -- web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx` is empty; last touch was f0f7f29.

IMPACT, checked rather than assumed. `grep -rl 'href="/workspace"' web/out --include='*.html'` returns nothing, and the sole occurrence of the string in out/index.html is the prose eyebrow "Your workspace". The only in-repo links (`grep -rn '"/workspace' web/src`) are account-menu.tsx:149 and credentials-wall.tsx:331 — both signed-in surfaces — plus router.replace calls in the auth flow. So discovery requires an external link or a stray referrer, which is why I judge this low and not medium: real, dormant, no money or security surface. The durable cost is the finder's second point — sitemap.ts asserts a protection that does not exist, so the next person to audit indexing will read that list and check nothing.

### The pricing page and the QPU panel still publish two different credit prices for the same IQM Garnet run

`web/src/components/quantum/qpu-submit-panel.tsx:332` — `fafb6aed0` · low · partly true · consistency · observed live · re-raised from `fe95b2089` · fix plan 02

**Claim.** Still true; the only change to this file since 4aec7f8 was colour-token renaming. `runCost = creditsForMicros(costMicros(100))` at :332 derives from raw provider list rates (`cost.ts:6 IQM: { perTask: 0.3, perShot: 0.00145 }`) → ceil(445,000 µ$ / 10,000) = **45 credits**, and the surrounding copy states it flatly: "You pay for these runs at cost. We add nothing on top." (:304), "the exact Amazon Braket price… with no markup" (:310-314), "Runs are billed at the Amazon Braket price with no markup — a 100-shot run costs 45 credits" (:348). The published sheet says otherwise: pricing.ts:85 `creditsPerShot: 0.163` for IQM Garnet plus pricing.ts:60 `TASK_FEE_CREDITS = 34` → jobCredits() = **50.3 credits** for the identical run. Two figures, 12% apart, for one thing. Rule 5 (every metered surface at the same markup) and rule 9 (QPU debits at the same markup as the tutor) both name this; CLAUDE.md records the reconciliation as open work blocked behind rule 14.

**Correction.** Three things in the finding's reasoning/scope are wrong. (1) The divergence is NOT undocumented — `web/src/components/pricing/cost-estimator.tsx:1-10` states it verbatim in a header comment ("Different table, different currency, $SPREAD_PCT apart, so do not describe the two as one estimate") and `web/__tests__/app/pricing-page.test.tsx:404-415` carries a dedicated copy-honesty pattern barring the page from claiming the two estimates are the same, with an explicit retirement condition ("Retire this pattern only when one table feeds both surfaces"). The finder cites only CLAUDE.md, framing this as untracked drift when it is guarded, commented, tracked open work. (2) The "45 vs 50.3 side by side" comparison is not what the two live surfaces render. `/pricing` hardcodes `exampleShots = 1000` (pricing-page-content.tsx:84) and ships 197 credits for IQM Garnet; the estimator also defaults to 1,000 shots (cost-estimator.tsx:94). 50.3 is reachable only by moving the estimator's shot control to 100. The live default comparison is 197 (sheet) vs 175 (panel formula at 1,000 shots). The underlying disagreement is real at every shot count, but the specific pair of numbers quoted is not co-rendered. (3) "12% apart" is 11.78% at 100 shots (50.3/45); the repo's own $SPREAD_PCT figure is the 1,000-shot ratio (197/175). Minor: the copy is at :305, not :304, and the finder missed a third instance at :786 ("credits fund every run at the same Braket rates, with no markup"). Severity is low, not medium: LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS is 0, the effectiveCap > 0 guard holds, the deployed QPU has no wallet metering, and the storefront is closed by rule 15 — so no figure can be charged, and CLAUDE.md blocks the cutover behind exactly this reconciliation.

Making 45 and 50.3 agree would either disclose or destroy the spread. (2) Rules 5 and 9 govern what a METERED surface debits. ### The privacy page's log-retention statement no longer describes what the platform does with visitor request logs

`web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:947-948` — `f30eea6e9` · low · partly true · privacy · observed live · fix plan 05

**Claim.** `privacyUi.retentionLogs` tells readers, in both locales, that "Operational service logs (used for debugging and abuse prevention) are retained in AWS CloudWatch for 30 days and then deleted automatically" (en.ts:947, es.ts:875), and it is the only sentence on the page about request logs. Since #247 a live scheduled Lambda reads the site's CloudFront access logs through Amplify's `GenerateAccessLogs` (lambda/analytics/index.mjs:62-69) — a store that is neither CloudWatch nor covered by that 30-day sentence — and writes a derived daily row to `quantum-analytics-daily` with `TimeToLiveSpecification` deliberately omitted (template.yaml:64) and PITR on. I confirmed both are live and running: `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-analytics` returns State Active, and the table is ACTIVE with 8 items and TTL DISABLED. The "What we store" list (en.ts:919-931) names Cognito, progress, prefs and hardware runs; it does not mention this. The changelog CI guard cannot catch the omission either, because `scripts/changelog/rules.mjs:60-80 LEARNER_VISIBLE` watches no path under `lambda/`.

**Correction.** Two of the three legs are wrong, and the strongest leg is one the finder set aside.

(a) "Since #247 a store that is neither CloudWatch" misattributes the gap. The Amplify/CloudFront access-log store predates the change and is not created by it. `scripts/analytics/backfill.mjs:35` reads `const LAUNCH = "2026-06-28"; // Oldest day with retrievable logs, verified.` — logs existed two months before the collector deployed (2026-08-20) — and the stack's only log-side IAM action is `amplify:GenerateAccessLogs` (template.yaml:96), a read. So the "operational logs live in CloudWatch for 30 days" sentence was already partial about access logs before #247; the change added a reader, not a store.

(b) The "permanent derived record" leg is the weakest, not the strongest. A live scan shows the row holds day + counts only, no identifier: `aws dynamodb scan --table-name quantum-analytics-daily --region us-east-2 --max-items 2` returns day/requests/uniqueIps (a count, 212)/humans/humanPageViews/googleSignIns/malformed/buckets/botFilterComplete/computedAt. Nothing personal is retained forever, so a missing retention clause about that row is not the defect.

(c) What is genuinely new and undisclosed is the PURPOSE, which the finder concedes to the code's defense. `privacyUi.retentionLogs` limits those logs to "debugging and abuse prevention" (en.ts:948, es.ts:876); `humans`, `humanPageViews` and `googleSignIns` are audience measurement, not abuse prevention. And `noAnalytics` renders as a bullet under the heading `whatWeDont` = "What we don't collect" (privacy-page-content.tsx:39-45), which makes "No analytics ... none exist anywhere on this site" read as a collection claim, not the script-only claim `index.mjs:9-16` and README.md:11-18 defend it as.

**Correction.** Three parts of the reasoning are wrong or overstated. (1) The retentionLogs sentence is not false and does not "no longer describe" anything — it describes CloudWatch Lambda log groups, and every template still sets exactly that: `RetentionInDays: 30` / `LogRetentionInDays` default 30 in analytics, qpu, stripe, sync, tutor, review-email, ci-standby. Nothing #247 shipped contradicts it. (2) The Amplify/CloudFront access-log store predates #247 and exists regardless of the Lambda — Amplify records it whether or not anything reads it — so "since #247 a store that is neither CloudWatch nor covered by that sentence [exists]" is not a new condition, and "a reader is not told that request logs are separately collected" was equally true before the PR. #247 changed only what is *derived* from them. (3) The permanent artifact holds no personal data whatsoever: the row is `day` plus eight integers/booleans (`requests`, `uniqueIps`, `humans`, `humanPageViews`, `googleSignIns`, `malformed`, `buckets`, `botFilterComplete`, `computedAt`), pinned by an allowlist assert in lambda/analytics/index.test.mjs:68-88 that fails the build if any other attribute is written. "A permanent derived record is kept" is true but it is anonymous day-level statistics — outside what a retention section exists to bound. The real, narrower gap is one of PURPOSE, not retention: the page says request logs are "used for debugging and abuse prevention" and lists "No analytics" under "What we don't collect," and neither now describes daily audience measurement. The finder waved that line through as surviving "on its letter" and anchored the finding on the one sentence that is still literally true.

**Impact.** A legal page states a complete-sounding retention rule that is now partial. The two adjacent claims survive on their letter — nothing is added to the browser (no script, cookie or beacon), and only counts are written — but a reader is not told that request logs are separately collected and processed, nor that a permanent derived record is kept. This is live in production, not dormant.

**Evidence.** en.ts:947 / es.ts:875 retentionLogs; en.ts:934 noAnalytics ("No analytics or tracking scripts — none exist anywhere on this site."); privacy-page-content.tsx:41,54 render both. lambda/analytics/index.mjs:62-69 GenerateAccessLogsCommand; :79-95 PutItem of day/requests/uniqueIps/humans/humanPageViews/googleSignIns/malformed/buckets/botFilterComplete/computedAt; lambda/analytics/template.yaml:64 "DELIBERATELY NO TimeToLiveSpecification". aws describe-table → ACTIVE, ItemCount 8; aws describe-time-to-live → DISABLED.

**Severity drift.** Finder claimed medium; verification published low.

The changelog leg holds: `sed -n 50,90p scripts/changelog/rules.mjs` shows `LEARNER_VISIBLE` lists only `web/src/**` and the numbered notebook dirs — no `lambda/` path, so a lambda-only PR is never required to announce itself.

Live (read-only), us-east-2: `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-analytics` → State Active, LastModified 2026-08-20, TABLE_NAME quantum-analytics-daily. `aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name quantum-analytics-daily` → ACTIVE, ItemCount 8; `aws dynamodb describe-time-to-live` → DISABLED. `aws dynamodb scan ... --max-items 2` → the 2026-08-26 row: 1940 requests, 212 uniqueIps, 3 humans, 0 googleSignIns, per-bucket counts. Running in production, and the row is counts only.

Severity: low, not medium. The remedy is one sentence of copy; no personal data is retained (verified by the scan); the log collection itself predates the change and is already disclosed as operational logs; and further processing for statistical purposes is expressly compatible under GDPR Art. 5(1)(b), so the exposure is a transparency/purpose-statement inaccuracy on a legal page, not a data-handling defect. ## Claims and copy honesty

Surviving: 2 high, 5 medium, 9 low.

### How it actually works

Copy honesty in this repo is enforced by a small, unusually thoughtful set of denylist guards, and the defects cluster precisely where those guards do not reach.

The machinery. `web/__tests__/app/pricing-page.test.tsx` holds `UNDELIVERABLE_CLAIMS` — ~12 regexes (present-tense metering, `sponsor\w*|patrocin\w*`, blanket-free promises, model "unlocks", priority queues) run over the rendered `/pricing` page in both locales plus its metadata export. `web/__tests__/_support/changelog-ban-list.ts` (#238) is the same shape for `/changelog`: `BANNED_CLAIMS` plus `firstAffirmativeMatch`, which walks *every* match and treats the **clause** (not the sentence) as the negation window — #240 pinned exactly the "Credits are not sold yet, but you can now top up" shape that the first version let through. It is scanned over three surfaces: `CHANGELOG`/`CHANGELOG_ES` strings, the rendered page in en+es, and the metadata export. Rule 6 has its own guard, `web/__tests__/infra/no-commercial-terms.test.ts`, which enumerates `git ls-files` (not a filesystem walk, so CI and a contributor's machine see the same set), asserts it scanned >200 files, and bans markup identifiers, markup-as-prose, cost-per-credit and breakeven figures. All four suites pass at HEAD (126 tests). I found **no rule 6 leak** anywhere in tracked files.

`scripts/changelog/rules.mjs` makes the changelog mandatory: `LEARNER_VISIBLE` is a literal list (`web/src/app/`, `web/src/components/`, `web/src/i18n/locales/`, seven curriculum dirs, and nine named `web/src/lib` content files), and any diff touching it must also touch `web/src/lib/changelog.ts` — satisfied either by an entry or by a `SILENT` row carrying the PR number and the reason it is not news. #244 and #246 are recorded there.

Where it breaks. The guards are page-scoped, and the front door has none. The public landing page (`home-page-content.tsx:98-102`, `:163`, `:265`) still sells "real quantum hardware", "Graduate from simulator to real QPUs" and an "on-ramp to real quantum hardware" in the present tense, in both locales, while `/pricing` — the guarded page — says "hardware runs are not currently available". `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:47` sets `LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0` and `:563-568` refuses every submit that no allowance and no wallet can fund, so that promise is false for 100% of learners. `README.md:7` still opens with "sponsored, so a learner never pays".

The docs tier lags the code by one migration. `README.md` describes four Lambdas (there are six) and calls the tutor Bedrock in four places; `PRODUCT.md:118-122, 178-181, 216` and `docs/billing-cutover-runbook.md:188-197` all still carry the Bedrock-era rate story and the "margin is the subscription, not a markup on inference" doctrine that `RATE_CARD` superseded on 2026-08-17. The Lambda READMEs, by contrast, are current — `lambda/tutor/README.md:7-22` and `lambda/qpu/README.md:10-16` both state the migration and the allowance withdrawal correctly.

Finally, the new `quantum-analytics` stack is deployed and collecting (verified live: `quantum-analytics-daily` holds real rows), which puts pressure on a privacy bullet written when nothing collected anything.

### What is genuinely good here

- The rule 6 guard is real and has teeth: web/__tests__/infra/no-commercial-terms.test.ts:188-224 enumerates tracked files via `git ls-files` (deliberately, so a CI clone and a contributor's machine scan the same set), asserts `files.length > 200` so the walker cannot silently no-op, and bans markup identifiers, markup-as-prose, per-credit cost and breakeven figures. I grepped the whole repo independently and found no markup constant, cost basis, or margin arithmetic in any tracked file.
- The changelog ban list's negation handling is genuinely better than the usual denylist: web/__tests__/_support/changelog-ban-list.ts:80-98 evaluates EVERY match rather than `pattern.exec`'s first, and `clauseStartBefore` scopes the negation window to the clause, not the sentence — the file documents both failures it was written to fix ("You cannot buy credits yet. You can purchase a plan today." and "Credits are not sold yet, but you can now top up your wallet.").
- web/src/lib/changelog.ts:5-19 makes `shipped` mean visible-in-production rather than merged, and says plainly that no test can enforce it — "the field name is the whole enforcement." The SILENT array at :113-124 then puts the decision NOT to announce (#244, #246) into version control with its reason, which is more reviewable than a magic string in a PR description.
- docs/instrument-after-dark.md:63 records that the design kit's aspirational "QPU live · IQM Garnet" HUD line shipped instead as "Simulator live · in-browser" because hardware runs are not available — and hero.tsx:30 carries the same note in code. A rule 13 decision taken during a pure design pass, and documented at both ends.
- lambda/analytics/index.mjs:9-16 and :81-95 are as advertised: the written item is `day/humans/requests/malformed/buckets/googleSignIns/computedAt` and nothing else. I scanned the live `quantum-analytics-daily` table read-only and confirmed the deployed rows carry no address, user agent, or path — the README's "stores no identifiers" claim is true.
- lambda/tutor/README.md:7-22 and lambda/qpu/README.md:10-16 are current where the root docs are not: the tutor README states the Bedrock migration, the availability-vs-entitlement trap, and that `RATES` stopped being a placeholder; the QPU README states `LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0` and that grandfathered `capMicros` rows are still honored.
- docs/exercise-convention.md's central claim holds: all 45 notebooks under the seven curriculum directories contain `### Exercise` cells, and `tests/solutions/` carries exactly 45 canonical-answer files with no notebook missing one. PRODUCT.md:207's "7 / 45 / 32" also reconciles against web/src/lib/content-manifest.json.
- The global no-emoji-in-UI rule is honored: a Unicode scan over every tracked .ts/.tsx under web/src returns zero emoji characters.
- lambda/analytics/README.md:104-109 names the four hand-maintained lists a new Lambda must join and says lambda/stripe was missed in two of them for three weeks — and all four (.github/workflows/ci.yml:162, infra/ci-standby/template.yaml:186, scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs:52, web/__tests__/infra/wallet-ttl.test.ts:46) do register `analytics`.

### README.md's opening tagline still promises sponsored, never-pay QPU runs — the promise withdrawn on 2026-07-28

`README.md:7` — `f98cc585b` · high · confirmed · rule-violation · observed live · RESOLVED 2026-08-27 · fix plan 01

**Resolved 2026-08-27.** Merged to main 2026-08-28 in PR #248 (squash commit 2a06bef); live on the next Amplify deploy. All three README claims rewritten: the opening tagline now reads "free in your browser, or on real Braket hardware from your own AWS account"; the Philosophy note reads "Hardware runs are not currently available on quantum.altivum.ai"; and `allowlisted_gate_devices()` is described as the "hard-capped" rather than "sponsored" submit path. `grep -nE "sponsor|never pays|platform pays" README.md` now returns nothing. The structural half is closed too, along the line the verifier recommended: rather than build a new guard, `tests/test_pricing_prose.py` — which already loaded README.md for the dollar-figure scan — gained `test_no_withdrawn_hardware_promise_in_learner_facing_prose`, a claim guard over README.md plus all 14 GUIDE files in both locales. It was proved to fire on all five removed sentences and to stay silent on all five replacements before being accepted. 699 pytest pass; ruff clean.

**Claim.** The first bold sentence of the public repository README reads: "The Braket-native learning platform where the code you write runs unmodified — free in your browser, or on a real 20-qubit QPU — sponsored, so a learner never pays." Line 34 repeats it operationally ("On quantum.altivum.ai the platform pays for QPU runs") and line 373 names "the sponsored QPU-submit path". The sponsored allowance was withdrawn 2026-07-28; `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:47` is `LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0` and the platform pays for nothing. `lambda/qpu/README.md:10-16` states the withdrawal correctly, so the two READMEs in the same repo contradict each other. The pricing page's guard bars `/sponsor\w*|patrocin\w*/` in both locales (pricing-page.test.tsx:322-324) and the changelog ban list bars it too (changelog-ban-list.ts:57-58) — but no guard reads README.md, which is why the withdrawn promise survives in the loudest place it appears.

### PRODUCT.md's "Known divergences" and tutor sections state four things the code and the live account disprove

`PRODUCT.md:118-122` — `fd5710618` · medium · confirmed · docs-drift · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 02

**Claim.** PRODUCT.md is the designated "durable product truth" and four of its load-bearing statements are false at HEAD. (1) :118-121 — the tutor "settle[s] on real Bedrock token usage"; it settles on Anthropic first-party usage since 2026-08-17. (2) :121-122 — "Charged at cost — the margin is the subscription, not a markup on inference" directly contradicts CLAUDE.md rules 5 and 9 and the shipped `RATE_CARD` factor. (3) :177-179 — "The live QPU function predates the sponsorship withdrawal and runs without wallet metering; … In production the platform still pays"; `quantum-qpu-submit` was last modified 2026-08-18, three weeks *after* the 2026-07-28 withdrawal, so the platform pays for nothing. (4) :180-181 — "Roughly nine shipped pricing strings in both locales still tell learners hardware runs are platform-sponsored, and one is locked by a test"; grep finds exactly one sponsorship string left in each locale (`credentialsUi.outOfReachDetail`, en.ts:614 / es.ts:597), deliberately kept, and the pricing test now *bars* the pattern rather than locking it. (5) :216-218 — "no verified Bedrock inference rates — the tutor's rate table is an explicitly unverified placeholder and is the single named blocker on reopening the storefront"; CLAUDE.md records that item closed 2026-08-17 and lists several other open blockers.

**Correction.** Item (3)'s conclusion "so the platform pays for nothing" is wrong, and its evidence was too weak as offered. (a) The LastModified timestamp alone proves a redeploy, not that the deployed code carries the withdrawal — I strengthened it by running `node scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs`, which reports "All 11 functions match git," so the deployed quantum-qpu-submit does contain the post-withdrawal LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0. (b) The platform still pays for the tutor: `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-tutor --query "Environment.Variables"` returns only {"SECRET_ID": "quantum-tutor"} — no wallet, no user pool, no RATE_CARD — so the live tutor is free and unmetered and every answer is on the platform's dime. PRODUCT.md:179 "In production the platform still pays" is therefore TRUE of the tutor half of that same bullet; only the QPU half is false. The correct statement of the defect is narrower: the bullet's heading ("Deployed Lambdas lag `main`") and its QPU clause are false, while its tutor clause is the one thing in the divergence register that is still accurate.

**Impact.** A divergence register that lists already-closed divergences and misses the live ones is worse than none: it will send the next person to re-do a copy sweep that was completed, and it tells them the QPU Lambda is stale when it is current. Item (2) is the more dangerous one — it states a pricing doctrine the project has explicitly superseded, in the file another engineer would treat as authoritative.

### The privacy page's "What we don't collect: No analytics" bullet is contradicted by a deployed analytics stack that classifies every visitor daily

`web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:934-935` — `f89164e09` · medium · confirmed · privacy · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 05

**Claim.** Under the heading "What we don't collect" / "Qué no recopilamos", the page states "No analytics or tracking scripts — none exist anywhere on this site" (en.ts:934-935; es.ts:862-863). Since 2026-08-20 the `quantum-analytics` Lambda has run daily against the previous day's CloudFront access logs, classifying every visitor as human/scanner/declared-bot/datacenter/high-rate/high-volume/no-assets and writing the counts, plus a Google sign-in count, to `quantum-analytics-daily`. I confirmed live: the function exists (LastModified 2026-08-20) and the table returns real rows. `lambda/analytics/README.md:12-18` and `index.mjs:9-16` defend the wording — "the privacy policy states … that no analytics or tracking scripts exist anywhere on the site, and that remains true as written" — and the narrow reading is correct (there is no beacon, cookie, or script, and no identifier is stored). But the bullet sits under a heading about *collection*, not about scripts, and a reader parses it as "no analytics are collected here." Two related strains: the collection is server-side analytics that no locale discloses, and `retentionLogs` (en.ts:947-948; es.ts:875-876) scopes operational logs to "debugging and abuse prevention" and promises 30-day CloudWatch deletion, while these are Amplify/CloudFront access logs read for a third purpose and distilled into DynamoDB rows that outlive them (`lambda/analytics/template.yaml:64` deliberately declares no TTL).

**Correction.** Three parts of the finding are wrong or overstated. (1) The title's "contradicted" overstates: the English sentence is literally true and stays true — nothing is added to the browser (no script, cookie, beacon), no identifier is written, and `lambda/analytics/index.test.mjs:85-86` asserts every written attribute is in an allowlist, so identifiers cannot creep in. The defect is a scope mismatch between the sentence and its heading, not a false statement of fact. (2) The two locales are not equally exposed, and the finder treats them as one. English "No analytics or tracking scripts" can be read as "no analytics-scripts or tracking-scripts", which is the reading the README defends. Spanish `es.ts:862` is "Sin analítica ni scripts de seguimiento" — *analítica* is a separate noun from *scripts*, so the script-only defence does not exist in Spanish. es is the weaker half and the one to fix first. (3) The retention strain is overreach as argued. The DynamoDB rows are aggregate counts with no identifier (verified by scan: no IP, user-agent or path attribute on any row), so nothing about a person outlives the logs, and the function's own CloudWatch logs ARE at 30 days (`template.yaml:34-36`, `109-113`), matching `retentionLogs`. What is genuinely undisclosed is narrower: that Amplify/CloudFront access logs exist at all and are read for visitor counting, a purpose outside the stated "debugging and abuse prevention".

**Impact.** This is a published privacy commitment on an indexed public page in two languages, and it is the one claim in the policy a reader is most likely to rely on. The defence rests on a distinction (script vs. server-side aggregation) the sentence does not draw. Fixing it is a copy change, not an architecture change — the implementation is genuinely privacy-preserving; the disclosure is what lags. Live, not dormant.

**Evidence.** en.ts:933-935 `whatWeDont: "What we don't collect"`, `noAnalytics: "No analytics or tracking scripts — none exist anywhere on this site."`; es.ts:861-863 same. en.ts:947-948 `retentionLogs` ("Operational service logs (used for debugging and abuse prevention) … 30 days"). lambda/analytics/index.mjs:81-95 writes `{day, humans, requests, malformed, buckets, googleSignIns, computedAt}`; template.yaml:64 "DELIBERATELY NO TimeToLiveSpecification". Live: `aws lambda list-functions` shows quantum-analytics (2026-08-20); scanning quantum-analytics-daily returns populated rows.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: confirmed · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, medium, observed live). I tried to refute this on the README's own defence and could not.

COPY — every cited line is exact. `grep -n "noAnalytics\|whatWeDont\|retentionLogs" web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts web/src/i18n/locales/es.ts` → en.ts:933 `whatWeDont: "What we don't collect"`, 934-935 `noAnalytics`, 947 `retentionLogs`; es.ts:861/862/875. Decisive: `grep -rn "analytics\|visitor\|access log" web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts` returns EXACTLY ONE hit — line 935, the denial. No locale discloses server-side visitor counting anywhere, so the "already disclosed as operational service logs" defence rests entirely on retentionLogs, which scopes them to "debugging and abuse prevention" — not audience measurement, which the README states is the actual motive ("Answering 'how many users do we have?'").

PUBLISHED AND INDEXED — `curl -s https://quantum.altivum.ai/privacy` → 200, renders "No analytics or tracking scripts — none exist anywhere on this site." and the retentionLogs sentence verbatim. `curl -s .../robots.txt` → `Allow: /`; `curl -s .../sitemap.xml | grep privacy` → `/privacy` listed. Spanish is a client-side locale switch (`/es/privacy` is 404), but the string ships live: I fetched every chunk on the page and found "Sin analítica ni scripts de seguimiento — no existen en ningún lugar de este sitio." in `/_next/static/chunks/0xsq7_lswd-lp.js`. Two languages confirmed.

LIVE AND RUNNING, not merely deployed — `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-analytics --region us-east-2` → State `Active`, LastModified 2026-08-20T17:17:57Z. `aws dynamodb scan --table-name quantum-analytics-daily --region us-east-2` → 8 rows; newest `day: 2026-08-26`, `computedAt: 2026-08-27T13:30:40.490Z` — it fired on the cron THIS MORNING, hours before this audit. Real classification: `uniqueIps: 212`, `humans: 3`, buckets `declared-bot: 97`, `no-assets: 81`, `scanner: 15`, `datacenter: 7`, `high-rate: 5`, `no-page-view: 4`. `aws dynamodb describe-time-to-live --table-name quantum-analytics-daily` → `DISABLED`, corroborating template.yaml:64's deliberate no-TTL: derived rows are permanent while the source logs age out, which is the finder's retention strain.

TWO NITS, both of which UNDERSTATE rather than overstate: the finder's attribute list omits `uniqueIps`, `humanPageViews` and `botFilterComplete` (uniqueIps matters — it is derived from addresses in the access logs), and the bucket list omits `no-page-view`. SEVERITY medium, agreeing with the finder. Against higher: zero actual privacy harm — no identifier, cookie, beacon or third party; the implementation is genuinely privacy-preserving and the sentence is defensible in a dispute. Against lower: this is live today, public, indexed, in two languages, and is a privacy commitment — the claim a reader is most likely to rely on. Fix is copy, not architecture.

CLAUDE.md rules 5 and 9 make a shared markup over true cost load-bearing, and the mechanism landed 2026-08-17: both kernels REQUIRE the injected `RATE_CARD` factor and throw rather than fall back to raw cost, because raw cost is itself a divergent rate. **Correction.** The causal half of the title — "which the deployed rate-card mechanism is built to refuse" — and the sentence "There is no configuration in which the deployed system charges at cost" are both wrong. The copy conflicts with the settled monetization rules and with the sheet the site already publishes — not with a mechanical impossibility.

CLAUDE.md rule 13 states "The pricing page is test-guarded on rendered text in both locales," and the pricing suite does scan en and es — but a string that never enters the i18n dictionaries has no Spanish twin to scan and no `i18n.test.ts` parity check to fail on.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. App-wide, 55 of 147 `.tsx` files under `src/components` + `src/app` call `useLocale`, so partial localization is the pre-existing condition, not something done to the money copy in particular. Dormant — every submit is refused today — but this is the surface that will carry the quote-versus-debit copy the cutover depends on.

Only the sentences some branch actually renders live here: the rest of qpu-submit-panel.tsx is still English prose (see the panel's own note), and adding keys nothing reads would be dead dictionary." ### The top-up card's checkout-failure message is hardcoded English while its Spanish translation exists and the sibling button uses it

**Impact.** A Spanish learner whose top-up checkout fails gets an English error on an otherwise fully translated page, at the moment they are trying to give the product money. The translation is already written and paid for; only the call site is wrong. Dormant while the storefront is closed (rule 15), and a one-line fix.

**Evidence.** web/src/components/pricing/top-up.tsx:48 `setError("Could not start checkout. Please try again.");` vs web/src/components/pricing/checkout-button.tsx:64 `{t("pricingUi.checkoutFailed")}`; keys at web/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:873 and es.ts:810.

Source (`cat -n web/src/components/pricing/top-up.tsx`): line 48 is exactly `setError("Could not start checkout. Please try again.");` — a raw English literal in the catch of `go()`. - `web/src/i18n/locales/es.ts:810: checkoutFailed: "No se pudo iniciar el checkout. Inténtalo de nuevo."`

I then deleted the temp file; `git status --porcelain` is byte-for-byte identical to the session's starting snapshot. No tracked file was touched and nothing live was contacted.

### Three copy-honesty guard rationales are disproved by the code they cite, on the one page whose guard is the project's model for honest copy

`web/__tests__/app/pricing-page.test.tsx:347-350` — `f3a2b5d51` · low · confirmed · docs-drift · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `f82984d24` · fix plan 03

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD, and further from the code than when it was raised. (1) :347-348 justifies the model-unlock ban with "lambda/tutor/index.mjs binds one process.env.TUTOR_MODEL_ID; ask-tutor.tsx posts only {slug, question}. No model parameter, no tier lookup, no per-tier routing." Every clause is false: `TUTOR_MODEL_ID` no longer exists (`handler-wiring.test.mjs:83` asserts its absence as "a Bedrock-era leftover"), `ask-tutor.tsx:259-260` posts `{slug, question, model, meta}` on the metered branch, `:114` reads `TUTOR_ROSTER[wallet.tier]`, and `index.mjs:293-294` routes per tier through `ROSTER`/`MODEL_IDS`. (2) :380-382 says "ask-tutor.tsx (473 lines) renders no cost, credit, price, or wallet value anywhere" — the file is 560 lines and `:467-472` renders `t("tutor.costCredits", { credits: cost.credits })` from the server's cost trailer. (3) The `presentTenseMetering` note at :283-286 asserts "no code path outside lambda/stripe touches the wallet," which the tutor's wallet-reserve path and `qpu-core.mjs`'s wallet funding leg contradict once configured.

**Correction.** "Every clause is false" (sub-claim 1) overstates by one clause. "ask-tutor.tsx posts only {slug, question}" is still true of every request the SHIPPED app can make: `grep -rn "AskTutor" web/src --include="*.tsx"` shows exactly one mount, web/src/app/layout.tsx:111, rendering `<AskTutor />` with no props — so `wallet` is undefined, `models` is null (ask-tutor.tsx:114), `metered = Boolean(models && authToken)` is false (:258), and the ternary at :260 always takes the legacy `{slug, question}` branch. The model picker and the cost line at :466-473 are unreachable dead code in production, which also means the `why` strings the finding targets ("the tutor takes no model parameter and no tier is consulted", "renders no cost, credit, or price") remain accurate descriptions of deployed behavior even though the mechanism comments describing the source are stale. Sub-claim 3 is correctly hedged by the finder ("once configured") and is therefore stale-as-source-description only, not a present falsehood. Two minor citation slips: the cost block spans :466-473 (not :467-472), and the file's stated doctrine is "check it against what the deployed Lambdas actually do" (:258-260) — a deployment standard, by which these rationales' conclusions still hold.

**Impact.** The patterns themselves are still the right thing to ban (nothing is metered in production, so the copy would still be false). The damage is to the guard's usefulness: its own doctrine is that a ban whose rationale has expired should be re-examined rather than kept on faith, and a reviewer who checks these rationales against the code will find them wrong and lose confidence in the file that is the project's reference implementation of copy honesty.

### The cutover runbook's Phase 4 acceptance gate names 50.3 credits, a figure neither the client quote nor the server debit can produce

`docs/billing-cutover-runbook.md:378` — `fe6cac801` · low · partly true · correctness · ran locally · re-raised from `f07ed1963` · fix plan 11

**Claim.** Still true at HEAD. Step 3 of Phase 4 reads: "submit 100 shots on IQM Garnet. The pre-flight quote and the wallet debit must be the **same number** (50.3 credits)." 50.3 is the *published sheet* figure — `HARDWARE_RATES` IQM Garnet `creditsPerShot: 0.163` (pricing.ts:86) × 100 + `TASK_FEE_CREDITS = 34` (pricing.ts:60) = 50.3. What the client actually quotes is `creditsForMicros(costMicros(100))` = `ceil((300_000 + 1_450×100)/10_000)` = **45** whole credits (`qpu-budget.ts:23-34`), and the server mirrors that arithmetic. Credits are also integers on both sides, so a fractional acceptance value can never be produced by either. This is a concrete instance of the reconciliation CLAUDE.md flags as unresolved — the published sheet and a single scalar factor do not stand in one common ratio.

**Correction.** The finding's claim that "the server mirrors that arithmetic" is wrong at HEAD, and it understates the problem. `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:97-100` defines `creditsForMicros(micros, factor)` — it REQUIRES the injected rate factor, throws `"qpu-core: rate factor missing or invalid; metered pricing refused"` without one, and multiplies BEFORE the ceil. The client's `web/src/lib/qpu-budget.ts:34` version takes one argument and applies no factor. So post-cutover — the only moment Phase 4 step 3 ever runs — the operator does not see "45 on both sides"; they see a three-way divergence: client quote 45 (unfactored), server debit `ceil(445000 x factor / 10000)` which equals 45 only at factor 1 (raw cost, which the code and CLAUDE.md rule 5 both refuse), and a gate reading 50.3. That is the same client-quote-understates-the-debit hazard CLAUDE.md already records as blocking the cutover, so the step is more broken than the finding says, not less.

**Correction.** Two parts of the finder's reasoning are wrong, and both understate rather than overstate. (1) "the server mirrors that arithmetic" is false at HEAD — `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:97` takes a REQUIRED `factor` (the deployed RATE_CARD, added in dd7abb7, `git log -S "creditsForMicros(micros, factor)"`), throws rather than defaulting to 1, and multiplies before the ceil. Only the client is factor-free. (2) The impact's "An operator running it sees 45 on both sides" therefore does not describe the post-cutover run this step is for: the operator sees 45 from the client pre-flight and a larger integer from the factored server debit, so the step's real pass condition ("the same number") fails on its own terms — which is the separate, already-recorded open item in CLAUDE.md ("the confirm screen would understate the debit"). The unreachable 50.3 parenthetical is a second, independent wrongness layered on top of that, not the only reason the step fails.

**Impact.** The step is the runbook's own designated proof that quote and debit agree. An operator running it sees 45 on both sides, reads 50.3 in the gate, and concludes the change failed — or, worse, edits a number to make it match. Dormant until cutover, but the whole point of the step is that it is the thing you do not skip.

Checked for a refuting guard and found none: tests/test_pricing_prose.py:30-33 scopes its corpus to 0*-*/GUIDE.md, notebooks, README.md and CLAUDE.md, with the comment "(PRODUCT.md / docs/ are internal design docs.)" — docs/ is deliberately outside every prose guard, so nothing in CI can ever catch this line. That is why it survived.

Severity: low, and I agree with the finder. It is an internal engineering note (not learner-facing copy, so no rule 13 surface), no rule 6 disclosure, on a path deliberately switched off (live tutor free and unmetered). The one real risk — someone re-implementing caching — is blocked by the in-code comment and test at the edit site. Fix is a three-line doc edit: state that caching shipped 2026-08-17, rename MAX_TOKENS -> MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (per-model), and replace `cachePoint` with `cache_control`.

### Rule 8's "a test asserts it" is false — the CATALOG guard hardcodes a third copy of the credit figures instead of reading pricing.ts

`lambda/stripe/index.test.mjs:122-128` — `f53966a4e` · low · confirmed · test-coverage · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 08

**Claim.** CLAUDE.md rule 8 says `TIERS` in `web/src/lib/pricing.ts` and `CATALOG` in `lambda/stripe/index.mjs` "must stay in lockstep — a test asserts it," and "Do not restate the numbers anywhere else." No such test exists. The only candidate, `lambda/stripe/index.test.mjs:122-128` ("CATALOG credit counts mirror the published pricing"), asserts `CATALOG.ql_plus_monthly.credits === 1900`, `ql_pro_monthly === 6500`, `ql_credits_500 === 500`, `ql_credits_10000 === 10000` — literals typed into the test, never read from `pricing.ts`. Nothing under `web/__tests__` imports or reads `CATALOG` at all (`grep -rln CATALOG` over every test file returns only `lambda/stripe/index.test.mjs`). The values happen to agree today (`pricing.ts:261` `monthlyCredits: 1900`, `:277` `6500`), so the divergence is latent, not present. The test is also itself the "restate the numbers anywhere else" that rule 8 forbids — a third hand-copy of the grant figures.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. ### CLAUDE.md contradicts itself about which Stripe account is the sandbox, and the sandbox-provisioning script documents the wrong one

`CLAUDE.md:55-56` — `f368cca95` · low · confirmed · docs-drift · observed live · fix plan 08

**Claim.** CLAUDE.md:55-57 states: "Sandbox is **`$STRIPE_SANDBOX`** (\"Quantum Learner Sandbox\"…). An older `$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD` is recorded in some places and is NOT the one that is provisioned." Twenty-five lines later, CLAUDE.md:82 says "**Anything Stripe gets exercised in the sandbox (`$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD`) before it is believed about live.**" — naming the account the file has just disowned. The same wrong id is the documented `--expect-account` value in `scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs:40`, the script that *writes* products, prices and a webhook endpoint; the sibling `scripts/stripe/e2e-sandbox.mjs:16` uses the correct `$STRIPE_SANDBOX`.

**Impact.** CLAUDE.md is the file an agent or engineer reads to avoid exactly this mistake — the section exists because the owner's login controls three Stripe accounts and writing to the wrong one is silent. The `--expect-account` guard means following the documented command fails safe rather than provisioning the wrong account, so no money or data is at risk; the cost is a confidently-wrong instruction sitting inside the warning that was written to prevent it, in a repo whose own doctrine is that a written-down account id is never evidence.

**Evidence.** CLAUDE.md:55-57 vs CLAUDE.md:82. scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs:40 `--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD` vs scripts/stripe/e2e-sandbox.mjs:16 `--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX`.

**Severity drift.** Finder claimed medium; verification published low.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, observed live). Reproduces exactly as written, and I settled which id is right by asking Stripe.

LIVE CHECK (read-only GET, key never printed):
  K=$(op read "op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key") && curl -s https://api.stripe.com/v1/account -u "$K:" | jq -r '"\(.id) | \(.settings.dashboard.display_name)"'
  -> $STRIPE_SANDBOX  |  Quantum Learner Sandbox

So CLAUDE.md:55 is correct and CLAUDE.md:82 is wrong, not the other way round.

The contradiction (verified by `grep -rn "$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD\|$STRIPE_SANDBOX" .`):
- CLAUDE.md:55-58 — sandbox is $STRIPE_SANDBOX; "An older $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD ... is NOT the one that is provisioned"
- CLAUDE.md:82 — "exercised in the sandbox ($STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD)"
- /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs:40 — documented `--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD`
- /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/scripts/stripe/e2e-sandbox.mjs:16 — `--expect-account $STRIPE_SANDBOX` (correct)

`git blame` + `git show ac25c22 -- CLAUDE.md` shows why: one commit (ac25c22, 2026-08-17) both made the correction and left the stale id behind. Its diff is literally `-Sandbox is $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD.` / `+Sandbox is $STRIPE_SANDBOX ...`, while the prose ADDED in the same commit at what is now line 82 still names the old id. The commit message itself says "THE SANDBOX. $STRIPE_SANDBOX mirrors live's structure" — so the author's own intent is unambiguous. This is an incomplete find-and-replace, not a disputed fact.

Fail-safe confirmed by reading the guard: provision-sandbox.mjs:65 requires --expect-account, and 101-105 compares it to the authenticated account and dies "Refusing to write." Following the documented line with the documented key aborts rather than provisioning the wrong account, so nothing is at risk — the cost is a wasted cycle and a confidently-wrong instruction inside the warning written to prevent exactly this.

ONE ADDITION the finder missed (additive, not a correction): the same stale id appears a fourth time in /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/Makefile:48, the documented `make stripe-parity` sandbox invocation. Those two parity scripts are read-only and carry the same --expect-account guard, so it also fails safe.

SEVERITY: I judge low, not medium. The claim is fully accurate, but every path that consumes the wrong id refuses to act on it, and the refusal message names the real account — so the error self-corrects at the point of use. It is a clean four-line fix (CLAUDE.md:82, provision-sandbox.mjs:40, Makefile:48 -> $STRIPE_SANDBOX).

**Verification — correct as written** (confirmed, low, observed live). Every factual assertion in the finding checks out, and I could not refute it.

VERIFIED TEXT. `grep -rn` for all four account ids confirms CLAUDE.md:55-57 names the sandbox as $STRIPE_SANDBOX and explicitly disowns $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD ("is NOT the one that is provisioned"), while CLAUDE.md:82 says "exercised in the sandbox (`$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD`)". scripts/stripe/provision-sandbox.mjs:40 documents the stale id; scripts/stripe/e2e-sandbox.mjs:16 uses the correct one.

WHICH ID IS AUTHORITATIVE — three ways.
(1) Live, read-only. Command run:
  KEY=$(op read "op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key"); curl -s https://api.stripe.com/v1/account -u "$KEY:" | jq -r '"\(.id)  \(.settings.dashboard.display_name)"'
  -> "$STRIPE_SANDBOX  Quantum Learner Sandbox". The key the repo itself points at resolves to the id at line 55, not line 82. (Guarded against a live key first; GET only, no mutation.)
(2) Git history. `git log --oneline -L 52,60:CLAUDE.md` shows 6c8ab06 (#205) wrote "Sandbox is $STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD", then ac25c22 (#234) corrected it to $STRIPE_SANDBOX. `git log --oneline -L 80,84:CLAUDE.md` shows the SAME commit ac25c22 introduced the contradicting line 82 — the correction and the regression shipped together.
(3) Direction of drift is therefore unambiguous: 1U5IQr is the correction, 1TuFpH is the residue.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED. The --expect-account guard is genuine and enforced before any write (provision-sandbox.mjs:59/65/101-105; same pattern at check-catalog-parity.mjs:88 and check-webhook-parity.mjs:71), and the script also refuses any sk_live_/rk_live_ key (line 66). So following the stale documented command produces a refusal, never a wrong-account write — exactly as the finder conceded. The guard does not rescue the docs, though: it converts wrong instructions into a failed run.

SCOPE THE FINDER UNDERCOUNTED (not an error, an omission): a THIRD stale site at Makefile:48 — `make stripe-parity ACCOUNT=$STRIPE_SANDBOX_OLD KEYREF="op://Quantum Learner/Stripe Sandbox/Secret Key"` — pairs the correct sandbox keyref with the wrong account, so that documented invocation can never succeed. Full stale set: CLAUDE.md:82, provision-sandbox.mjs:40, Makefile:48. Correct set: CLAUDE.md:55, e2e-sandbox.mjs:16.

SEVERITY: medium -> LOW. All three stale sites are prose, a JSDoc usage example, or a Makefile comment; none is executable configuration or a hardcoded constant. The guard fails safe AND its refusal message prints the actually-authenticated account id (line 105), so the mistake self-corrects on first run and points the reader at the right answer. No money, data, or wrong-account write is reachable. Real cost is a few wasted minutes plus a self-contradicting warning section — worth fixing, not worth medium.

## Curriculum, the Python library and the build

Surviving: 1 high, 4 medium, 11 low.

### How it actually works

The curriculum is 45 notebooks under seven numbered section directories, each with `GUIDE.md` + `GUIDE.es.md` (both rendered by `web/src/lib/content.ts:31` at `/learn/<slug>`), a `scripts/` dir that is mostly thin re-exports of `lib/` (e.g. `04-quantum-ml/scripts/feature_maps.py` is 7 lines of `from lib.ml.feature_maps import ...`), and — for 03/05 — two real implementations, `oracles.py` and `vqe_runner.py`.

`lib/` is the shared Python library: `circuits/common.py`, `utils/{cost,results,statevector,visualization}.py`, `ml/{feature_maps,classifiers,training}.py`, `chemistry/{ansatz,hamiltonians}.py`, `hardware/devices.py`, and `grading.py`. `lib/hardware/devices.py:70-114` is the single source of truth for every billable device (ARN + `lib/utils/cost.py` `PRICING` provider key + `gate_capable`/`allowlist`/shot bounds); `run_circuit` gates on all of it before constructing an `AwsDevice`, so no billable submit happens without a printed cost estimate. `lib/grading.py` is the browser-safe `with check("Exercise N"):` context manager — stdlib only, prints for the learner, re-raises under `QL_GRADING_STRICT=1`.

`qcsim/` is a 908-line pure-NumPy stand-in that registers itself as `braket`, `braket.circuits`, `braket.devices` in `sys.modules` *only if* real Braket is not already imported (`qcsim/src/qcsim/__init__.py:38-41`). That guard is the source of a whole bug class the repo now defends against explicitly: a test that imports `braket` first silently exercises the real SDK while claiming qcsim.

Three engines execute notebooks. `scripts/validate_runnable.py` AST-scans every `<!-- browser-runnable -->` notebook against a denylist (`DENIED_IMPORT_PREFIXES`, `DENIED_NAMES`, `DENIED_CALL_ATTRS`, and `DIVERGENT_CALL_ATTRS` for `state_vector()`), and writes `web/src/lib/content-manifest.json`, which is the *only* reader of the marker — the portal's Run button reads the manifest. `tests/test_notebook_contract.py` executes all 32 runnable notebooks under a forced qcsim alias; `tests/test_notebook_real_sdk.py` executes a 3-notebook sample under the real SDK; `tests/test_exercise_checks.py` executes every notebook twice — once with `tests/solutions/<section>/<stem>.py` injected under strict grading, once untouched, asserting no check reports success unsolved.

The build is `web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh`: it self-hosts two independently-pinned Pyodide distributions (lesson runtime under `public/pyodide`, lab kernel under `static/pyodide`), computes each one's wheel closure from `pyodide-lock.json`, prunes shadowing `*-tests` siblings, bundles `comm` into the piplite index, sets `disablePyPIFallback`, and asserts every staged `.wasm` stays under CloudFront's 10,000,000-byte compression ceiling. `check_notebook_coverage.py` fails the build if a runnable notebook imports a lock package the closure omits.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs four jobs — python, web, a Lambda matrix, and a build-smoke that greps the *built* `web/out/learn/01-foundations.html` for KaTeX/hljs output. `infra/ci-standby/template.yaml` mirrors it into an inline CodeBuild buildspec. `drift.yml` assumes a read-only OIDC role daily and runs `check-lambda-drift.mjs` + `check-rate-parity.mjs`.

### What is genuinely good here

- 03-algorithms/scripts/oracles.py:43-79 — the multi-controlled-Z is now an exact phase-polynomial decomposition at any n, and the docstring is honest about the 2^n-1 term count. I rebuilt the full unitary for n=2..6 and confirmed max deviation from the ideal (up to the documented global phase) is 1.0e-15 for the oracle and 1.8e-16 for the diffusion operator.
- scripts/validate_runnable.py:174-181 — an unparseable cell is now a contract *violation*, not a warning, and `_MAGIC_LINE_RE` requires an identifier after the sigil so a printf `%` continuation survives. The scanner can no longer be exempted by the cells it cannot read.
- tests/test_guide_runnable_fences.py:127-146 — the fence runner spawns a fresh interpreter, inserts `qcsim/src` directly, and asserts `Circuit.__module__.startswith('qcsim')` *before* executing anything. The guarantee in the docstring is now itself tested rather than assumed.
- qcsim/src/qcsim/devices.py:16-30 and tests/test_qcsim_parity.py:805,844 — qcsim samples from a module-private `np.random.Generator` because real Braket neither honours `np.random.seed` nor advances the global stream, and there are two dedicated parity tests pinning both halves of that. This is a divergence almost nobody would think to look for.
- tests/test_notebook_hygiene.py:62-72 — the output guard reads `git cat-file blob :<path>` (the INDEX), not the working tree, so it asserts "no notebook ENTERS the repo with outputs" instead of crying wolf at anyone who actually ran a lesson in JupyterLab.
- web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh:22-27 — the venv is rebuilt when its interpreter cannot *run*, not merely when the directory is absent. That is the exact failure a restored actions/cache produced (exit 127 reading like a missing package).
- web/jupyterlite-build/check_notebook_coverage.py:115-128 — `find_uncovered` returns the number of notebooks actually scanned, so a discovery regression that empties the scan cannot report a clean result. `tests/test_lab_build_guards.py` exercises it against synthetic locks.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:266-289 — the KaTeX/highlight assertion greps the built static export for `katex-html`, `katex-mathml`, a rendered `⟩` glyph, `hljs-` token spans, and zero `katex-error` spans. Every Jest suite mocks those plugins into no-ops, so this step is the only place the render pipeline is observed at all.
- lib/hardware/devices.py:189-199 — `list_available_devices` applies no status filter and its docstring says so explicitly: "picking a row blind can target a retired machine." The library is more honest about device status than the GUIDE prose that surrounds it.

### Fixed since the 2026-08-18 audit

- **fe61f70c2** (`fe61f70c2`) — FIXED in 0108042 (#242). `03-algorithms/scripts/oracles.py:43-79` now carries `_apply_multi_controlled_z`, which builds C^(n-1)Z exactly at any n as a phase polynomial (one CNOT parity ladder + Rz per non-empty subset), and both `grover_oracle` (:105) and `grover_diffusion` (:136) call it. I verified independently rather than trusting the commit message: I reconstructed the full unitary column by column via `lib.utils.statevector.statevector` for n=2..6 and compared to the ideal. Oracle max deviation (after dividing out the documented global phase): 0.0, 0.0, 3.6e-16, 1.0e-15, 8.9e-16. Diffusion vs 2|s><s|-I: 0.0, 5.6e-17, 1.8e-16, 1.4e-16, 1.8e-16. `tests/test_oracles.py` (137 new lines) pins the unitary phase-insensitively and end-to-end amplification at n=2..5.
