### The hardware lesson promises every free account a sponsored QPU budget on IQM Garnet, in both locales, and it is live in the shipped static export

`02-hardware/GUIDE.md:18-20` — `f3451313b` · high · confirmed · rule-violation · observed live · RESOLVED 2026-08-27 · fix plan 01

**Resolved 2026-08-27.** Merged to main 2026-08-28 in PR #248 (squash commit 2a06bef); live on the next Amplify deploy. The sponsored-budget paragraph is gone from `02-hardware/GUIDE.md` and its Spanish twin. Both now open by stating that hardware runs are not currently available, that everything on the page runs free in the browser against the simulator, and that executing on a real QPU today requires the learner’s own AWS account which Braket bills directly. Covered going forward by the new claim guard in `tests/test_pricing_prose.py`, which scans every GUIDE in both locales and carries Spanish patterns (`patrocin\w*`, `no pagas nada`, `la plataforma paga`) alongside the English ones.

**Claim.** `02-hardware/GUIDE.md:18-20` reads: "You don't need an AWS account to touch a real QPU at all: a free Workspace account comes with a sponsored budget on IQM Garnet, a 20-qubit superconducting device — the platform pays Amazon Braket, you pay nothing." `02-hardware/GUIDE.es.md:18-20` says the same in Spanish ("presupuesto patrocinado en IQM Garnet ... tú no pagas nada"). No such budget exists: `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:47` sets `LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0`, the `effectiveCap > 0` guard at qpu-core.mjs:563 makes a zero cap deny every run, wallet metering is off, and the storefront is closed. CLAUDE.md records the allowance as WITHDRAWN on 2026-07-28 and rule 11 as "No free credits. Ever." The 2026-08-17 copy correction rewrote the *i18n* sponsorship strings and added a ban list — `web/__tests__/app/pricing-page.test.tsx:322` bars `/\b(sponsor\w*|patrocin\w*)\b/i` with the rationale "sponsored hardware: LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS is 0 and no wallet is wired — nobody gets a platform-funded run" — but that guard only reads the pricing page's rendered text and the locale files. It never reads a GUIDE, so the same promise survived on the lesson page the same app renders.

**Impact.** Every visitor to /learn/02-hardware, in English and Spanish, is told they can run on real quantum hardware for free with a free account. They cannot: a new learner's lifetime QPU allowance is 0 and there is no funded path to a hardware run at all. This is the exact rule-13 failure the copy-honesty guard was written for, on a live page, and it is the second surface of the same withdrawn promise — the first was caught and this one was not, because the guard's reach stops at the locale files.

**Evidence.** `grep -o "sponsored budget on IQM Garnet[^\"]*" web/out/learn/02-hardware.html` returns "sponsored budget on IQM Garnet, a 20-qubit superconducting device — the platform pays Amazon\nBraket, you pay " and the Spanish grep returns "presupuesto patrocinado en IQM Garnet..." — both ship in the built static export. `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:47`: `export const LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0;`. `grep -rn -i "sponsor|patrocin" 0*-*/GUIDE*.md` returns exactly these two files and no others.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, high, observed live). Reproduced end to end, on the live site and against the deployed backend.

1) Source, at the cited lines. `grep -n -iE "sponsor|patrocin" /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/0*-*/GUIDE*.md` returns exactly two hits, both line 19: `02-hardware/GUIDE.md` ("a free Workspace account comes with a sponsored budget on IQM Garnet, a 20-qubit superconducting device — the platform pays Amazon Braket, you pay nothing") and `02-hardware/GUIDE.es.md` ("una cuenta gratuita de Workspace incluye un presupuesto patrocinado en IQM Garnet ... tú no pagas nada"). Both files are clean in git (`git status --porcelain`), so this is committed main, not a local edit. `git log -S"sponsored budget on IQM Garnet"` dates it to 2a51fea (2026-07-14), before the withdrawal.

2) It renders. `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/web/src/components/lesson-body.tsx:33` — `const markdown = locale === "es" ? markdownEs : markdownEn;` — feeds both GUIDEs straight into `<MarkdownRenderer />`, so both locales ship in one page payload.

3) It is LIVE, not just built. `curl -sL https://quantumlearner.dev/learn/02-hardware` redirects to `https://quantum.altivum.ai/learn/02-hardware` (200, 84 KB) and greps positive for BOTH strings: "sponsored budget on IQM Garnet, a 20-qubit superconducting device — the platform pays Amazon\nBraket, you pay nothing." and "presupuesto patrocinado en IQM Garnet, un dispositivo superconductor de 20 cúbits — la plataforma le\npaga a Amazon Braket, tú...". The finder's `web/out` evidence is a gitignored local build; the production fetch is the stronger proof and it agrees.

4) The promise is false against the DEPLOYED Lambda, not merely against main. `aws lambda get-function --function-name quantum-qpu-submit --region us-east-2` (downloaded the package to scratchpad, unzipped): the shipped `qpu-core.mjs` carries `export const LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0;` at line 47 and `const fitsAllowance = effectiveCap > 0 && alreadySpent + cost <= effectiveCap;` at line 563 — the exact cited lines. `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-qpu-submit --region us-east-2` shows env of only LEDGER_TABLE / TASKS_TABLE / RESULTS_BUCKET / EDGE_SECRET — no wallet table. So `walletTable` is undefined and `!fitsAllowance && !walletTable` returns `402 over-lifetime-budget` for every learner without a grandfathered stamped `capMicros`. LastModified 2026-08-18, i.e. post-withdrawal; PRODUCT.md:178's "the live QPU function predates the sponsorship withdrawal ... in production the platform still pays" is itself stale, and correcting it does not rescue the GUIDE copy — it makes the copy false in production too.

5) The guard's reach is exactly as claimed. `web/__tests__/app/pricing-page.test.tsx:322` bans `/\b(sponsor\w*|patrocin\w*)\b/i`, but `assertNoUndeliverableClaims` (line 472) is only ever fed `container.textContent` from `renderPricingIn(locale)` and the `metadata` export. `grep -rn "sponsor\|patrocin" web/__tests__ tests scripts` finds guards on the pricing page, the privacy page (privacy-page.test.tsx:51) and the changelog ban list (_support/changelog-ban-list.ts:54-55) — nothing reads a GUIDE. The GUIDE-touching tests (`content/guide-reps`, `content/reps-corpus`, `content/tutor-corpus`) check rep/fence structure, not copy honesty.

Two immaterial corrections to the write-up: the 2026-07-28 withdrawal date is recorded in PRODUCT.md:146, not CLAUDE.md (CLAUDE.md:233 references the withdrawal without the date); and the guard reads the locale strings indirectly, via the rendered pricing tree plus the metadata export, rather than reading the locale files directly. Neither changes the defect.

Severity high, and deliberately not discounted as a dormant path: the copy itself is the live surface. Every visitor to /learn/02-hardware in either language is told a free account funds a real QPU run, and the deployed function refuses that run with a 402. This is the rule-13 failure the copy-honesty guard was written for, on its second surface.

**Verification — correct as written** (confirmed, high, observed live). Verified end to end, and stronger than the finder claimed: this is live in production, not merely in a local build artifact.

TEXT AND PIPELINE. `sed -n '17,20p' 02-hardware/GUIDE.md` and the .es.md twin return the quoted sentences verbatim at lines 18-20 of each. `git show HEAD:02-hardware/GUIDE.md` returns the same, so it is committed, not a working-tree edit. The delivery path is real: web/src/lib/content.ts:29-38 (`readGuide`) reads GUIDE.md / GUIDE.es.md from REPO_ROOT at build time, and web/src/app/learn/[section]/page.tsx:69-72 passes BOTH `markdownEn` and `markdownEs` into <LessonBody>, so both locales ship in the same static page payload. (`web/out/` is gitignored per web/.gitignore:24 — irrelevant, since Amplify rebuilds from the same HEAD sources.)

LIVE. `curl -sL --max-time 30 https://quantumlearner.dev/learn/02-hardware` -> HTTP 200, final URL https://quantum.altivum.ai/learn/02-hardware, 84,296 bytes. `grep -c "sponsored budget on IQM Garnet"` = 1 and `grep -c "presupuesto patrocinado en IQM Garnet"` = 1 in the served HTML. Both sentences are being served to the public right now.

FALSITY. lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:47 `export const LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0;` and :563 `const fitsAllowance = effectiveCap > 0 && alreadySpent + cost <= effectiveCap;` (effectiveCap defaults to the constant at :392 when the row carries no capMicros). The comment block at :37-46 states outright "WITHDRAWN 2026-07-28. The platform no longer sponsors hardware runs", with exactly one grandfathered production row. A new free Workspace account gets cap 0, so `fitsAllowance` is false and every hardware submit is refused. The sentence is flatly false for its stated audience.

GUARD GAP CONFIRMED. `grep -rn -i "sponsor|patrocin" web/__tests__` puts every ban list on surfaces that never read a GUIDE: pricing-page.test.tsx:322, privacy-page.test.tsx:51, _support/changelog-ban-list.ts:54-55. Neither prior audit found it — `grep -n "sponsored budget on IQM" docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-16.md docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-18.md` returns nothing. The sweep did reach README.md (grep for sponsor over 0*-*/GUIDE*.md, README.md, docs/*.md leaves only these two curriculum files plus internal audit/runbook prose), which is what makes this the surviving surface.

REFUTATION ANGLES I TESTED AND REJECTED. (a) AuthWall — web/src/app/layout.tsx:108 wraps children, and auth-wall.tsx:73-98 redirects signed-out visitors to /login?mode=signup. But the payload still serves unauthenticated (my curl was signed-out and returned both strings), and the audience the sentence names, free-account holders, is exactly who reads the rendered page. Impact essentially undiminished. (b) An existing guard — tests/test_pricing_prose.py:30 DOES glob `0*-*/GUIDE.md`, so a prose guard already walks this exact file; it only validates dollar figures against lib.utils.cost.PRICING, never claims, so it cannot catch this (and it skips .es.md entirely). (c) Dormant-path discount does not apply: the QPU code path being off is the reason the copy is false; the copy itself is rendered, not dormant.

TWO PERIPHERAL CITATION NITS worth fixing before publishing, neither affecting the defect: (1) the finder attributes "WITHDRAWN on 2026-07-28" to CLAUDE.md — `grep -n "2026-07-28" CLAUDE.md` returns nothing. That date lives in lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:37, lambda/qpu/README.md:10 and __fixtures__/hardware-ladder.json; CLAUDE.md carries rule 11 and the 2026-08-17 copy correction. (The repo is itself inconsistent — changelog-ban-list.ts:54 dates the withdrawal 2026-08-17.) (2) "Every visitor to /learn/02-hardware" is more precisely every signed-in learner, plus anyone reading the raw payload.

SEVERITY: high, agreeing with the finder. A false promise of platform-funded compute, live in production in two locales, is the exact rule-13 failure the copy-honesty guard was written for, and it is the second surface of a promise already withdrawn once.

### The read-only drift role's account-wide lambda:ListFunctions returns every function's environment variables in plaintext, and the comment beside it says it does not

`infra/github-oidc-drift-role.yaml:64-68` — `f39750658` · medium · confirmed · security · observed live · SPLIT VERDICT · re-raised from `fb854583f` · fix plan 04

**Claim.** The policy grants `lambda:ListFunctions` on `Resource: "*"` with the comment "ListFunctions cannot be resource-scoped; it is read-only and returns metadata only (no code, no environment secrets)." That is factually wrong. I ran `aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-2 --max-items 3` and the very first result (`RegainCoaching`, an unrelated Altivum production function) came back with a full `Environment.Variables` block: table names, a Cognito `USER_POOL_ID`, an S3 bucket, gateway endpoints. `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` (scoped to `quantum-*`) does the same for this project's functions. So the `${FunctionNamePrefix}-*` scoping on the GetFunction statement is defeated by the unscoped ListFunctions beside it, and "no environment secrets" is not true of either action. Separately, `.github/workflows/drift.yml:36,56,62` pins `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4` and `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` by mutable major tag in the one workflow that holds `id-token: write`.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong, and the impact is understated rather than inflated.

(1) "The ${FunctionNamePrefix}-* scoping on the GetFunction statement is defeated by the unscoped ListFunctions" is only half right. ListFunctions returns FunctionConfiguration objects with no `Code` field at all — verified, top-level keys are [Architectures, CodeSha256, CodeSize, Description, Environment, EphemeralStorage, FunctionArn, FunctionName, Handler, LastModified, Layers, LoggingConfig, MemorySize, PackageType, RevisionId, Role, Runtime, SnapStart, Timeout, TracingConfig, Version, VpcConfig]. There is no `Code.Location` presigned URL, so the deployment-package half of the prefix scoping still holds; an attacker cannot download the code of non-quantum functions. Only the *configuration* half is defeated. The comment's "no code" clause is true; its "no environment secrets" clause is false.

(2) Naming lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration as part of the same problem ("does the same for this project's functions") is wrong. That statement is correctly scoped to quantum-* AND is required: scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:36-51 calls `aws lambda get-function-configuration --query Environment.Variables.RATE_CARD` on quantum-tutor and quantum-qpu-submit. Reading quantum-* env vars is the job, not the leak. Deleting it would break the rate-parity guard. Only the ListFunctions statement is the over-grant, and it is pure dead weight — nothing in the repo calls it.

(3) Severity direction: the finder's impact ("least-privilege and blast-radius problem rather than an open door") understates it. Their own sample cites benign config, but the same call also returns another business's live credential material.

**Impact.** Any workflow that can run on `refs/heads/main` in this repo — or any compromised release of the three tag-pinned actions it uses — can enumerate the plaintext environment configuration of every Lambda in account $PROD_ACCOUNT, including functions belonging to other Altivum products. The trust policy's `sub` condition is correctly tight, so this is a least-privilege and blast-radius problem rather than an open door, but the comment actively tells a reader not to worry about it.

**Evidence.** `aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-2 --max-items 3` returns, for the first function, `"Environment": {"Variables": {"USER_POOL_ID": "us-east-2_xwY7t5DSq", "RESUME_BUCKET_NAME": "regain-resume-$PROD_ACCOUNT", ...}}`. `infra/github-oidc-drift-role.yaml:64-68` grants `lambda:ListFunctions` on `"*"` under the quoted comment.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: confirmed · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, medium, observed live). I tried to refute this and could not — every element reproduces, and the finding is if anything understated.

1) The policy text is as quoted. `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/infra/github-oidc-drift-role.yaml:64-68` grants `Action: lambda:ListFunctions` / `Resource: "*"` under the comment "ListFunctions cannot be resource-scoped; it is read-only and returns metadata only (no code, no environment secrets)."

2) The role is DEPLOYED and LIVE, not just a template. `aws iam get-role-policy --role-name quantum-ci-drift-check --policy-name read-lambda-code-only` returns the template's two statements verbatim, including `{"Action":"lambda:ListFunctions","Resource":"*","Effect":"Allow"}`. `aws iam get-role --role-name quantum-ci-drift-check` shows `RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate: 2026-08-26T13:54:30+00:00` in us-east-2 — the daily job assumed it yesterday, so it is not skipping for a missing `AWS_DRIFT_ROLE_ARN`.

3) The comment is false. `aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-2 --max-items 3` reproduced the finder's result exactly: the first function is `RegainCoaching` and it carries a full `Environment.Variables` block including `"USER_POOL_ID": "us-east-2_xwY7t5DSq"` and `"RESUME_BUCKET_NAME": "regain-resume-$PROD_ACCOUNT"`. `FunctionConfiguration` in the ListFunctions response includes `Environment`; IAM authorizes the call and does not filter response fields, so the drift role sees the same payload my admin creds did.

4) The blast radius is LARGER than the finder wrote, and I only ever read key NAMES, never values. `aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-2 --query "length(Functions[?Environment!=null && !starts_with(FunctionName,'quantum')])"` summed to 188 env-carrying functions belonging to other products. `... --query "Functions[?Environment!=null && !starts_with(FunctionName,'quantum')].{fn:FunctionName,k:keys(Environment.Variables)}"` surfaces key names `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `IBM_API_KEY`, `USAJOBS_API_KEY`. The finder framed the leak as "environment configuration — table names, a user pool, a bucket"; it is in fact live third-party credentials of unrelated Altivum businesses, whose plaintext values ListFunctions returns.

5) The `GetFunctionConfiguration` half is confirmed too: `aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name quantum-qpu-submit --region us-east-2 --query "keys(Environment.Variables)"` -> `LEDGER_TABLE EDGE_SECRET TASKS_TABLE RESULTS_BUCKET`, and `aws lambda get-function ... --query "keys(Configuration.Environment.Variables)"` returns the same. So "no environment secrets" is untrue of both actions.

6) The workflow pins are exactly where claimed. `grep -n "actions/checkout\|setup-node\|configure-aws-credentials" /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/.github/workflows/drift.yml` -> `36: actions/checkout@v4`, `56: actions/setup-node@v4`, `62: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4`, in the one workflow holding `id-token: write` (line 24).

ONE THING THE FINDER MISSED, which makes the fix free: nothing calls ListFunctions. `grep -rn "list-functions\|ListFunctions" . --include="*.mjs" --include="*.js" --include="*.py" --include="*.yml" --include="*.yaml" --include="Makefile"` (excluding node_modules/.git) hits only the YAML comment itself and a prior audit doc. `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs:40-55` iterates a hardcoded `FUNCTIONS` list and shells out to `lambda get-function` (line 76) and `lambda get-function-configuration` (line 92); `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:33-51` calls only `get-function-configuration` on a hardcoded `["quantum-tutor","quantum-qpu-submit"]`. The wildcard statement is dead permission and can be deleted with zero functional cost.

Counterweight on severity, which is why I hold medium rather than high: the trust policy is genuinely tight (`aud` = sts.amazonaws.com AND `sub` = `repo:AltivumInc-Admin/quantum-computing:ref:refs/heads/main`, verified in the deployed AssumeRolePolicyDocument), the workflow has no `pull_request` trigger, and `MaxSessionDuration` is 3600. A fork PR on this public repo runs as `refs/pull/N/merge` and cannot assume the role. Exploitation therefore needs write access to main or a compromised release of one of the three `@v4`-tagged actions first. Real, deployed, and worth fixing today — but latent, not an open door.

**Verification — correct as written** (partly true, medium, observed live). The central claim holds, and I confirmed it live rather than from the source alone.

**The comment is factually false.** `aws lambda list-functions --region us-east-2 --max-items 5` returns a populated `Environment.Variables` dict for 4 of the first 5 functions. Sample (I printed key NAMES only, deliberately): `RegainCoaching` -> AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_ENDPOINT, USER_POOL_ID, RESUME_BUCKET_NAME, 16 more; `tj-scents-api-dev-dbQuery` -> **DB_PASSWORD, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET**, COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID, DB_HOST/USER, 6 more. A plaintext value does come back: `--query 'Functions[?FunctionName==`VetROI_Recommend_CF`].Environment.Variables.ENABLE_S3_DATA'` returned the value. So `infra/github-oidc-drift-role.yaml:64-65` ("returns metadata only (no code, no environment secrets)") is wrong on the environment clause.

**Blast radius, measured.** `--query 'length(Functions)'` across pages: 269 functions in us-east-2. `--query 'length(Functions[?Environment!=`null`])'`: 199 carry environment config. Roughly 11 are quantum's; the rest are unrelated Altivum production workloads (VetROI, tj-scents, RegainCoaching). The uniquely damaging item is another business's live Stripe secret key and DB password — the finder's benign-looking sample obscured this.

**It is live, not dormant.** `aws iam get-role-policy --role-name quantum-ci-drift-check --policy-name read-lambda-code-only` returns the template verbatim, including `{"Action":"lambda:ListFunctions","Resource":"*","Effect":"Allow"}`. `aws iam get-role` shows the role created 2026-08-05; `gh variable list` shows AWS_DRIFT_ROLE_ARN set to that ARN. drift.yml runs daily at 13:00 UTC.

**The grant is unnecessary.** `grep -rn "list-functions|list_functions" scripts/ Makefile` -> no matches. check-lambda-drift.mjs:39-56 uses a hardcoded 11-entry `FUNCTIONS` array and calls only `aws lambda get-function --query Code.Location`; check-rate-parity.mjs:33 hardcodes `["quantum-tutor","quantum-qpu-submit"]`. Nothing enumerates. This kills the only real defense ("the drift check needs it") — the fix is deleting five lines with no behavior change.

**Refutation attempts that failed:** no guard elsewhere (deployed policy == template); no recorded deliberate decision (`git log -S ListFunctions` on the file returns only the single introducing commit 2286697, and CLAUDE.md says nothing); the trust policy IS tight and I confirmed it (`aud` + `sub` pinned to `repo:AltivumInc-Admin/quantum-computing:ref:refs/heads/main`), which correctly blocks fork PRs since those run as `refs/pull/N/merge`.

**Why medium, not high.** Reaching it needs a second compromise first — repo write access to main (already a higher privilege) or a malicious release of one of the three mutable-tag-pinned actions in the one job holding `id-token: write` (drift.yml:36, 56, 62 — that part of the claim is accurate as written). That is a demonstrated supply-chain path, not a theoretical one, but it is a precondition. Medium is the right call; the finder's severity number was right even though the reasoning behind it was wrong in both directions.

The most damaging property here is not the grant but the comment: it tells the next reader the exposure does not exist, which is how this survived review.

> Correction. Two parts of the reasoning are wrong, and the impact is understated rather than inflated.

(1) "The ${FunctionNamePrefix}-* scoping on the GetFunction statement is defeated by the unscoped ListFunctions" is only half right. ListFunctions returns FunctionConfiguration objects with no `Code` field at all — verified, top-level keys are [Architectures, CodeSha256, CodeSize, Description, Environment, EphemeralStorage, FunctionArn, FunctionName, Handler, LastModified, Layers, LoggingConfig, MemorySize, PackageType, RevisionId, Role, Runtime, SnapStart, Timeout, TracingConfig, Version, VpcConfig]. There is no `Code.Location` presigned URL, so the deployment-package half of the prefix scoping still holds; an attacker cannot download the code of non-quantum functions. Only the *configuration* half is defeated. The comment's "no code" clause is true; its "no environment secrets" clause is false.

(2) Naming lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration as part of the same problem ("does the same for this project's functions") is wrong. That statement is correctly scoped to quantum-* AND is required: scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs:36-51 calls `aws lambda get-function-configuration --query Environment.Variables.RATE_CARD` on quantum-tutor and quantum-qpu-submit. Reading quantum-* env vars is the job, not the leak. Deleting it would break the rate-parity guard. Only the ListFunctions statement is the over-grant, and it is pure dead weight — nothing in the repo calls it.

(3) Severity direction: the finder's impact ("least-privilege and blast-radius problem rather than an open door") understates it. Their own sample cites benign config, but the same call also returns another business's live credential material.

### The deployed tutor WAF still returns a bare 403 with no CORS headers, two PRs behind edge.yaml, and the daily drift job cannot see it

`lambda/tutor/edge.yaml:61-100` — `ff956fc7b` · medium · confirmed · correctness · observed live · re-raised from `f4b00f00a` · fix plan 10

**Claim.** `aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --name quantum-tutor-edge` returns `CustomResponseBodies: []` and a single rule `PerIpRateLimit` with `Action: {"Block": {}}`. The committed template at `lambda/tutor/edge.yaml:61-100` defines a `RateLimited` custom response body, `ResponseCode: 429`, and an explicit `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header — with a 30-line comment explaining that without that header the browser DISCARDS the throttle response, `fetch` rejects with `TypeError`, and `ask-tutor.tsx` maps it to `tutor.unreachable`. `.github/workflows/drift.yml` runs only `check-lambda-drift.mjs` (which downloads Lambda deployment packages) and `check-rate-parity.mjs` (which reads Lambda env config). Neither reads WAF, CloudFront, API Gateway or any other stack resource, so the daily job reports green over this.

**Impact.** A rate-limited learner today gets a 403 the browser refuses to expose to JavaScript, and the tutor UI tells them the service is down — the precise confusion PR #186 was written to remove, still shipping. More broadly: `make drift` and the daily job answer "is what is running what is in git?" only for Lambda *code*, so every non-Lambda resource in 17 CloudFormation templates can drift indefinitely under a green signal.

**Evidence.** `aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name quantum-tutor-edge --id b77fad07-0299-47b3-aab3-14f6cadbdec3` → `CustomResponseBodies: []` / `PerIpRateLimit {"Block": {}}`. Committed `lambda/tutor/edge.yaml:71`: `ResponseCode: 429`, `:96`: `- Name: Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, medium, observed live). Reproduced against the live account ($PROD_ACCOUNT, `aws sts get-caller-identity` = AltivumManager). Every load-bearing assertion holds.

1. The deployed ACL is the pre-#176 version. `aws wafv2 get-web-acl --scope CLOUDFRONT --region us-east-1 --name quantum-tutor-edge --id b77fad07-0299-47b3-aab3-14f6cadbdec3` returns one rule `PerIpRateLimit` with `"Action": {"Block": {}}`, `Limit: 300`, `EvaluationWindowSec: 60`, no scope-down statement, and **no `CustomResponseBodies` key at all** (the finding writes it as `[]`; the API omits the field — same thing). That is byte-for-byte the shape at `git show c75eb16:lambda/tutor/edge.yaml` (PR #57, bare `Block: {}`), not the committed `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/tutor/edge.yaml:61-100`.

2. "Two PRs behind" is exact. `git log --oneline -- lambda/tutor/edge.yaml` → #57 (2026-06-25), #176 (2026-07-20, adds `RateLimited` body + `ResponseCode: 429`), #186 (2026-07-26, adds `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` + the OPTIONS scope-down). `aws cloudformation describe-stacks --region us-east-1` shows `quantum-tutor-edge` at **CREATE_COMPLETE, created 2026-06-25, LastUpdatedTime 2026-06-25** — never updated in the 13 months since. It has been undeployed for a month.

3. The most damning confirmation the finding didn't cite: **the sibling stack got the same fix and it shipped.** `quantum-qpu-edge` is `UPDATE_COMPLETE` 2026-07-26 (PR #186's date), and its live ACL carries the full remedy — `CustomResponseBodies.RateLimited`, `ResponseCode: 429`, and `ResponseHeaders: [{Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://quantum.altivum.ai}]`. One half of PR #186 was deployed, the other half was not, and nothing noticed for a month. That is precisely the failure `scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs`'s own header prose describes.

4. The path is LIVE, not dormant. `aws amplify get-app --app-id d1ao02to23x85y` → `NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTOR_URL: https://$CF_DOMAIN.cloudfront.net/`, which `aws cloudfront list-distributions` resolves to E388TS3JCTNW3J — Enabled, origin `$LAMBDA_URL`, and `WebACLId` = the drifted tutor ACL ARN. A single benign preflight (`curl -i -X OPTIONS https://$CF_DOMAIN.cloudfront.net/ -H 'Origin: https://quantum.altivum.ai' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST'`) returns 200 with `access-control-allow-origin: https://quantum.altivum.ai` — confirming the request is genuinely cross-origin, so a header-less block response is unreadable to JS.

5. Nothing else can rescue the block response. `aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id E388TS3JCTNW3J` → `CustomErrorResponses.Quantity: 0`, `ResponseHeadersPolicyId: null`, zero extra cache behaviors. No layer downstream of WAF can attach the missing CORS header.

6. The client chain is as described: `web/src/components/ask-tutor.tsx:283` calls `transportErrorMessage(res.status, t)` only on a readable response; `:341-344` maps a `TypeError` (which is what a CORS-discarded response produces) to `t("tutor.unreachable")`.

7. The drift blind spot is real. `.github/workflows/drift.yml` runs exactly two steps: `node scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs` and `node scripts/check-rate-parity.mjs`; `make drift` (Makefile:53-63) runs the same two. `grep -rniE "waf|cloudfront|webacl|distribution|apigateway|cloudformation"` over both scripts returns one hit — a prose word in a comment. Both speak only `lambda` (`GetFunctionCommand`, `aws lambda get-function`). No WAF, CloudFront, API Gateway or CFN read exists anywhere in `.github/workflows/`.

Two calibrations, neither of which touches the defect:
- **Frequency.** The limit is 300 requests/minute per source IP, and edge.yaml's own parameter comment calls that "orders of magnitude above a real learner." Whoever trips this is running a script, not studying. The user-facing harm is therefore near-theoretical; the systemic half (a month-old fix invisible to a daily green guard, with a demonstrated one-of-two-stacks split) is what earns medium.
- **Secondary mechanism the finding omits.** Because the live ACL also lacks #186's OPTIONS scope-down, a burst that trips the limit blocks the *preflight* too — and a 429/403 on a preflight fails the request as a network error no matter what headers it carries. So in the live configuration the missing `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` is not the only reason the throttle is unreadable; it is one of two.
- Minor: the impact line says "17 CloudFormation templates." Counting files carrying `AWSTemplateFormatVersion` in the repo gives 27. The direction of the claim is unaffected (it understates it).

The realistic innocent case is a shared NAT (a lab or office). ask-tutor.tsx:72-76 already deliberately makes 403 and 429 read identically for exactly this drift window; it simply never executes. ### The curriculum teaches TN1 as a live, priced, dispatchable Braket simulator, but TN1 is RETIRED in every region

`lib/hardware/devices.py:85-90` — `ffcf96e3b` · medium · confirmed · correctness · observed live · fix plan 14

**Claim.** `aws braket search-devices` reports `RETIRED Amazon Braket TN1 arn:aws:braket:::device/quantum-simulator/amazon/tn1` in us-east-1, us-west-2 and eu-west-2 — every region where it ever existed. The repo still presents it as available everywhere: `lib/hardware/devices.py:85-90` registers `"tn1"` in `DEVICES` with `gate_capable: True`, so `run_circuit(circuit, device_name="tn1")` passes every gate and submits; `lib/utils/cost.py:18` prices it at $0.275/min; `02-hardware/GUIDE.md:184` lists it in the simulator ladder ("up to ~50 qubits, $0.275/min") and `:301` answers the selection quiz with "Large but lightly entangled circuit? TN1"; `README.md:584` lists its rate; `web/src/components/quantum/devices.ts:48` gives it a row in the device table with no status field and `cost.ts:14` prices it in the calculator; `web/src/lib/glossary.ts:213` and `glossary-es.ts:91` define Braket's simulators as "SV1, DM1 and TN1". `tests/solutions/02-hardware/01-device-discovery.py:22` makes `return "SV1" if n_qubits <= 34 else "TN1"` the *canonical answer* to an exercise.

**Impact.** A learner who follows the module's own device-selection guidance for a large lightly-entangled circuit picks a machine AWS retired, and their submit fails. The exercise whose canonical answer is TN1 teaches the wrong selection rule. No guard can catch this: `tests/test_pricing_prose.py` validates dollar *amounts* against `PRICING` and would happily keep blessing $0.275/min forever, and nothing in the repo compares `DEVICES` ARNs to `search-devices` status. The same class of staleness was caught once before (IonQ Aria, noted in the cost.py comment at line 11) and fixed by hand.

**Evidence.** `aws braket search-devices --filters "[]" --region us-east-1` → `RETIRED Amazon Braket TN1 arn:aws:braket:::device/quantum-simulator/amazon/tn1`; identical in us-west-2 and eu-west-2. `lib/hardware/devices.py:85-90` carries that exact ARN with `"gate_capable": True`. `lib/utils/cost.py:18`: `"TN1": {"per_minute": 0.275},`.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, medium, observed live). Tried to refute on three fronts — is TN1 really retired, does the gate actually let it through, and does some guard catch it — and all three failed to refute.

1) TN1 IS retired everywhere (read-only AWS):
`for r in us-east-1 us-west-2 eu-west-2 eu-north-1; do aws braket search-devices --filters "[]" --region $r --query 'devices[].[deviceStatus,deviceName,deviceArn]' --output text; done`
→ `RETIRED TN1 arn:aws:braket:::device/quantum-simulator/amazon/tn1` in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-2 (absent in eu-north-1). Confirmed directly:
`aws braket get-device --device-arn "arn:aws:braket:::device/quantum-simulator/amazon/tn1" --region us-east-1` → `TN1  RETIRED  SIMULATOR`.
AWS's own current developer guide corroborates: the "Submitting quantum tasks to simulators" page now lists only DM1, SV1 and LocalSimulator — TN1 has been removed from the submittable set. (Stale AWS marketing/FAQ pages still describe TN1; the live API and the dev guide are authoritative.)

2) The dispatch path really does submit — reproduced with the AwsDevice constructor stubbed so nothing was sent:
`.venv/bin/python -c "...patch('lib.hardware.devices.AwsDevice')...run_circuit(c, device_name='tn1', shots=1000, s3_location=('bkt','pfx'), estimated_minutes=2.0)"`
→ prints `[TN1] Estimated cost: $0.5500 (~2.0 min @ $0.275/min)` and constructs `AwsDevice('arn:aws:braket:::device/quantum-simulator/amazon/tn1')`, then reaches `device.run()`. No gate rejects it: the spec keys across all of DEVICES are only `['allowlist','arn','gate_capable','max_shots','min_shots','provider']` — there is no status/retired field anywhere. Live confirmation that the failure lands at submit, not construction:
`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1 .venv/bin/python -c "from braket.aws import AwsDevice; d=AwsDevice('...tn1'); print(d.status)"` → constructs fine, `status = RETIRED`.
Ironic detail: the gate's own comment at lib/hardware/devices.py:237 claims it rejects "a retired or misspelled device", and 01-device-discovery.ipynb cell 5 warns that a retyped ARN copy "silently goes stale when a device is retired" — the single source of truth is the thing that went stale.

3) No guard catches it — `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_pricing_prose.py tests/test_devices.py tests/test_cost.py -q` → **63 passed**, fully green while the curriculum teaches a retired device. test_pricing_prose derives valid dollar figures from `PRICING` itself, so $0.275/min stays blessed forever. `grep -rn "search_devices|search-devices"` finds nothing comparing DEVICES ARNs to live status; `make drift` is Lambda/rate-card drift only.

Every cited line verified verbatim at the stated number: devices.py:85-90 (tn1, `gate_capable: True`), cost.py:18, GUIDE.md:184 + :301, README.md:584, web devices.ts:48 (no status field), cost.ts:14, glossary.ts:213, glossary-es.ts:91, solutions/…/01-device-discovery.py:22.

### The QPU allowance comment states a $2.50 lifetime cap that the constant twelve lines above sets to 0

`lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:407` — `f5eb9edb2` · low · confirmed · docs-drift · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 09

**Claim.** `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:407` reads "a learner who was promised a $5.00 allowance by name keeps it forever, even though LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS is now $2.50." `qpu-core.mjs:47` reads `export const LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0;`. The grandfathering mechanism the comment describes (`if_not_exists(capMicros, :cap)`) is correct and the `effectiveCap > 0` guard at :563 is correct; only the stated value is stale — the $2.50 allowance was withdrawn 2026-07-28, which `lib/hardware/devices.py:57-61` records accurately.

**Correction.** The scope and the impact argument are misattributed. The finder cites only :407 and then argues the harm through CLAUDE.md rule 16 ("read the fences there"). But a rule-16 reader lands on lines 37-47, which state the withdrawal correctly and at length ("WITHDRAWN 2026-07-28 … a new learner's default allowance is ZERO"), immediately above `export const LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0;`. That reader is not misled by :407, which is 360 lines away inside the TransactWriteItems funding leg and is read by a maintainer, not a learner of the fences. The line that actually does what the finder describes is `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:57` — "the hard caps below (per-user $2.50 lifetime + $15/day global) remain the real spend boundary" — which sits in the constants block itself, ten lines under the zeroed constant, and the finder missed it. A fix that touches only :407 leaves the more visible stale statement in place.

**Impact.** CLAUDE.md rule 16 tells every reader to learn the spend fences by reading these constants "there". A reader who does gets a comment saying new learners have a $2.50 hardware allowance when they have none, in the file that decides whether real money is spent. No behaviour is wrong — the code reads the constant, not the comment.

**Evidence.** `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:47`: `export const LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS = 0;`. `lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs:407`: `// LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS is now $2.50. Never write a cap-lowering`.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: confirmed · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). The stale comment is exactly where and as claimed.

Read + machine-checked (`cd /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lambda/qpu && node -e "..."` printing the parsed constant and the two cited lines):
- constant source at :47 is `0` -> $0.00
- line 407 text: `// LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS is now $2.50. Never write a cap-lowering`
- `grep -n 'LIFETIME_CAP_MICROS|\$2\.50|\$5\.00' lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs` -> :47 (=0), :57, :328, :392, :406, :407, :421

Git history settles the drift (`git log -L 40,50:lambda/qpu/qpu-core.mjs`): 5_000_000 in fcc5f3e -> 2_500_000 in 2a51fea -> 0 in 9ae3889 ("withdraw the sponsored QPU allowance"). The :406-407 comment was written for the middle state and never followed the constant down to 0.

The claim's other assertions check out: `if_not_exists(capMicros, :cap)` grandfathering at :418, and the load-bearing guard is verbatim at :563 — `const fitsAllowance = effectiveCap > 0 && alreadySpent + cost <= effectiveCap;`. `cd lambda/qpu && node --test` -> 88/88 pass, so nothing guards the comment text and no behavior is at stake; the code reads the constant, as the finder says.

Three refinements the finder missed or got loose, none of which unseat the defect:
1. UNDER-SCOPED — the same stale $2.50 appears a second time at qpu-core.mjs:57: "the hard caps below (per-user $2.50 lifetime + $15/day global) remain the real spend boundary". That one is arguably worse, because it is in the entitlement-gate preamble a rule-16 reader hits first. Any fix should take both.

### A script that deletes and recreates the LIVE Stripe webhook endpoint exists only as an untracked working-tree file

`scripts/stripe/rotate-webhook-endpoint.mjs:1` — `f1c8fe326` · low · partly true · hygiene · ran locally · re-raised from `fadbcc77f` · fix plan 08

The only "delete-and-recreate" is in the header prose describing why repinning `api_version` mints a new secret. What is untracked is the automation plus the signed-probe verification — real added value, but not undocumented knowledge. "No CI runs it" is true but non-distinguishing: no CI runs the tracked Stripe scripts either (`grep -rn stripe .github/workflows/` finds only the lambda unit-test matrix; `make stripe-parity` is manual).

### The Makefile's documented sandbox-provisioning command names the superseded Stripe account and would be refused by --expect-account

### lambda/sync is the only Lambda that vendors node_modules — 2,560 tracked files, 72% of the repo, that nothing verifies and CI deletes before testing

`lambda/sync/package.json:13-15` — `f62f1c5d1` · low · confirmed · hygiene · ran locally · fix plan 14

**Claim.** `git ls-files lambda/sync/node_modules | wc -l` → 2,560. Every other Lambda is 0: `.gitignore:47,79,84` explicitly ignores `lambda/{tutor,review-email,qpu}/node_modules/` with the documented rationale "npm ci restores them from the committed package-lock.json", and stripe and analytics are untracked too. Only sync is vendored, with no comment anywhere explaining why. Nothing checks it: `scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs:15-17` explicitly excludes node_modules from the deployed-vs-git comparison, `sourceFiles` at :62-69 scans only top-level `.mjs`/`.js`, CI's `npm ci` in `lambda/sync` deletes and reinstalls the tree from the lockfile before `npm test`, and the documented deploy (`lambda/sync/README.md:71`) is `npm ci && sam build`, which regenerates it too.

**Correction.** Two citation slips, neither changing the conclusion. (1) "72% of the repo" is 73.7% by tracked-file count (2560/3474); by bytes it is 51% (14,008 KB of 27,396 KB tracked) — the percentage holds only on the file-count reading. (2) "stripe and analytics are untracked too" understates the finder's own case: both carry their own `lambda/<name>/.gitignore` whose line 1 is `node_modules/` (`git check-ignore -v` names the rule). All five other Lambdas are therefore DELIBERATELY ignored — three in the root `.gitignore`, two in per-directory files — leaving sync the only one of six with no ignore rule anywhere. Also, the "npm ci restores them from the committed package-lock.json" rationale is at `.gitignore:77-78` and `:82-83` (review-email, qpu) only; line 47's tutor entry sits under a different comment about build artifacts and corpus.json. And `sourceFiles` is at check-lambda-drift.mjs:61-66, not :62-69.

**Impact.** The committed tree is never the tree that is tested and never the tree that is deployed — it is 2,560 files of pure review surface in a public repo, and a hand-edit or a partial `npm install` inside it would be invisible to every guard. Currently benign: I compared all 29 `node_modules/*/package.json` versions against `lambda/sync/package-lock.json` and found zero mismatches. The cost is bloat and reviewer noise, not a live defect.

**Evidence.** `git ls-files lambda/sync/node_modules | wc -l` → 2560; the same command for analytics/qpu/review-email/stripe/tutor → 0. `.gitignore:79,84` ignore two of them by name. My version comparison across the lockfile's 29 `node_modules/` entries: `checked 29 mismatches 0`.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). Every substantive claim reproduces. Commands run (all read-only; the npm ci was done on a COPY in the scratchpad, never in the repo):

1. Count. `git ls-files lambda/sync/node_modules | wc -l` -> 2560. Loop over `lambda/*/`: analytics 0, qpu 0, review-email 0, stripe 0, tutor 0, sync 2560. `git ls-files | wc -l` -> 3474.

2. Ignore rules. `grep -n node_modules .gitignore` -> :47 (tutor), :79 (review-email), :84 (qpu), exactly as cited. Additionally `lambda/stripe/.gitignore` and `lambda/analytics/.gitignore` each contain `node_modules/` + `.aws-sam/`. `lambda/sync/` has NO .gitignore. So five of six Lambdas exclude it by one mechanism or the other and sync is the lone exception — the finding's direction, only stronger than it stated.

3. No guard sees it. `scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs` docstring lines 15-17 read verbatim "Compares hand-written source only — node_modules and build metadata legitimately differ…"; `sourceFiles` is at :60-67 and filters `readdirSync(dir)` to top-level `.mjs|.js`, so the subtree is unreachable. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:162 matrix `dir: [tutor, qpu, sync, review-email, stripe, analytics]`, :165 `working-directory: lambda/${{ matrix.dir }}`, :179 `npm ci`, :182 `npm test` — sync's committed tree is deleted and reinstalled before any test runs. `lambda/sync/README.md`:71 is exactly `cd lambda/sync && npm ci && sam build`. `lambda/sync/template.yaml` declares no `CodeUri`, no `Globals`, no `Metadata: BuildMethod`.

4. Currently benign — stronger than the finder proved. I copied only `package.json` + `package-lock.json` to the scratchpad, ran `npm ci`, then `diff -rq <scratchpad>/node_modules lambda/sync/node_modules` -> 0 lines of output, and `find … -type f | wc -l` -> 2560 on both sides. A fresh install from the committed lockfile reproduces the committed tree BYTE-FOR-BYTE, not merely at matching versions. `git status --porcelain lambda/sync` is clean. `node -e` over the lockfile confirms 29 `node_modules/` entries.

Nits that do not move the verdict: the cited location `lambda/sync/package.json:13-15` does not exist — the file is 13 lines and the `dependencies` block is 10-12; `sourceFiles` is :60-67 not :62-69; the share is 73.7% (2560/3474), not 72%; and the "npm ci restores them from the committed package-lock.json" rationale is the comment above :79 and :84 only — :47's tutor comment says something different.

One thing the finding does not disclose and the reader should know: this is a re-report of an already-tracked item. `docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-16.md:276` carries the same finding (at 2560/3405 = 75%), and `gh issue view 219` returns OPEN, titled "2,560 files of node_modules are committed under lambda/sync — 75% of every tracked file in the repo", created 2026-08-17. That audit's verifier reached the same conclusion (hygiene, not a defect) and additionally established `git log --oneline -- lambda/sync/node_modules` returns exactly one commit, 8ea76b8 (#110) — which I re-ran and confirmed.

Severity: low, agreeing with the finder. Zero functional, security or deploy consequence, and one qualifier on the impact prose: a hand-edit inside the tree would NOT be invisible to every guard — it lands in `git status` and in the PR diff. What is true is that no automated check compares it to the lockfile and nothing ever executes the committed copy, so the guard that would catch it is human review of a 2,560-file diff.

**Verification — correct as written** (confirmed, low, ran locally). I tried to refute this and could not — every load-bearing claim survived, and one of my checks came back stronger than the finder stated.

Counts (`git ls-files lambda/sync/node_modules | wc -l`): sync 2560; tutor, qpu, review-email, stripe, analytics all 0. Confirmed.

Searched for a rationale and found none. `git log --diff-filter=A -- lambda/sync/node_modules` returns exactly one commit (8ea76b8, PR #110, 2026-07-05) and `git log -- lambda/sync/node_modules | wc -l` is 1 — added once, never touched since. The nearest thing to a recorded decision is commit 32730dd's message ("sync and tutor already track theirs"), but that is about package-lock.json, not node_modules. Note that `lambda/sync/.aws-sam/` IS in the root .gitignore while `lambda/sync/node_modules/` is not — the sibling artifact was ignored and this one was missed, which reads as oversight, not intent.

Nothing verifies it, and I checked more guards than the finder did. `scripts/check-lambda-drift.mjs:15-17` excludes node_modules by design ("comparing them would make this cry wolf until someone turned it off") and `sourceFiles` (:61-66) scans only top-level .mjs/.js. All three infra guards skip it too: `wallet-ttl.test.ts:47`, `credit-writers.test.ts:62`, and `no-commercial-terms.test.ts:33` each carry a node_modules skip — so the tree sits outside even the rule-6 commercial-terms leak guard.

Both CI paths destroy it, not just the one cited: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:179` runs `npm ci` in the `lambda/${{ matrix.dir }}` matrix (sync included, :162), and the standby mirror at `infra/ci-standby/template.yaml:186-189` loops `(cd "lambda/$d" && npm ci && npm test)` over the same six. `lambda/sync/README.md:71` is `npm ci && sam build`. So the committed tree is never tested and never deployed.

I re-ran the parity check independently and it is not merely "29 versions match" — the vendored set is exactly the lockfile set: 29 lockfile `node_modules/` entries, 29 vendored packages, 0 in lockfile but not vendored, 0 vendored but not in lockfile, 0 version mismatches. So it is not even a partial install; it is a faithful, wholly redundant snapshot.

Severity: I agree with the finder's "low" and would not raise it. Nothing in the repo reads from the tree (only `check-lambda-drift.mjs:51` and `wallet-ttl.test.ts:46` reference `lambda/sync` at all, and the latter skips node_modules). One nuance on the impact clause: a hand-edit inside the tree would indeed be invisible to every guard, but it would also be inert — `npm ci` overwrites it on both CI paths and on the documented deploy, so it cannot reach the deployed artifact except via a local `sam build` that skipped `npm ci`. Genuine hygiene, correctly scoped by the finder as reviewer noise rather than a live defect.

### The unsolved-notebook gate asserts only that a check did not say 'correct', never that it said 'not attempted', and grading.py's markers are not the machine contract its comment claims

`tests/test_exercise_checks.py:302` — `f125f11a6` · low · confirmed · test-coverage · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 14

**Claim.** `lib/grading.py:19-20` states "The printed markers are machine-parsed by the harness — change them only in lockstep with tests/test_exercise_checks.py." The harness imports nothing from `lib.grading`: `NOT_ATTEMPTED_MARKER` and `NOT_YET_MARKER` are never referenced there at all (only `tests/test_grading.py` uses them), and the one marker it does key on is hardcoded as the string literal `" correct."` at line 302, not read from `CORRECT_MARKER`. So the lockstep is a comment, not a coupling. Two consequences: (a) renaming `CORRECT_MARKER` makes `test_checks_do_not_pass_unsolved` vacuously green — it would never again find the substring it is negating — while `test_checks_pass_with_canonical_solutions` (strict mode, no marker parsing) keeps passing; (b) the docstring's stronger promise, "Unsolved, every check must say 'not attempted' — never 'correct'", is not tested: a check keyed on a variable the teaching cells already define fails unsolved with a plain `AssertionError` ("not yet - ..."), which satisfies both assertions and ships as a fresh-names-rule violation.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. (1) The title's claim that "grading.py's markers are not the machine contract its comment claims" overstates. lib/grading.py:19-20 says "The printed markers are machine-parsed by the harness — change them only in lockstep with tests/test_exercise_checks.py." The harness DOES machine-parse the printed correct marker (as a literal at line 302), and "change only in lockstep" is exactly the right human mitigation for a literal coupling — the comment never claims a code-level import. Only its plural is loose: two of the three constants (NOT_ATTEMPTED_MARKER, NOT_YET_MARKER) are parsed by nothing in the harness. (2) The Impact mis-attributes the overclaim. docs/exercise-convention.md:56-58 states the enforcement accurately — "The harness executes the unsolved notebook and fails if any check passes on its own" — which is precisely what the harness does. The stronger, untested promise ("every check cell must report 'not attempted'") lives only in tests/test_exercise_checks.py's own module docstring (line 16) and the function docstring (line 274). The convention doc is not overclaiming; the test file is overclaiming about itself.

**Impact.** The fresh-names rule in `docs/exercise-convention.md` — the thing that makes an exercise an exercise rather than a re-print of a teaching cell — is only partially enforced, and the enforcement can be silently disabled by an edit that looks cosmetic. This was raised in `docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-16.md:601-604` and is unchanged at HEAD.

**Evidence.** `grep -n "CORRECT_MARKER|NOT_ATTEMPTED_MARKER|NOT_YET_MARKER" tests/test_exercise_checks.py` returns nothing; the only marker assertion is `tests/test_exercise_checks.py:302`: `assert " correct." not in stdout, (`. `lib/grading.py:19-20` carries the lockstep comment; `lib/grading.py:31-32` define the two unused markers.

**Split verdict.** reproduces: confirmed · correct as written: partly true. Published at the more severe reading.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). Every cited fact is exact, and I reproduced both consequences mechanically.

Facts verified (`grep -n "correct\." tests/test_exercise_checks.py` and `grep -rn "CORRECT_MARKER|NOT_ATTEMPTED_MARKER|NOT_YET_MARKER" --include="*.py" .`):
- /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/lib/grading.py:19-20 carries the lockstep comment verbatim; :30-32 define the three markers.
- The only marker references outside lib/grading.py are in /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/tests/test_grading.py:8-10,34,43,45,54,64,74. The harness references none of them; its sole occurrence of the string "grading" is line 168, a grep of NOTEBOOK source for `from lib.grading import check`, not an import.
- /Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/tests/test_exercise_checks.py:302 is exactly `assert " correct." not in stdout, (` — a hardcoded literal. (The third grep hit, web/jupyterlite-build/files/lib/grading.py, is gitignored build output — `git check-ignore -v` confirms — so it is not a second source of truth.)

Reproduction (scratchpad script, `uv run python .../repro.py`): a check keyed on a variable the teaching cells already define fails unsolved through lib.grading and prints `[check] Exercise 1: not yet - only the two GHZ outcomes. Revisit the hints and try again.` Applying the harness's two assertions to that stdout: `"[check]" in stdout` -> True, `" correct." not in stdout` -> True. The gate passes; NOT_ATTEMPTED_MARKER is absent, so the docstring's stronger promise ("every check must say 'not attempted'") is not what is tested. Consequence (a) reproduces the same way against a stdout of `[check] Exercise 1: solved.`

One nuance, stated rather than a correction: renaming the IDENTIFIER `CORRECT_MARKER` would break tests/test_grading.py at import (`from lib.grading import CORRECT_MARKER`). It is changing the marker's printed VALUE that goes silent — which is exactly what the finding's own clause "it would never again find the substring it is negating" describes, so the mechanism as stated is right.

Blast radius today is nil, which supports low severity. I scanned all 45 converted notebooks / 133 exercises with an AST script (`uv run python .../freshnames2.py`) computing, per check cell, whether any loaded name is unbound on the unsolved run (teaching-cell bindings + scaffold bindings + builtins + the check cell's own imports all counted as available — a bias that over-reports holes): 0 checks can avoid a NameError unsolved. So every shipping check does report "not attempted" today; the defect is a latent weakness in the guard, not a live fresh-names violation. There is no second guard — test_structure (lines 147-199) enforces cell shape, the grading import and the hint tiers only, never name freshness. ### Two content guards scan only GUIDE.md and never GUIDE.es.md, leaving the Spanish half of every lesson page ungated

`tests/test_guide_runnable_fences.py:61` — `f025525e9` · low · confirmed · test-coverage · ran locally · fix plan 12

**Claim.** `find_runnable_fences()` builds its path as `REPO_ROOT / section / "GUIDE.md"`, so the ```runnable fence at `01-foundations/GUIDE.es.md:251` is neither AST-scanned against the qcsim contract nor executed. `tests/test_pricing_prose.py:30` has the same shape: `GUIDES = sorted(REPO_ROOT.glob("0*-*/GUIDE.md"))`, so no Spanish guide's dollar figures are ever compared to `lib.utils.cost.PRICING`. Both files are shipped: `web/src/lib/content.ts:31` selects `GUIDE.es.md` for the `es` locale, and `runnable` is a registered widget fence in `web/src/components/quantum/widget-langs.ts`, so a Spanish learner gets a real Pyodide sandbox seeded from unscanned source.

**Impact.** A Spanish fence that imports PennyLane or calls a Braket result type ships and fails in the learner's browser with no CI signal; a stale rate in a Spanish GUIDE outlives a repricing. Neither is live today — the ES fence's code is byte-identical to the EN one, and I ran `test_pricing_prose`'s own extractor over all seven `GUIDE.es.md` files and found zero non-derivable amounts — so this is a scope hole, not a current defect.

**Evidence.** `tests/test_guide_runnable_fences.py:61`: `guide = REPO_ROOT / section / "GUIDE.md"`. `tests/test_pricing_prose.py:30`: `GUIDES = sorted(REPO_ROOT.glob("0*-*/GUIDE.md"))`. `web/src/lib/content.ts:31`: `const fileName = locale === "es" ? "GUIDE.es.md" : "GUIDE.md";`. My run of `extract_amounts` + `valid_amounts` over `0*-*/GUIDE.es.md` printed no offenders.

**Verification — reproduces** (confirmed, low, ran locally). Both halves reproduce exactly as written, and I could not find any other guard that covers the Spanish guides.

1) The runnable-fence guard never sees the ES fence. `/Users/cperez/dev/altivum-inc/quantum/tests/test_guide_runnable_fences.py:61` is verbatim `guide = REPO_ROOT / section / "GUIDE.md"`. Ran `.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_guide_runnable_fences.py --collect-only -q` -> exactly 3 tests, the only parametrized id being `01-foundations/GUIDE.md:251#1`. `grep -rn '```runnable' 0*-*/GUIDE*.md` shows two fences in the repo: `01-foundations/GUIDE.md:251` and `01-foundations/GUIDE.es.md:251`. The ES one is collected by nothing.

2) The hole is a real gate, not a cosmetic one. Loading the test module and calling its own `scan_source` on a mutated copy of the ES fence body (scratchpad only, no tracked file touched): the real ES body returns `[]`, while `"import pennylane as qml" + body.replace("state_vector()","probability()")` returns `["forbidden import 'pennylane'", "forbidden call '.probability()' (qcsim has no Braket result types)"]`. So the qcsim contract would catch a bad ES fence; the path is the only reason it doesn't.

3) The pricing-prose guard has the same shape. `tests/test_pricing_prose.py:30` is `GUIDES = sorted(REPO_ROOT.glob("0*-*/GUIDE.md"))`; loading the module and printing `[p.name for p in tpp.GUIDES]` gives seven `GUIDE.md` and zero `GUIDE.es.md`. Running its `extract_amounts` + `valid_amounts` over all seven `0*-*/GUIDE.es.md` reproduces the finder's result — zero non-derivable amounts today — but the ES corpus is NOT empty: `02-hardware/GUIDE.es.md` carries {0.075, 0.08, 0.275, 0.3, 1.2, 80.3} and `06-hybrid-jobs/GUIDE.es.md` carries {0.1, 0.29, 3.85, 58, 87, 90, 120, 4800, 4890}. Real Braket rates and worked examples sit in Spanish prose that no repricing guard reads.

4) The shipping path is confirmed: `web/src/lib/content.ts:31` selects `GUIDE.es.md`, `getContent` returns it as `markdownEs`, `web/src/app/learn/[section]/page.tsx:70` passes it to `web/src/components/lesson-body.tsx:34` (`const markdown = locale === "es" ? markdownEs : markdownEn`), and `runnable` is in `WIDGET_LANGS` in `web/src/components/quantum/widget-langs.ts`. Also verified the ES fence body is byte-identical to the EN one, so nothing is broken today.

Worth adding for the reader (a strengthening, not a correction): the hole is wider than two guards. `web/__tests__/content/guide-reps.test.ts:75` and `:184` also build `path.join(REPO_ROOT, entry, "GUIDE.md")`, and `tests/test_content_manifest.py:36` and `scripts/validate_runnable.py:267` likewise. `grep -rn "es\.md" --exclude-dir=node_modules .` finds NO test or CI file referencing `GUIDE.es.md` anywhere in the repo — only `web/src/lib/content.ts` and `scripts/changelog/rules.mjs` routing. Meanwhile each ES guide ships 11-16 interactive widget fences (`grep -c` over quiz/qsim/qchallenge/qpredict/qcostestimate/qdebug/qexpect/qscrub/qblochtarget per file), all of them unparsed by the Rep/quiz corpus gate.

Severity stays low, and I agree with the finder's own framing: this is a scope hole in CI, not a live defect. Nothing ships broken today in either locale.

**Verification — correct as written** (confirmed, low, ran locally). I tried hard to refute this and could not. Every citation is verbatim-accurate and I confirmed the hole by running the guards themselves rather than reading them.

SCOPE HOLE IS REAL AND MEASURED:
- `.venv/bin/python -c "import tests.test_guide_runnable_fences as t; print(t.FENCES)"` returns exactly ONE fence: `01-foundations/GUIDE.md:251#1`. `grep -rn '^```runnable' 0*-*/GUIDE*.md` shows TWO shipped fences — `01-foundations/GUIDE.md:251` and `01-foundations/GUIDE.es.md:251`. The guard collects 1 of 2. Both the AST scan and the subprocess qcsim execution are parametrized off that same collector, so the ES fence gets neither check.
- I ran `test_pricing_prose`'s own `extract_amounts` + `valid_amounts` over all seven `0*-*/GUIDE.es.md`: 20 dollar amounts present in ES prose, 0 non-derivable. So 20 learner-facing figures sit entirely outside the corpus while currently being correct — exactly the "latent, not live" framing the finder used.

REFUTATION AVENUES I CLOSED:
- No EN/ES parity guard exists. `grep -rn "GUIDE\.es"` across the repo hits only `web/src/lib/content.ts` (the reader), the two prior audit docs, and `scripts/changelog/rules.mjs` (path classification, not validation). Nothing compares the two files.
- The EN-only pattern is repo-wide, not compensated elsewhere: `web/__tests__/content/reps-corpus.test.ts:37`, `tutor-corpus.test.ts:25,30,38` and `guide-reps.test.ts` all hardcode `"GUIDE.md"` too. And `guide-reps.test.ts`'s TOKEN_TO_KIND map covers only `q*` Rep tokens — it never collects `runnable`, as the Python docstring already concedes.
- Not machine-generated: no translation tooling under `scripts/`, `Makefile`, or `.github/workflows/`. The ES guides are hand-authored (committed once in `ec356bb` #183), so divergence is a real editing risk, not structurally impossible.
- Reachability confirmed: `web/src/lib/content.ts:31` selects `GUIDE.es.md` for `es`, and `widget-langs.ts:17` registers `"runnable"`. A Spanish learner does get a real Pyodide sandbox seeded from unscanned source.
- I verified the fence bodies are byte-identical (extracted both via the test's own FENCE_RE and compared reprs), so there is no defect today — the finder stated this honestly rather than overselling.

SEVERITY: "low" is correct, and I'd resist inflating it. No live defect on either half; the affected surface is the free curriculum (rules 1/3), not billing, auth, or a metered path; and `01-foundations/GUIDE.md` has had no commits since the ES file's last touch, so the two are currently in sync.

CONTEXT WORTH FLAGGING TO THE READER (not a correction — the finding claims no novelty): the pricing-prose half is a RE-REPORT. `docs/codebase-audit-2026-08-16.md:587-590` already raised the identical `GUIDES` glob claim and its verifier already confirmed it at low severity, noting "the figures currently match, so this is a latent drift hole." The runnable-fence half does appear novel — that test's docstring dates it to 2026-08-18, after the earlier audit. So the deliverable value here is the fence half plus the observation that the two guards share one root cause.

### The changelog guard's learner-visible path list omits lib/ and qcsim/ — the Python library and browser simulator learners actually execute

`scripts/changelog/rules.mjs:60-81` — `f52fa3cf8` · low · confirmed · test-coverage · ran locally · fix plan 14

**Claim.** `LEARNER_VISIBLE` watches `web/src/app/`, `web/src/components/`, eight named `web/src/lib/*.ts` files, and the seven curriculum directories. It does not watch `lib/` or `qcsim/`. Both are learner-facing execution surfaces: `web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh:229` stages `lib/` verbatim into the in-browser lab, every notebook imports from it (`from lib.grading import check`, `from lib.utils.statevector import statevector`), and `qcsim` IS the browser simulator — its 0.3.0 changelog in `qcsim/src/qcsim/__init__.py:29-35` describes changes a learner sees directly ("`print(circuit)` now lays out one column per MOMENT"). The doc comment above `LEARNER_VISIBLE` enumerates three "DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS" (content/reps, web/public, changelog-es) and a "KNOWN BLIND SPOT" (renames); `lib/` and `qcsim/` appear in neither, so by the file's own standard this is an oversight rather than a decision.

**Impact.** A PR that changes only `lib/ml/feature_maps.py` (i.e. the IQP convention fix in #242, which reached the changelog only because it also touched `03-algorithms/` and `web/src/components/`) or only `qcsim/src/qcsim/circuits.py` passes the guard silently, and the bilingual changelog the project just built stops being the record it claims to be.

**Evidence.** `scripts/changelog/rules.mjs:60-81` — the array contains `"00-prereqs/"` … `"06-hybrid-jobs/"` and eight `web/src/lib/*.ts` entries, and no `"lib/"` or `"qcsim/"`. `web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh:228-229`: `rm -rf files/lib; cp -R ../../lib files/lib`.

`infra/ci-standby/template.yaml:156-236` — `f44701f97` · low · confirmed · consistency · ran locally · SPLIT VERDICT · fix plan 14

**Claim.** The buildspec's own header says "Mirror of .github/workflows/ci.yml (jobs: web, lambdas, python, build-smoke)". It is not. `ci.yml` runs two steps the mirror has no counterpart for: `node --test scripts/changelog/*.test.mjs` plus the `Changelog guard` step (ci.yml:120-149), and the `Assert the KaTeX + syntax-highlight render path ran` step (ci.yml:266-289). `grep -n "changelog\|katex" infra/ci-standby/template.yaml` returns nothing. **Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. (1) "is NOW behind" implies drift after the fact: the KaTeX step landed 2026-07-20 in #175 (52a89cc), while infra/ci-standby/template.yaml was CREATED 2026-07-29 in #197 (c24b9dd) — the mirror never carried that assertion, it was born incomplete. Only the changelog family is true drift (#238, 2026-08-19, after the mirror existed; the template was then edited again in #247 on 2026-08-27 without picking it up). Copying it would be a bug, not a fix. Only the changelog *unit tests* (`node --test scripts/changelog/*.test.mjs`, zero deps, identical shape to the founding-credit line the mirror does carry) are a clean omission, and they are near-worthless in the standby since the guard they test cannot run there. **Impact.** The failover CI cannot catch a broken math/highlight pipeline or an unannounced learner-visible change. Because the mirror is inline in the template (deliberately, so a PR cannot edit it), keeping it in sync is a manual step with no guard — the founding-credit and analytics gaps above are the same failure mode one layer down. ### The Pyodide runtime shipped to every learner is fetched over the network with no integrity check and cached indefinitely by version alone

`web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh:75-104` — `f9c491ba1` · low · partly true · security · ran locally · re-raised from `f049f7b89` · fix plan 04

**Claim.** `fetch_pyodide_core` (build.sh:74-93) downloads `pyodide-core-${version}.tar.bz2` from GitHub releases with `curl -fsSL --retry 3` and no checksum, then caches it at `.cache/pyodide-core-${version}.tar.bz2` and reuses it forever on a `-s` test alone. `fetch_closure_wheels` (build.sh:98-105) fetches every closure wheel from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` with no hash either, verifying only `test -s`. Both CI (`ci.yml` cache key `jupyterlite-v3-...`) and Amplify (`amplify.yml` caches `jupyterlite-build/.cache/**/*`) persist that directory across builds. `requirements.txt` pins `jupyterlite-core==0.7.6` and `jupyterlite-pyodide-kernel==0.7.0` but leaves `jupyter-server>=2.14` and `build>=1.2` floating, with no hashes and no transitive pins.

**Correction.** Two parts of the reasoning are wrong. (1) "every wheel the in-browser lab loads [is] accepted on TLS alone" is false: the CDN wheels are integrity-verified at load time in the browser against pyodide-lock.json's per-package sha256. Pyodide's own PackageManager.loadPackage defaults to `{checkIntegrity:!0}` and builds an SRI string from the lock ("sha256-"+base64(l.sha256)) — grep -o 'sha256[^,;)]\{0,80\}' web/public/pyodide/pyodide.asm.js — and micropip calls _validate_sha256_checksum whenever a sha256 is known (micropip/wheelinfo.py:150,188, extracted from the staged micropip-0.11.0 wheel). A jsdelivr-only tampered wheel therefore makes the lab REFUSE to load the package, not silently execute it. The tarball half stands fully, because the lock ships inside that same unverified tarball and so is not an independent trust anchor. (2) The CI-persistence framing overstates: the ci.yml key `jupyterlite-v3-...` hashes requirements.txt + qcsim only and contains no Pyodide version (version keying is the .cache FILENAME, not the Actions key), and GitHub Actions cache scoping means a fork or feature-branch PR cannot write into the cache main's builds restore. The indefinite-reuse surface that actually matters is Amplify's `jupyterlite-build/.cache/**/*` (amplify.yml:28, not :27). Minor: fetch_pyodide_core is lines 73-92, not 74-93.

**Correction.** The impact sentence "the wasm, the stdlib, and every wheel the in-browser lab loads are accepted on TLS alone" is wrong for the wheels — which are the large majority of the fetches the finding cites (27 of them for the lab, 3 for the lesson runtime). Every wheel `fetch_closure_wheels` pulls from jsdelivr is a Pyodide-lock package, and Pyodide applies real Subresource Integrity to each one at load time in the browser, keyed on a hash from a DIFFERENT origin (the GitHub-released core tarball's `pyodide-lock.json`). A tampered jsdelivr wheel therefore fails closed in the learner's browser instead of executing. "It is the one input to the build that nothing in the repo verifies" also overstates: the repo does hold a hash pin for a Pyodide artifact (`PYODIDE_CDN_SRI`, sha384, in `web/src/lib/pyodide-runtime.ts`), and that file records this exact supply-chain analysis as a deliberate decision. What survives is narrower than the title: the pyodide-core TARBALL from GitHub — `pyodide.asm.wasm`, `python_stdlib.zip`, `pyodide.asm.js`, and `pyodide-lock.json` itself — is the unverified root of trust, and the floating `jupyter-server>=2.14` / `build>=1.2` pins are real.

**Impact.** The wasm runtime, the stdlib, and every wheel the in-browser lab loads are accepted on TLS alone; a single bad fetch that lands in `.cache/` is then reused by every subsequent build on that runner or Amplify app, because the cache key is the version string. This is the artifact that executes in every learner's browser, and it is the one input to the build that nothing in the repo verifies. Nothing is known to be compromised — this is a missing control, not an incident.

**Evidence.** `web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh:80-83` (curl of the core tarball, no `--checksum`/`sha256sum`), `:102-103` (`curl -fsSL --retry 3 "${cdn}/${whl}" -o "$dest/$whl"` then `test -s`), `:75` (`local tarball=".cache/pyodide-core-${version}.tar.bz2"`), `amplify.yml:27` (`- jupyterlite-build/.cache/**/*`), `web/jupyterlite-build/requirements.txt:3-4`.

**Verification — reproduces** (partly true, low, ran locally). REPRODUCED the core defect. Extracted the function verbatim and ran it against a hand-made poisoned cache entry: `sed -n '73,92p' web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh > fn.sh`; built a fake `pyodide-core-0.29.0.tar.bz2` whose `pyodide/pyodide.js` contains `globalThis.__pwned = 1`; then `bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source ./fn.sh; fetch_pyodide_core 0.29.0 ./dest'`. Output: "using cached .cache/pyodide-core-0.29.0.tar.bz2", and the attacker pyodide.js + a 15-byte "pyodide.asm.wasm" were staged into dest with no hash check. The `-s` test plus a successful `tar -xjf` is the entire acceptance criterion, and the CI assertions downstream (package.json version match, `ls micropip-*.whl`) are all trivially satisfiable by a crafted tarball; the WASM_COMPRESSION_CEILING guard only checks size. `grep -n "curl\|wget\|pip install\|sha256\|shasum\|--require-hashes\|checksum" web/jupyterlite-build/build.sh` returns exactly lines 30, 31, 80, 102 — two unpinned pip installs and the two unverified curls, and no checksum logic at all. requirements.txt is as quoted (jupyterlite-core==0.7.6, jupyterlite-pyodide-kernel==0.7.0 pinned; jupyter-server>=2.14, build>=1.2 floating; no hashes, no --require-hashes).

Nothing is currently compromised, and the fix is cheap: `shasum -a 256 web/jupyterlite-build/.cache/pyodide-core-0.29.0.tar.bz2` vs `curl -fsSL https://github.com/pyodide/pyodide/releases/download/0.29.0/pyodide-core-0.29.0.tar.bz2 | shasum -a 256` both give fe85edd0d5c9828598da14c98d2f79cea45aac5a9e6448ca65dcc2d58d4ed033 — the release bytes are stable, so a one-line expected-sha256 constant beside PYODIDE_VERSION would close the whole tarball exposure. Likewise the staged wheels already match the lock (shasum of micropip-0.11.0 = d98e61…, numpy-2.2.5 = 2ca46b…, identical to pyodide-lock.json), so build-time wheel verification is a `python -c` away — it would only move a failure the browser already catches earlier into the build.

Severity low, as the finder judged: it is a missing control on a build input, not an incident; the wheel path already has runtime integrity; and the one genuinely unverified artifact (core tarball: wasm, python_stdlib.zip, pyodide.js, the lock itself) comes from GitHub release assets over TLS with a stable pinned version.
